Brain health & nerve function
Antioxidant

Energy production
Acetyl L-carnitine is the acetylated form of the amino acid L-carnitine and occurs naturally in the body where it is synthesised in the brain, liver and kidneys.
The major difference between acetyl L-carnitine and carnitine is that acetyl L-carnitine is more easily absorbed from the gut, and more readily crosses the blood-brain barrier.
The richest sources of carnitine are meat, poultry, fish and dairy products, while grains, vegetables and fruits contain relatively small amounts placing vegetarians at risk of primary deficiency.
The L-isomer of carnitine is the biologically active form, whereas the D-isomer may compete with L-carnitine for absorption and transport.
Carnitine acts as an antioxidant in the cell membrane and protects tissues from oxidative damage.
Fat metabolism & energy production
Acetyl L-carnitine supports energy production and fat metabolism. It facilitates the uptake of acetyl CoA into the mitochondria during fatty acid oxidation, which allows the body to turn fat into energy. It also assists the transport of fat across the cell membranes in muscle tissue for use as an energy source.
Acetyl L-carnitine is most concentrated in tissues that use fatty acids as their primary fuel, such as skeletal and cardiac (heart) muscle. In this regard, L-carnitine plays an important role in energy production by conjugating fatty acids for transport into the mitochondria for beta oxidation.
Cognitive function
Acetyl L-carnitine supports cognitive function and brain function.
Acetyl L-carnitine can traverse the blood-brain barrier and modulate phospholipid metabolism, synaptic morphology and transmission, enhancing the synthesis and release of neurotrophic factors, neurohormones and multiple neurotransmitters which helps support cognitive function. Improvement in cognitive function may be connected to processes influenced by the brain’s energy production1.
Acetyl L-carnitine serves as a precursor to acetyl coenzyme A and contributes acetyl groups to acetylcholine. Acetyl L-carnitine also seems to promote acetylcholine release and increases choline acetyltransferase activity.
Acetyl L-carnitine may have neuroplasticity effects in some regions of the brain. It can increase levels of brain-derived neurotrophic factor and the release of glutamate, an excitatory neurotransmitter that plays an important role in learning and memory.
In an open-label, randomised study, 30 individuals with fatigue were given 2g/day of acetyl L-carnitine for 24 weeks. Significant improvements in mental fatigue and attention concentration were seen in the acetyl L-carnitine group. Two weeks after discontinuing treatment 52% of individuals experienced worsening of fatigue2.
Muscle health & post-exercise recovery
Acetyl L-Carnitine supports muscle performance and aids post exercise recovery. Due to its role as a transporter of long-chain fatty acids across the mitochondrial membrane for beta-oxidation,
L-carnitine supports endurance exercise, which requires the use of long-chain fatty acids as an energy substrate. L-carnitine can enhance exercise performance by increasing fatty acid oxidation in skeletal muscle, thereby reducing muscle glycogen usage and increasing overall exercise capacity.
Multiple studies have examined the favourable effects of L-carnitine on reducing exercise-induced hypoxia, subsequent muscle damage and delayed-onset muscle soreness (DOMS)3.
A single-blind study in 6 untrained subjects found that 3g/day of L-carnitine significantly reduced pain, tenderness and CK release
after 20-minute eccentric effort compared to placebo. This effect was attributed to the vasodilatory properties of L-carnitine that improves energetic metabolism of hypoxic/damaged muscles4.
Both chronic and acute supplementation with L-carnitine, with or without protein during training, have been reported to enhance exercise capacity and endurance at a dose of 1-2g/day5.
Sperm health
Acetyl L-Carnitine supports sperm health by improving sperm motility and reducing the levels of reactive oxygen species (ROS) in seminal fluid and improving semen quality6.
L-carnitine is highly concentrated in the epididymis and sperm where it plays a role in promoting sperm motility, maturation and fertilisation. Due to its antioxidant activity, it helps protect sperm against oxidative damage, reduces apoptosis in spermatogenic cells and inhibits sperm aggregation. L-carnitine is used by spermatozoa for mitochondrial beta-oxidation of fatty acids for use as an energy source.
A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial involving 89 males with low sperm quality found that 2g of L-carnitine daily significantly improved sperm concentration and motility over the course of 2 months7.

Activated B Complex contains therapeutic doses of all B vitamins. It contains:
Riboflavin-5-phosphate, the active form of vitamin B2.
Pyridoxal 5-phosphate (PLP), the active form of vitamin B6 (PLP is the most common form of B6 found in human tissue).
Methylfolate, the active form of folic acid.
Methylcobalamin (mecobalamin), the metabolically-active coenzyme form of vitamin B12.
As B vitamins are water soluble, regular daily intake is required to support general health. B vitamins work synergistically in the body and are, therefore, best taken together.
Vitamins B2 and B3 support liver detoxification and are involved in antioxidant enzyme systems that help maintain tissue antioxidant defences. Vitamin B2, as a cofactor of glutathione reductase, helps recycle the important antioxidant glutathione.
Folate and B12 are important for cell growth and replication.
Activated B Complex helps prevent dietary B viatmin deficiencies.
Activated B Complex is suitable for preconception, pregnancy and breastfeeding to help meet the increased nutritional requirements. It provides 400 micrograms of methylfolate, also known as
5-methyltetrahydrofolate (5-MTHF), to support healthy foetal development.
Energy
B vitamins support energy production and help relieve fatigue. They are required for the metabolism of dietary carbohydrates, proteins and fats and the production of energy in every cell.
Vitamin B1 is an essential coenzyme in the production of energy and is stored in muscles, where it plays a central role in energy production.
Vitamin B2 is an essential part of the coenzymes flavin mononucleotide (FMD) and flavin-adenosine dinucleotide (FAD) that play central roles in cellular respiration and the production of ATP in the mitochondria.
Vitamin B3 is a component of the reduced and oxidised forms of the coenzyme nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NADH2 and NAD,
respectively), both of which are involved in energy metabolism.
Vitamin B5, as CoA, transfers fatty acids into the mitochondria for energy production.
Vitamin B12 is involved in the synthesis of the citric acid cycle intermediate, succinyl-CoA, necessary for energy production.
B vitamins support healthy exercise capacity. Athletes and people who engage in vigorous exercise have an increased requirement for B vitamins.
Nervous system
B vitamins support healthy nervous system function. They are required for the synthesis of neurotransmitters such as acetylcholine, norepinephrine, dopamine, GABA and serotonin and help maintain healthy mood.
B vitamins support the stress response. Deficiencies have been linked to mild anxiety and mood changes. Requirements for
B vitamins increase during times of physical and mental stress.
Vitamin B1 is located in the nerve cell membrane and is important for the transmission of nerve impulses. It plays a role in the metabolism of several neurotransmitters, including acetylcholine, GABA and serotonin.
Vitamin B5 is known as the “anti-stress vitamin” as it supports adrenal function and is involved the production of adrenal hormones. It is also necessary for the production of acetylcholine.
Vitamin B6 is important for the synthesis of lipids that form the myelin sheath surrounding nerves and is required for the formation of several neurotransmitters including serotonin, dopamine, GABA and norepinephrine. Pyridoxine is a cofactor in the conversion of tryptophan to serotonin and deficiency is associated with mood alterations.
Vitamin B12 and methylfolate are essential for healthy brain and memory function. Supplementation with 400 micrograms of folate has been positively associated with improved results in the Word List Memory Test and Constructional Recall Test scores1. Low B12 status is associated with more rapid cognitive decline in older adults2.

subsections.heading: DRUG INTERACTIONS
subsections.text:
Caution with cholestyramine and colestipol (hypolipidaemic agents)
- may decrease the absorption of vitamin B3 and folate. Separate dose by at least 4-6 hours.
Caution with phenobarbital and phenytoin (anticonvulsants) - high doses of vitamin B6 or folate can decrease their efficacy. Monitor.
Caution with L-Dopa - vitamin B6 increases the peripheral metabolism of levodopa and may lower levodopa levels for CNS penetration, resulting in reduced levodopa effects. The effect of pyridoxine is prevented by administration of a dopa-decarboxylase inhibitor (e.g. benserazide, carbidopa) with levodopa, as is common clinical practice.
Caution with antiepileptic and anticonvulsant medications – folic acid may reduce serum levels of these medications. Patients should take folate only under the supervision of a health professional.
Caution with methotrexate (folic acid antagonist) - co-administrate with folate may reduce the effects. Patients should take folate only under the supervision of a health professional.
Caution with tetracycline hydrochloride (antibiotic) - B vitamins may reduce drug bioavailability. Separate dose by at least 2 hours.
Several medications may deplete folate status, including trimethoprim (antibiotic), pyrimethamine (antimalarial), triamterene (blood pressure), sulfasalazine (for ulcerative colitis) and oral contraceptives.
Several medications can decrease the absorption of vitamin B12 or increase the risk of deficiency, such as acid-suppressing medications (proton-pump inhibitors e.g. omeprazole and
histamine2 (h2)-receptor antagonists), metformin (hypoglycaemic), oral contraceptives, neomycin (antibiotic) and colchicine (anti-gout).

subsections.heading: CAUTIONS
subsections.text:
B vitamins are stimulatory in nature. To avoid any sleep interferance, avoid taking before bed.
Taking at night may result in more vivid dreams (vitamin B6).

subsections.heading: SIDE EFFECTS
subsections.text:
Supplemental B vitamins may cause nausea or mild gastrointestinal upset if taken on an empty stomach. Best taken with food to reduce risk.
Riboflavin can impart a bright yellow colour to urine.

subsections.heading: TECHNICAL INFORMATION
subsections.text:
Vitamin B12 (cobalamin) is a water-soluble vitamin that is essential for DNA synthesis, cell reproduction, carbohydrate metabolism, immune health, nervous system health and cardiovascular health.
Activated B12 Spray contains methylcobalamin (mecobalamin), the metabolically-active coenzyme form of vitamin B12 that is ready for use in the body. Commonly used cyanocobalamin is a form of vitamin B12 that does not occur naturally in foods and needs to be converted to methylcobalamin for use in the body. Methylcobalamin differs from cyanocobalamin in that the non-toxic cyanide molecule is replaced by a methyl group.
Vitamin B12 is mostly obtained from animal protein in the diet, with high levels found in organ meats, sardines, oysters, egg yolk, fish, beef, cheese and milk.
Activated B12 Spray supports energy production in the body. Vitamin B12 is involved in the synthesis of the citric acid cycle intermediate, succinyl-CoA, necessary for energy production.
Activated B12 Spray provides high-strength vitamin B12 in each spray, which can be easily administered under the tongue as an alternative to oral and sublingual tablets to help prevent a vitamin B12 deficiency. Activated B12 Spray has a natural mixed berry flavour and is naturally sweetened with Stevia for compliance.
Nervous system & brain health
Vitamin B12 is essential for nervous system health and an adequate intake is essential for normal neurological function. It is essential for the synthesis of myelin, the protective sheath surrounding many nerves. Additionally, B12 is involved in the synthesis of neurotransmitters and, in conjunction with folate, is involved in S-adenosylmethionine (SAMe) production, which is involved in healthy mood.
Vitamin B12 supports brain health and healthy cognition. The European Food Safety Authority concluded that there is a cause-and-effect relationship between the dietary intake of vitamin
B12 and contribution to normal neurological and psychological functions1. Low B12 status is associated with more rapid cognitive decline in older adults2.
Methylcobalamin appears to have better uptake by neurons than cyanocobalamin and may, therefore, be a better option to support nervous system health. Studies show that methylcobalamin
can improve nerve conduction and promote nerve and axonal regeneration, has neuro-protective properties and can protect against glutamate-induced neurotoxicity3.
Cardiovascular system & blood health
Activated B12 Spray helps maintain blood health and a healthy cardiovascular system.
Vitamin B12 is necessary for red blood cell production and for the synthesis of haemoglobin, which carries oxygen in red blood cells throughout the body.
Vitamin B12, together with folate and vitamin B6, helps maintain healthy homocysteine levels in the body by facilitating the conversion of homocysteine to methionine. High homocysteine levels are associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes.
A double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomised, cross over study in 55 healthy vegetarians investigated the impact of 500 micrograms of vitamin B12 on cardiovascular function. Of the 55 subjects, 35 (70%) had suboptimal serum B12 levels.
Supplementation with 500 micrograms of vitamin B12 daily significantly increased serum vitamin B12 (p<0.0001) and lowered plasma homocysteine (p<0.05). Supplementation also improved brachial flow mediated dilation (FMD) (p<0.0001)4.
B12 absorption
Activated B12 Spray delivers vitamin B12 sublingually, where it can be absorbed directly into sublingual capillaries, bypassing the digestive tract.

subsections.heading: TECHNICAL INFORMATION
subsections.text:
Healthy foetal development
Supports healthy cell growth & replication
Supports brain health & memory function
Beneficial for individuals with MTHFR polymorphisms
Supports cardiovascular health & homocysteine metabolism
Folate is the generic term for a large family of chemically similar compounds known as vitamin B9. Folic acid is a synthetic form of folate used to fortify foods and in supplements.
Methylfolate is the active form of folate. After ingestion, both dietary folate and synthetic folic acid need to undergo a complex conversion via a multistep pathway in the liver to their active form. Folic acid itself has no biological functions unless it is reduced to dihydrofolate and tetrahydrofolate. Folate from animal sources is present in a ‘free form’ and is readily absorbed, but folate in plants exists in conjugated forms which require deconjugation by zinc-dependent enzymes in the gut prior to absorption.
Methylfolate is the active form of folate in the body and accounts for approximately 98% of folates in human plasma. Supplemental
methylfolate is directly available and does not need to be metabolised.
Activated Folate 500 helps prevent dietary folate deficiency. Studies comparing methylfolate and folic acid supplementation have found the two compounds to be comparable in physiological activity, bioavailability and absorption at equimolar doses1. However, there is some evidence that methylfolate may be more effective than folic acid in improve folate status. A double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled study investigated the effect of supplementing with folic acid and methylfolate and measured the resulting increase on red blood cell folate concentration, an indicator of folate status. The increase in red blood cell folate was significantly higher in the group receiving methylfolate than the group receiving the same dose of folic acid (p=0.001)2.
Quatrefolic®
Activated Folate 500 contains methylfolate as Quatrefolic®, the glucosamine salt of (6S)-5-methyltetrahydrofolate. Quatrefolic® is an active form of folate, immediately available for its biological action without being metabolised in the body.
Quatrefolic® has higher bioavailability than folic acid and is more bioavailable than other forms of methylfolate, including the calcium salt. Rat studies show that the glucosamine salt is 12% better absorbed than the calcium salt3. A crossover study comparing the bioavailability of a single oral dose of 400mcg of folate as glucosamine salt (Quatrefolic®) to the calcium salt in healthy adults found that Quatrefolic® had 10% higher bioavailability4.
Functions of folate
Folate is essential for cell growth and replication. Without folate, living cells cannot divide. Folate-containing coenzymes are essential to the
production of DNA and RNA in growing and dividing cells. Rapidly dividing cells, such as blood cells and cells lining the digestive tract, are particularly dependent on folate. Folate helps maintain red blood cell health.
Folate helps the body metabolise proteins.
Activated Folate 500 supports brain health, cognitive function and memory. In a study of 100 adults with mild cognitive impairment and 121 normal adults, folate intake was positively associated with the Word List Memory Test and Constructional Recall Test scores5.
Activated Folate 500 helps support emotional wellbeing. Quatrefolic® crosses the blood-brain barrier and enters the central nervous system where it sustains the release of neurotransmitters including serotonin, norepinephrine and dopamine.
Cardiovascular health & homocysteine
Methylfolate is well studied for its ability to lower levels of homocysteine, a strong predictor of cardiovascular risk, and therefore contribute to cardiovascular health. Increased homocysteine is a risk factor for adverse cardiovascular events and adverse pregnancy outcomes.
Methionine, an amino acid from dietary protein, is converted to homocysteine in the body. As homocysteine is a toxic metabolite, the body remethylates homocysteine back to methionine via an enzyme methionine synthase, which requires methylfolate as the methyl donor and vitamin B12 as a cofactor6.
A double-blind, randomised, controlled intervention trial in 144 females compared 2 doses of methylfolate (208 micrograms or 406 micrograms) with 400 micrograms of folic acid for their ability to lower homocysteine levels during 24 weeks of supplementation. Homocysteine levels decreased in a similar amount in all three supplemental groups (p<0.001) and the authors concluded that methylfolate is an adequate alternative to folic acid in reducing homocysteine concentrations7.
Pregnancy & neural tube defects (NTD)
Activated Folate 500 helps support healthy foetal development.
Current recommendations state that women of childbearing age should ensure a daily intake of at least 400 micrograms of folate for at least four weeks before conception and during pregnancy to reduce the risk of having a child with a neural tube defects (NTD), including spina bifida and anencephaly.

An intervention study compared the efficacy of sublingual and oral administration of 500 micrograms of vitamin B12 in 30 subjects with B12 deficiency. After 4 weeks, B12 increased in both the sublingual and oral supplementation groups (p=0.0001), with no significant difference between the group5.

subsections.heading: TECHNICAL INFORMATION
subsections.text:
R,S-alpha Lipoic acid
Supports energy production
Maintains blood vessel health
Supports nervous system health
Alpha Lipoic acid is a powerful antioxidant that regenerates other antioxidants, including vitamin E, vitamin C and reduced glutathione, and has metal-chelating activity. Both fat and water soluble, it is readily absorbed from the gut and crosses cellular and blood-brain membrane barriers.
Antioxidants are molecules that inhibit oxidation of other molecules. Oxidation is a chemical reaction that can produce free radicals in the body. These free radicals can start a chain reaction that potentially leads to damage within DNA, proteins and lipids in cell membranes.
Direct antioxidants bind directly to a free radical, whereas indirect antioxidants recycle direct antioxidants and help cells produce antioxidant enzymes. Alpha Lipoic acid can directly and indirectly scavenge free radicals in the body.
Alpha Lipoic acid contains an asymmetric carbon molecule, meaning it can exist as one of two possible optical isomers, also called enantiomers. These enantiomers are mirror images of each other and exist as R-Lipoic acid and S-Lipoic acid. Alpha Lipoic 300 contains a mixture of 50% R and 50% S-Lipoic acid (R,S-alpha Lipoic acid). Almost twice as much R-alpha-Lipoic acid is absorbed as the S-alpha-Lipoic acid with oral supplementation. Combining S-Lipoic acid with R-Lipoic acid helps with the absorption.
Energy production
Alpha Lipoic 300 supports energy production. It is an essential cofactor for coenzyme complexes involved in energy production, playing a role in carbohydrate metabolism in the mitochondrial citric acid cycle to produce adenosine triphosphate (ATP).
Glucose uptake
Alpha Lipoic 300 helps support the cellular uptake of glucose. Alpha Lipoic acid plays a key role in the citric acid cycle, acting as a coenzyme for pyruvate and a-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase to regulate glucose metabolism and regulates insulin sensitivity.
Nerve health
Alpha Lipoic 300 supports nervous system function and nerve health. Due to the potent antioxidant effect of alpha Lipoic acid, it can reduce free radical damage to the peripheral nerves.
A double-blind, randomised trial compared the effects of alpha Lipoic acid (ALA) to acetyl L-carnitine (ALC) on 64 individuals with sciatic nerve pain associated with a herniated disc. Participants in group 1 (n=33) received ALC 1180mg/day; participants in group 2 (n=31) received ALA 600mg/day for 60 days. Both groups experienced significant improvements in neuropathic symptoms, however, ALA was statistically superior to ALC1.
A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial examined the effect of 600mg, 1200mg and 1800mg/day of ALA in 181 patients with polyneuropathy. Significant improvements in stabbing and burning pain were noted in all ALA groups after 5 weeks of administration. The
mechanisms of the rapid improvement may be related to improved nerve flow mediated by the antioxidant action of ALA2.
Blood vessel health
Alpha Lipoic 300 maintains blood vessel health.
Blood vessels are lined with vascular endothelial cells which form the physical barrier between blood and the vessel wall and play a role in vasodilation and constriction.
The elasticity of the vessel wall is regulated by nitric oxide (NO) which is produced by endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS). Loss of eNOS activity causes endothelial dysfunction leading to decreased vasodilation and vascular inflammation.
Alpha Lipoic acid can significantly improve endothelial function, increase NO synthesis and prevents loss of eNOS phosphorylation to support healthy vasodilation3.
Mild migraines
In a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 54 migraine patients with and without aura were given 600mg/day of ALA for 3 months. The group receiving ALA reported a reduction in migraine attack frequency, headache days and headache severity compared to placebo4.
In an open-label cohort study, 32 people suffering from migraines received 400mg of ALA twice daily for 6 months, in addition to on-going treatment. A significant reduction was seen in the number of attacks. One potential mechanism by which ALA may reduce
migraine attacks is via its potent antioxidant effect, as migraines have been linked to oxidative stress5.

subsections.text:
Assists with recovery from illness
Supports energy levels
Relieves fatigue and general debility
Supports mental focus, clarity and cognitive function
Healthy immune system function
With clinically studied Holixer™
Relieves symptoms of stress
Improves sleep quality
Astra Recharge is a combination of herbs, including high-strength Astragalus and the mushroom Reishi. This unique formula supports recovery from illness, targeting the multi-faceted symptom picture of debility, low energy, poor immune health and brain fog as well as increased stress and poor sleep.
Astra Recharge is suitable to be used either during the winter months following illness, or at any time during the year to support recovery from general debility and fatigue and in times of high stress.
Astra Recharge contains Holixer™, a clinically studied extract of Ocimum tenuiflorum (Holy basil), to relieve the symptoms of stress, promote body adaptation to stress and improve sleep quality.
Astra Recharge also contains the mushroom Reishi. Reishi is listed among the superior tonics in the oldest surviving Chinese materia medica and has been considered “the mushroom of immortality” in China, Japan, Korea and other Asian countries for more than 4000 years.
Immune health
Astra Recharge contains Astragalus, Siberian ginseng and Reishi, supporting immune system health and healthy immune system function.
Astragalus and its saponins have immune-modulating activity by stimulating macrophage activity and enhancing B- and T-cell activity1.
Siberian ginseng is a medicinal plant originating from Russia, northern areas of Korea, Japan and China, and grows naturally in the wild in the cold to moderate climates of East Asia. Typically, the root of the plant is used, containing the active constituents eleutherosides A-M, which are chemically distinct glycosides. Siberian ginseng supports immune health by increasing T-helper cells and natural killer (NK) cell activity2.
Siberian ginseng supports recovery from illness. It is used as a tonic to either prevent the body from becoming run-down, or to restore it to a better state of wellbeing following a period of illness.
Reishi contains both polysaccharides and β-glucans, known to have strong immunomodulating action, including the activation of immune effector cells such as T cells, macrophages and NK cells3.
Reishi also has a long history of use in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) to reduce excess mucus, loosen chest phlegm and relieve cough.
Schisandra is considered one of the 50 fundamental herbs of TCM, used traditionally to reduce and relieve cough.
General debility and mental clarity
General debility is a state of general weakness or fragility that may be a result of either illness, stress or poor sleep. General debility is often accompanied by a melting pot of symptoms including low energy levels, weariness or fatigue, poor concentration, focus and mental clarity and poor immune health.
Astra Recharge supports mental concentration, focus and clarity, which can be beneficial for individuals experiencing brain fog, either because of recent infection or from general debility.
Siberian ginseng has been approved by the Commission E for use in times of fatigue and debility, declining capacity for work or
concentration, and during convalescence4. Similarly, the World Health Organisation (WHO) recommend Siberian ginseng as a restorative tonic for enhancement of mental and physical capacities in cases of weakness, exhaustion and tiredness and during convalescence5.
A randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind, crossover study found that 625mg of Siberian ginseng twice daily significantly improved selective memory, cognitive function and wellbeing over 3 months compared to placebo (p<0.02). Individuals taking Siberian ginseng also noted improvements in wellbeing and levels of physical activity6.
Stress
Astra Recharge contains selected herbs, including Astragalus and Siberian ginseng, to support a healthy stress response in the body.

Convenient one-a-day tablet
Synergistic formula
B Sustained Release contains therapeutic doses of all 8 B vitamins including B1, B2, B3, B5, B6, B12, biotin (B7) and folic acid (B9), as well as choline, inositol and vitamin C.
B Sustained Release is specifically formulated to slowly release nutrients into the digestive tract in a continuous manner over an extended period of time, rather than all at once.
B vitamins perform essential, inter-related roles in the body to enable cellular functioning, as well as acting as co-enzymes in a vast array of catabolic and anabolic enzymatic reactions. Their most important role is to convert carbohydrates, protein and fat into energy.
Choline and inositol are both members of the B vitamin family. Choline is necessary for the structure and function of cells and inositol is involved in the transport and metabolism of fats.
B vitamins are not synthesised by the body and therefore must be taken through the diet.
Typically, B vitamins are synthesised by plants, however, humans obtain most of their B vitamins from higher up the food chain in foods of animal origin, such as meat, dairy and eggs.
B vitamins are water soluble, meaning the body is unable to store them in large amounts. As such, regular daily intake is required to support general health.
B vitamins work synergistically in the body, so are best taken together.
Several factors increase the requirements for B vitamins, including dietary choices, pregnancy, certain medications and alcohol use.
Energy production
B Sustained Release supports energy production. The B vitamins collectively function as coenzymes involved in mitochondrial energy production, supporting normal digestion and the conversion of food into energy.
B vitamins are essential for the proper functioning of the Krebs cycle in the mitochondria. The Krebs cycle is responsible for producing adenosine triphosphate (ATP), the primary energy carrier in all cells.
Nervous system health
B Sustained Release supports healthy nervous system function.
Vitamins B1, B5, B6, B12 and folic acid play an important role in the synthesis of neurotransmitters to support the function and health of the nervous system.
Vitamin B1 is essential for the metabolism of acetylcholine, gamma aminobutyric acid (GABA) and serotonin.
Vitamin B5, commonly called the anti-stress vitamin, is involved in the synthesis of the neurotransmitter acetylcholine. Acetylcholine plays an important role in adrenal function and is required for the proper functioning of the adrenal cortex and the synthesis of steroid hormones, namely cortisone.
Vitamin B6 is involved in the conversion of tryptophan to niacin, the synthesis of GABA in the central nervous system as well as the metabolism of serotonin, norepinephrine and dopamine.
Folic acid and vitamin B12 play an important role in the development, differentiation and functioning of the CNS through methionine-homocysteine metabolism. Methionine is activated to S-adenosylmethionine (SAMe), which is indispensable for the
synthesis of nucleic acids (DNA and RNA), proteins, neurotransmitters and hormones.
Serotonin and dopamine are neurotransmitters that play a role in an individual’s mood and well-being. Dopamine plays a role in emotional responses, while serotonin contributes to feelings of wellbeing and happiness.
Specifically, vitamin B12 is essential for the proper functioning and development of the brain and nerve cells. It is required for the myelin sheath that covers and protects the nerves of the central and the peripheral nervous system, ensuring fast and effective nerve-impulse transmission.
Vitamin C supports a healthy stress response in the body and plays a crucial role in adrenal function. The adrenal glands contain the highest concentration of vitamin C in the body.
Cardiovascular health
B Sustained Release maintains cardiovascular system health and blood health.
Vitamins B6, B12 and folic acid are required for homocysteine metabolism and assist the conversion of homocysteine to methionine. High homocysteine levels are associated with a higher risk of adverse cardiovascular outcomes.
Vitamins B6, B12 and folic acid are important for the production of red blood cells, cell growth and cell reproduction. Vitamins B6 and B12 are also required for the synthesis of haemoglobin, the oxygen-carrying pigment in red blood cells.

Vitamin C supports a healthy stress response in the body and plays a crucial role in adrenal function. The adrenal glands contain the highest concentration of vitamin C in the body.
Cardiovascular health
B Sustained Release maintains cardiovascular system health and blood health.
Vitamins B6, B12 and folic acid are required for homocysteine metabolism and assist the conversion of homocysteine to methionine. High homocysteine levels are associated with a higher risk of adverse cardiovascular outcomes.
Vitamins B6, B12 and folic acid are important for the production of red blood cells, cell growth and cell reproduction. Vitamins B6 and B12 are also required for the synthesis of haemoglobin, the oxygen-carrying pigment in red blood cells.

Berberine ImmunoPlex provides a blend of herbs standardised to contain 109.26mg berberine per tablet from Phellodendron and Barberry.
Berberine is an isoquinoline plant alkaloid that belongs to the structural class of protoberberines. Protoberberine alkaloids include berberine (the major alkaloid), jatrorrhizine, palmatine,
columbamine. Berberine represents one of the most studied among the naturally occurring protoberberine alkaloids1.
Berberine has a distinctive yellow colour and bitter flavour and is naturally found in the bark, roots and rhizomes of various medicinal plants including Phellodendron, Barberry, Indian barberry, Golden seal and Chinese goldthread.
Antimicrobial
The stem bark of Phellodendron and Barberry contain isoquinoline alkaloids, including berberine, the primary active constituent responsible their pharmacological activity.
Phellodendron is traditionally used in Chinese medicine to ‘dispel and remove heat toxins’ and ‘detoxify and disinfect’. It is traditionally used for infections due to the presence of berberine.
In vitro research shows that berberine has antimicrobial effects including antibacterial and antifungal activity2,3. It has shown in vitro antibacterial activity against a wide variety of microorganisms including Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, fungi and protozoa4.
Preliminary research suggests berberine might inhibit bacterial sortase, a protein responsible for anchoring Gram-positive bacteria to cell membranes5.
In vitro studies have shown berberine has antifungal activity against Candida spp. and Cryptococcus neoformans strains, possibly by altering mitochondrial membranes and reducing biofilm formation6.
Berberine extracts have demonstrated in vitro growth inhibition of Giardia lamblia, Trichomonas vaginalis and Leishmania donovani7, 8.
A recent 2020 systematic review and meta analyses of 13 clinical trials showed that the addition of berberine to standard triple therapy improved the eradication rate of Helicobacter pylori, with improved symptom remission rate, accelerated ulcer healing and reduced adverse events in groups using berberine at doses ranging between 120-500mg9.
Berberine ImmunoPlex also contains Pau d’arco, a well-known antifungal herb. Pau d’arco and its constituents lapachol and
β-lapachone have demonstrated in vitro activity against various Candida species including Candida albicans and Candida tropicalis10. Bark extracts of Pau d’arco have also shown broad-spectrum activity in vitro, specifically active against most fungal strains11.
The mechanism of action may involve interference with the fungal cell membrane12. Napthoquinones, active components in Pau d’arco, are inhibitors of the electron chain transport and acts by uncoupling
oxidative phosphorylation, thus inhibiting ATP synthesis in the fungal cell.
Several constituents found in Pau d’arco have also demonstrated antibacterial activity in vitro, including lapachol, β-lapachone and anthraquinone-2-carboxylic acid. These isolated compounds have shown activity against Helicobacter pylori, Clostridium perfringens, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Streptococcus faecalis, Enterococcus and Bacillus species, and various strains of Staphylococcus aureus13,14.

subsections.heading: TECHNICAL INFORMATION
subsections.text:
Helps support healthy cholesterol
Cardiovascular health
Antioxidant
Equivalent to 132.5mg flavonoids
Cholesterol is a fat-like substance that is naturally produced by the body and found in the diet in eggs and animal products that are rich in fat, such as meats and full-fat dairy foods.
Cholesterol is essential for many of the body’s metabolic processes, including the production of hormones (oestrogen, testosterone and adrenal hormones) and vitamin D and is necessary for the structure of cell membranes and to produce bile acid, to digest fat. It is not necessary to consume cholesterol in the diet as the body can produce sufficient cholesterol to meet its needs.
Cholesterol is transported around the body in the blood attached to lipoproteins. There are two main types of lipoproteins: low-density lipoprotein (LDL) and high-density lipoprotein (HDL). LDL (considered ‘bad’ cholesterol) carries most of the cholesterol that is delivered to cells, while HDL (‘good’ cholesterol) helps remove excess cholesterol out of the cells, including cells in the arteries. Too much LDL in the bloodstream can lead to the development of fatty deposits in the arteries, causing narrowing of the blood vessels.
Bergamot Cholesterol Care helps maintain healthy cholesterol and supports cardiovascular system health.
Bergamot
Citrus aurantium (Bergamot) is a natural hybrid fruit derived from bitter orange and lemon, indigenous to Calabria, Italy. Essential oil obtained from the peel is used for its fragrant properties and
provides the classic bergamot aroma associated with Earl Grey tea.
Bergamot has a unique composition of flavonoids, including neoeriocitrin, neohesperidin, naringin, melitidin and brutieridin, that are potent antioxidants and believed to be responsible for the fruit’s pharmacological effects. Citrus aurantium has the highest concentration of flavonoids compared to other citrus fruits1.
Bergamot Cholesterol Care contains 500mg of Citrus aurantium extract, equivalent to 75g fresh fruit juice, with 132.5mg of flavonoids per tablet.
Bergamot helps maintain healthy cholesterol. The exact mechanism of action is not clear, however, it is likely due to multiple mechanisms. Several flavonoids in Bergamot, including naringin, can activate AMPK, the central regulator of lipid and glucose metabolism. AMPK facilitates glucose uptake and prevents the accumulation of fat by modulating downstream-signalling components, such as acetyl-CoA carboxylase (ACC) and HMG-CoA reductase2.
Polyphenols in Bergamot, including naringin, melitidin and brutieridin, also act as HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors, mimicking the action of statins and blocking the rate-limiting step in cholesterol synthesis.
Animal and human studies provide evidence of bergamot’s cholesterol-lowering effect. In one study, rats fed a typical Western diet high in fat and sugar for 6 months showed a 5-fold increase in fasting plasma triglyceride and an 8-fold increase in cholesterol levels compared with chow-fed rats. The addition of naringenin
(naringin aglycon) to the diet significantly decreased total cholesterol and triglycerides by 50% and reduced atherosclerotic lesions by more than 70%3.
A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled study in 237 patients with hyperlipemia found that 500mg or 1000mg of Bergamot extract daily for 30 days inhibited HMG-CoA reductase activity, significantly reduced total cholesterol, LDL and triglycerides and moderately increased HDL4.
Bergamot has also been found to enhance the effects of statins. One study found that the addition of Bergamot to rosuvastatin significantly enhanced the rosuvastatin-induced effect on serum lipemic profile compared to rosuvastatin alone5.
Globe artichoke
Globe artichoke has a long history of use, dating back to ancient Greece and Rome. Traditionally, it is used in Western herbal medicine as a liver tonic, choleretic and cholagogue to increase bile flow.
The leaf contains phenolic acids, mainly caffeic acid derivatives (e.g. chlorogenic acid, cynarin), sesquiterpenes, lactones and flavonoids, phytosterols, inulin and free luteolin.
Animal studies have found that artichoke leaf extract can lower cholesterol, possibly by indirect modulation of HMA-CoA reductase activity.
A study in hamsters found that artichoke leaf extract significantly lowered total cholesterol by 15%, non-HDL cholesterol by 30% and triglycerides by 25% compared to controls6.

Turmeric/curcumin
Curcumin is the main active component found in Turmeric, present in concentrations between 3-5% and gives Turmeric its distinctive yellow colour.
Turmeric has a long history of use in Ayurvedic medicine as an anti-inflammatory and anti-arthritic. Its traditional use has been
supported by scientific studies, showing curcumin to be responsible for the anti-inflammatory and anti-arthritic activity of Turmeric.
Curcuminoids are the active phenolic compounds in Turmeric. A mixture of three curcuminoids exist in Turmeric: monomolecular curcumin, demethoxycurcumin and bisdemethoxycurcumin, although these are collectively referred to as curcumin.
Meriva® curcumin is a clinically trialled curcumin formulation with improved bioavailability for enhanced absorption. Meriva® is comprised of these three curcuminoids to reflect the most typical ratio found in nature.
Curcumin has been widely studied with over 4000 pre-clinical investigations performed for a variety of therapeutic applications. Meriva® is the most pre-clinically and clinically documented bioavailable curcumin.
Meriva® absorption
Curcumin is known to be poorly absorbed as it is only slightly soluble in water and is rapidly degraded at intestinal pH.
Bio Curcumin 5400 contains Meriva® curcumin, a patented phytosome delivery system where curcumin is bound to sunflower lecithin to create a phospholipid matrix. By embedding curcumin into a phospholipid complex, curcumin is shielded from water
degradation and is stabilised in intestinal pH. The phospholipid matrix has a high affinity to cell membranes, increasing the cellular uptake of curcumin.
A comparative study conducted in humans showed the overall curcuminoid absorption of Meriva® to be 27-fold higher compared to an unformulated curcuminoid mixture, and demonstrated a
50 to 60-fold higher absorption rate for demethoxycurcumin and bisdemethoxycurcumin with Meriva®1.
As Meriva® curcumin is 27 times more bioavailable than regular curcumin, the daily dose of Bio Curcumin 5400 provides 200mg of curcumin, with absorption equal to 5400mg of regular curcumin.

subsections.text: High potency	✓ Healthy hair, skin & nails	✓ Strengthens brittle nails	✓ One-a-day

Biotin, also known as vitamin B7, forms part of the B vitamin family. Biotin is involved in cell growth, fatty acid production and in the metabolism of carbohydrates, fats and proteins.
Biotin is a water-soluble vitamin and is an essential cofactor for 5 carboxylase enzymes including:
Acetyl-coenzyme A (CoA) carboxylase 1 and acetyl-CoA carboxylase 2: binds bicarbonate to acetyl-CoA to form malonyl-CoA, required for the production of fatty acids.
Pyruvate carboxylase: critical for gluconeogenesis (formation of glucose from sources other than carbohydrates such as amino acids and fats).
Methylcrotonyl-CoQ carboxylase: essential step in the metabolism of the amino acid leucine.
Propionyl-CoA carboxylase: catalyses essential steps in the metabolism of amino acids, cholesterol and odd chain fatty acids.
Many foods contain small amounts of biotin and this depends greatly on the season. Foods that contain the most biotin include organ meats, eggs, fish, meat, seeds, nuts and certain vegetables including sweet potato.
Gastrointestinal enzymes break down the protein-bound forms of ingested biotin, which then undergo further processing by the
enzyme biotinidase in the intestinal lumen to release free biotin. The free biotin is then absorbed in the small intestine and most biotin is stored in the liver and central nervous system.
A diet high in raw egg whites can lead to a biotin deficiency. Raw egg whites are high in avidin, a protein that binds to biotin and inhibits its absorption. Cooking denatures avidin, making it unable to interfere with biotin absorption.
Signs and symptoms of biotin deficiency include skin rashes, brittle nails, thinning hair or hair loss.
Pregnancy increases biotin requirements as the fetus requires biotin for carboxylase reactions and DNA replication.
Hair, skin & nails
Biotin 3mg supports hair, skin and nail health. It plays a role in the normal structure and function of skin and mucous membranes. Biotin is a coenzyme for carboxylase enzymes that are involved in fatty acid synthesis, branched-chain amino acid catabolism and
gluconeogenesis, important for maintenance of healthy skin and hair.
Keratin is an important structural protein found in the epidermis. It is the key component of the hair, skin and nails. Keratin mainly functions to adhere cells to each other and to form a protective layer on the outside of the skin. Biotin plays a role in protein synthesis, specifically keratin production.
Biotin 3mg supports nail health, strength and thickness. Brittle nails are characterised by roughness of the surface of the nail plate, fragility and peeling. It is associated with an abnormality of keratin,
keratin associated proteins, water, and/or lipid content. Biotin appears to improve brittle nails by inducing epidermal differentiation.
In one study, 71 subjects with brittle fingernails were given 2.5mg of biotin per day. Out of the 45 subjects that completed the study, 91% showed a definite improvement with firmer and harder fingernails after an average treatment of 5.5±2.3 months1.
Another study investigated the effects of 2.5mg/day of biotin on brittle and splitting fingernails. A total of 32 subjects were placed into 3 groups: group A was the control (n=10), group B comprised subjects with brittle nails (n=8) studied before and after biotin supplementation, and group C included subjects with brittle nails in whom the administration of biotin did not coincide exactly with the initial and terminal clipping of the nails (n=14). The thickness of the nails in group B increased significantly by 25% and group C by 7%. Splitting of the nails were reduced in groups B and C and the irregular cellular arrangement of the dorsal surface of brittle nails became more regular in all nails of group B and in 8 of 11 nails of group C. Results were seen after 6 to 15 months of biotin supplementation2.

Breastfeeding Support contains two herbs, Fenugreek and Blessed thistle, to support milk supply in breastfeeding women.
Fenugreek and Blessed thistle are herbal galactagogues. A galactagogue is a substance that promotes the secretion and flow of milk.
A 2015 qualitative study found that Fenugreek and Blessed thistle were the two most commonly used herbal galactagogues1.
Breastfeeding
During pregnancy, breasts change and develop to be ready to supply milk. The amount of breastmilk usually increases a few days after the birth, when the milk “comes in”.
The first milk produced after the birth is called colostrum, which is more concentrated than mature milk and rich in protein and antibodies. It is gradually replaced by mature milk.
When a baby sucks at the breast, it stimulates nerves in the nipple that release hormones into the blood stream. Prolactin activates milk-making tissues, while oxytocin causes the breast to let down the milk (“let-down reflex”).
Breastmilk is the normal food for babies, containing all the baby’s nutritional needs for the first 6 months of life, satisfying both hunger and thirst, and supporting the baby’s immune system. The act of breastfeeding also helps the baby’s jaw development. Breastfeeding benefits the mother by helping the uterus return to its normal size after childbirth.
One of the most common reasons mothers cease breastfeeding earlier than planned is because they feel they don’t have enough milk for their babies.
Fenugreek
Fenugreek is a herb native to the Mediterranean region, southern Europe and western Asia. It is traditionally used in Western herbal medicine as a nutritive tonic and galactagogue to increase breastmilk production in breastfeeding women.
The mechanism of action of Fenugreek on breastmilk is not fully understood, but it is suggested that Fenugreek stimulates sweat production, which then enhances milk secretion because the breast is a type of sweat gland. Fenugreek may also have oestrogenic activity.
A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled study involving 66 mother-infant pairs assessed the effect of Fenugreek tea on breastmilk production. The mean measured breastmilk volume of
the mothers who received galactagogue tea was significantly higher than the placebo and control groups (p<0.05)2.
An anecdotal report of 1200 women taking 580mg or 610mg of Fenugreek three times a day stated that most women experienced an increase in milk supply within 24 to 72 hours of use3.
Fenugreek also supports healthy appetite.
Blessed thistle
Blessed thistle supports breastmilk production in breastfeeding women. It is believed to work by stimulating the flow of blood to the mammary glands, thereby enriching milk flow.
Blessed thistle is a weed native to the Mediterranean that has been used for over 2000 years to stimulate appetite, aid digestion and as a galactagogue. According to Grieves, “it is chiefly used now for nursing mothers the warm infusion scarcely ever failing to procure a proper supply of milk. It is considered one of the best medicines which can
be used for the purpose”4.

Caution with iron - Fenugreek can inhibit iron absorption. Separate dose by 2 hours.

Bromelain is the general name given to a family of proteolytic enzymes derived from Ananas comosus, the Pineapple plant. Bromelain is present in all parts of the pineapple plant, but the stem is the most common commercial source, presumably because it is readily available after the fruit has been harvested.
Bromelain Forte contains food grade bromelain enzyme isolated from a mixture of both the ripe and unripe fruit as well as the stem of the Pineapple plant. There are no solvents, preservative or antioxidants used in the manufacturing process.
The extraction process involves centriguation, ultrafiltration and lyophilization of cold Pineapple juice which yields a yellowish powder to produce Bromelain.
Figure 1: Bromelain processing
Various designations have been used to indicate the activity of bromelain. Bromelain Forte contains bromelain with 18 million
papain units (PU) per capsule, which is equivalent to 12000 gelatin digestion unit (GDU) activity.
The enzymatic activity of bromelain can be applied over a wide pH spectrum ranging from 5.5 to 8.
Bromelain can be absorbed in human intestines without being degraded or losing its biological activity.
Bromelain is absorbed in the gastrointestinal tract functionally intact and has been shown to retain its proteolytic activity in the plasma where it exhibits its pharmacological effect.
The body can absorb a significant amount of bromelain, with up to 12 grams per day being consumed with no major side effects reported1.
Bromelain Forte should be taken with meals to aid in the digestion of proteins or between meals to reduce swelling, bruising, healing time and pain related to soft tissue trauma.
Digestion
Bromelain Forte is beneficial to support healthy digestion and assists the digestion of proteins.
Bromelain is a digestive enzyme with proteolytic activity which aids the breakdown of proteins to form peptides and amino acids.
Bromelain contains several proteolytic enzymes, which differ in their specificity and optimum environments. Bromelain remains effective over a wide pH range, providing proteolytic activity in the stomach as well as the small intestine.
Bromelain has been used successfully as a digestive enzyme following pancreatectomy and in cases of exocrine pancreas insufficiency2.
Pain & inflammation
Bromelain Forte helps relieve inflammation. Bradykinin is an inflammatory mediator is involved in the mechanism of pain by directly stimulating primary sensory neurons, provoking the release of substance P and neurokinin.
Bromelain’s anti-inflammatory action is due to the inhibition of the generation of bradykinin at the inflammatory site, as well as the limitation of the formation of fibrin by reducing clotting cascade intermediates.
In vitro evidence suggests that bromelain may inhibit COX-2 expression and decrease substance P concentrations and in vivo studies show that bromelain decreases prostaglandin E23.
Bromelain has analgesic properties which are thought to be the result of its direct influence on pain mediators such as bradykinin.

Bulgarian Tribulus Complex contains a combination of Bulgarian and Indian Tribulus. Tribulus is a popular widespread herb found in China, southern Europe, eastern Asia and extending into western Asia. It
has a long history of use in traditional medicine systems, including Chinese and Ayurvedic medicine.
Tribulus terrestris is the most commonly supplemented species of the Tribulus genera. A variety of compounds are present at varying ratios depending on the plant part used. The fruits and root plant parts contain a mixture of different steroidal saponins.
Steroidal saponins are considered to be the most important constituent responsible for the biological activity of Tribulus. They consist of a furostanol or spirostanol-based aglycone and an oligosaccharide attached to a steroid nucleus. The main chemical components of the fruit are steroidal saponins, protodioscin, tribulosaponins A and B, tribulosin and terrestrosina A–K.

Bulgarian Tribulus Complex is a standardised formulation with a total saponin content of ≥40% and contains over 300mg of protodioscin per tablet.
Traditional use
Tribulus is traditionally used in Ayurvedic medicine as an aphrodisiac to enhance libido. The Ayurvedic action is referred to as ‘Vrsya’ which means ‘to increase sexual appetite’. It has also been used as a reproductive tonic to help improve virility and sperm production in men and lactation in women.
Tribulus is traditionally used in Ayurvedic medicine as a male tonic.
It is described as having ‘Brimhana’ and ‘Balya’ actions in Ayurveda, meaning it has the ability to increase body mass and enhance body strength when translated from Sanksrit.
Tribulus herb has also been traditionally used in European folk medicine to energise, vitalise and improve sexual function and physical performance in men.
Sperm health
Bulgarian Tribulus Complex maintains sperm health and supports sperm motility and production in men.
A 2019 systematic review of 7 clinical trials evaluated the effects of Tribulus terrestris on semen parameters in men. The review concluded that the consumption of Tribulus resulted in improved sperm number, motility and morphology, based on 6 out of 7
studies. Protodioscin was shown to be responsible for the increase in sperm count and motility, and increased levels of testosterone and dihydrotestosterone in several studies1.
Menopause support
Bulgarian Tribulus Complex supports healthy female hormonal balance during menopause.
Steroidal saponins present in Tribulus appear to increase serum levels of free and bioavailable testosterone. An increase in the active form of testosterone contributes to the improvement of sexual function in postmenopausal women.
Tribulus seems to increase follicle stimulating hormone (FSH) in women, which in turn increases levels of oestradiol. Steroidal saponins act on the hypothalamus and have been used for alleviating estrogen withdrawals in menopausal women.
Libido
Bulgarian Tribulus Complex supports sexual function and healthy libido in both men and women.
A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial tested the effects of 1500mg/day of Tribulus on 180 males with mild to moderate erectile dysfunction. Compared to placebo, the Tribulus group experienced significant improvements in sexual function, including increased sexual desire, orgasmic function and overall satisfaction after 12 weeks of treatment2.
A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled study evaluated the effects of 750mg/day of Tribulus on 40 healthy women with low libido. Women receiving Tribulus had an improvement in scores for sexual desire, excitation, lubrication, anorgasmia and satisfaction following 4 months of treatment. The placebo group experienced no improvements in sexual function3.

Calcium K2 with D3 contains two highly bioavailable forms of calcium derived from AquaminTM and calcium citrate to support bone density and strength. A diet deficient in calcium can lead to osteoporosis in later life. Calcium may help prevent osteoporosis when dietary intake is inadequate.
Calcium K2 with D3 also contains vitamins K2 and D3 making it an optimal bone health formula. Vitamin D3 improves intestinal absorption of calcium and regulates osteocalcin synthesis by osteoblasts, while vitamin K2 directs and binds calcium into
the bone.
Osteoporosis
Osteoporosis is a condition where bones become brittle, occurring when bones lose minerals, such as calcium, more quickly than the body can replace them, causing a loss of bone density. It is the most common bone disease in humans and increases the risk of fractures. Osteoporosis often has no symptoms and may not be diagnosed until a fracture occurs.
After 30 years of age, bone mass begins to decline in both men and women. Bones are in a constant state of turn over, with old bone being broken down by osteoclasts (resorption) and new bone being built by osteoblasts (formation). Osteoporosis occurs when there
is a significant imbalance between new bone formation and bone resorption.
Risk factors for osteoporosis include:
Low level of physical activity
Smoking
Excessive alcohol intake
Excess body weight
Family history of osteoporosis
Low calcium intake
Low vitamin D levels/lack of sun exposure
Being female
Early menopause
Osteoporosis is common in Australia, with 1.2 million people estimated to have osteoporosis and a further 6.3 million with low bone density1.
While both men and women are at risk of osteoporosis, post-menopausal women, in particular, are at greater risk due to the rapid decline of oestrogen during menopause. When oestrogen levels decrease, bones lose calcium and other minerals at a much faster
rate. As a result, bone loss occurs at approximately 2% per year for several years after menopause. Men also lose bone as they age, however testosterone levels in men decline more gradually so their bone mass usually remains adequate until later in life2.
Calcium for bone health
Calcium is essential for building bone and maintaining bone strength and bone mineralisation. Ninety-nine percent of the body’s calcium is located in the bone matrix. The remaining 1% is found in the blood and other fluids, and is essential for regulation of heartbeat, muscle contraction, release of neurotransmitters, nerve signaling and blood clotting.
Calcium homoeostasis is tightly regulated by parathyroid hormone (PTH), calcitonin and vitamins K and D. These hormones and vitamins determine the level of calcium absorption, excretion or retention via the kidneys and control bone remodeling.
Calcium, with vitamin D3, maintains bone health and healthy teeth. Calcium is stored in the teeth and bones, where it provides structure and strength.
Calcium is especially important for post-menopausal women to support bone health. The Cochrane Collaboration assessed the effects of calcium on bone density and fractures in postmenopausal women. The review covered 15 trials representing 1806 participants and concluded that calcium had a positive effect on bone density and was more effective than placebo in reducing rates of bone loss after two or more years of treatment3.
AquaminTM
Calcium K2 with D3 contains AquaminTM, an all-natural calcium extract derived from calcareous marine algae (Lithothamnion tophiforme). The seaweed is harvested from the North Atlantic seabed and is naturally rich in calcium, magnesium and 72 other trace minerals.
When the algae dies-off and breaks down, it settles naturally on the seabed floor where the calcified remains are harvested, washed, dried and milled. AquaminTM is sustainably sourced, with each step of harvesting controlled to ensure future generations can benefit from the resource. AquaminTM is tested for heavy metals and is GMO-free.
AquaminTM has a unique porous structure, which provides a large surface area for absorption and makes it easier to digest and absorb.
A double-blind, crossover study compared the effects of a single dose of AquaminTM, calcium carbonate or placebo in 12 postmenopausal women. Blood and urine samples were collected at baseline and over 12 hours to evaluate total calcium and parathyroid hormone.

subsections.heading: DRUG INTERACTIONS
subsections.text:
Contraindicated with integrase inhibitors (e.g. dolutegravir, elvitegravir, raltegravir – HIV therapy) – calcium decreases drug serum levels.
Caution with tetracycline and quinolone antibiotics – calcium may reduce drug bioavailability. Take antibiotics either 2 hours before or 4-6 hours after calcium.
Caution with aluminium salts (e.g. antacids) – calcium citrate may increase the absorption of aluminum. Separate dose.
Caution with bisphosphonates – calcium reduces drug absorption and may reduce effectiveness. Take bisphosphonates at least 30 minutes before calcium supplements.
Caution with calcipotriene – administration with calcium may increase the risk of hypercalcaemia.
Caution with sotalol – calcium may reduce drug absorption. Separate dose.
Caution with thyroxine – calcium may reduce drug absorption. Separate dose by at least 4 hours.
Caution with lithium – long-term use may increase risk of hypercalcaemia.
Caution with thiazide diuretics – drug decreases urinary excretion of calcium, potentially increasing risk of hypercalcaemia. Monitor serum calcium levels.
Caution with cardiac glycosides (Digoxin) – calcium and vitamin D supplementation may cause drug toxicity. Monitor use.
Caution with calcium channel blockers – vitamin D and calcium may increase the risk of hypercalcaemia and reduce drug effectiveness (theoretical).
Caution with orlistat – drug interferes with vitamin D and K2 absorption. Seperate dose.
Caution with anticoagulant/antiplatelet drugs – vitamin K may affect anticoagulant effect. Monitor.

subsections.heading: FEATURES & BENEFITS
subsections.text: Pau d’arco 1000mg	✓ Supports immune health	✓ Relieves symptoms of candida

Pau d’arco, also known as Red Lapacho or Taheebo, is a canopy tree native to the Amazon rainforest and can be found in tropical regions of South and Central America. Pau d’arco has been used by native Americans of Brazil, northern Argentina, Paraguay and Peru for over
1000 years, with a long history of medicinal use that pre-dates the Incas.
The bark of the Pau d’arco tree is hard and durable and well-known for its resistance to insect and fungal attack.
Pau d’arco is traditionally used in South American medicine to relieve symptoms of mild, superficial fungal skin infections. Traditionally, the bark/heartwood of Pau d’arco was prepared as a decoction or herbal tea and was prescribed for many ailments including fevers, sore throats, dysentery and snakebites as well as used topically for wounds and skin conditions.
Pau d’arco is also traditionally used in South American medicine to support gastrointestinal system health.
The inner stem bark of Pau d’arco naturally contains bioactive compounds called naphthoquinones and furanonapthoquinones that contribute significantly to the therapeutic activity of the herb.
Two main bioactive components have been isolated from Pau d’arco: lapachol and β-lapachone. These are key constituents responsible for the antifungal and antibacterial activity of Pau d’arco. The majority
of research has focused on the lapachol component, however, other napthoquinones and their furano derivatives are likely to contribute to the therapeutic activity of Pau d’arco.
Candida Relief contains Pau d’arco sourced from Brazil that has been HPLC tested for lapachol content to identify the plant species. Pau d’arco is commonly found to contain adulterants, so proper herbal identification and quality testing is essential.
Candida
Candida albicans (Candida) is a yeast-like fungus that normally inhabits the human microbiome, is present in small amounts on the skin and can be found in the mouth, digestive and reproductive tract.
Candida is a harmless, commensal yeast that exists in harmony with other yeasts and bacteria and is only considered a fungal pathogen when there is an overgrowth in certain areas of the body.
Candida overgrowth can lead to a condition called candidiasis. There are several types of candidiasis, the most common being:
Oral/oropharyngeal/oesophageal thrush: yeast infection in the mouth, throat and oesophageal area. Symptoms include white spots inside the mouth and on the tongue, redness, soreness and difficulty swallowing.
Genital thrush: most commonly experienced by women and characterised by extreme itching, soreness and redness in the vaginal area, accompanied by white clumpy vaginal discharge.
In men, the symptoms include a red rash on the penis and itching and burning on the tip of the penis.
A number of factors can lead to candida overgrowth including disruption to the pH of the environment, antibiotic use, a weakened immune system and immunosuppressants.
Antifungal activity
Pau d’arco supports healthy immune system function and relieves the symptoms of candida. Pau d’arco and its constituents lapachol and β-lapachone have demonstrated in vitro activity against various Candida species including Candida albicans and Candida tropicalis1. Bark extracts of Pau d’arco have also shown broad-spectrum activity in vitro, specifically active against most fungal strains2.
The mechanism of action may involve interference with the fungal cell membrane3. Napthoquinones are inhibitors of the electron transport chain and act by uncoupling oxidative phosphorylation, thus inhibiting ATP synthesis.
Several constituents found in Pau d’arco have also demonstrated antibacterial activity in vitro, including lapachol, β-lapachone and anthraquinone-2-carboxylic acid. These isolated compounds have shown activity against Helicobacter pylori, Clostridium perfringens, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Streptococcus faecalis, Enterococcus and Bacillus species, and various strains of Staphylococcus aureus4,5.
β-lapachone and other napthoquinone compounds have shown activity against methicillin-resistant staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), offering a potential synergistic effect with antimicrobial drugs6.

subsections.text:

Children’s Calci Care contains the key nutrients calcium, vitamin D3 and vitamin K2 to support healthy bone development and growth in children in a great-tasting strawberry-vanilla flavoured chewable tablet.
Children’s Calci Care contains the bioactive form of vitamin D3 (colecalciferol) that is identical to the vitamin D naturally produced by the body.
Children’s Calci Care contains vitamin K2 as menaquinone-7 (MK-7). MK-7 provides a high rate of absorption and bioavailability.
Vitamin D3 is sourced from wild-crafted Reindeer Lichen (Cladonia rangiferina), a natural plant-based source of vitamin D3 that is vegan friendly.
Children’s Calci Care is naturally sweetened with tooth-friendly xylitol. Xylitol is a natural sweetener found mainly in fibrous fruits and vegetables. While sugar has a glycaemic index of 100, xylitol has
a glycaemic index of 7, so it has a negligible effect on blood sugar levels. Xylitol is alkalising which creates an unfriendly environment for bacteria detrimental to tooth enamel.
Bone development
Bone formation in children begins very early in development, at about the third week of foetal life. Cartilage is produced in the shape of the future bone, then during the second trimester of pregnancy this cartilage turns to bone and begins to form the child’s adult-like skeleton. During pregnancy and breastfeeding, bone development and growth is supported by the mother’s calcium levels. However,
once a child moves to a diet of solid foods, their calcium requirements need to be met through their diet.
Skeletal development is most rapid in infancy, with bones growing and strengthening in childhood. Approximately 40% to 60% of adult bone mass is accrued during the adolescent years, with 25% of peak bone mass acquired during the 2-year period when a child
experiences their peak height growth. This peak bone mineral growth rate occurs on average at 12.5 years for girls and 14 years for boys.
At age 18 years, approximately 90% of peak bone mass has been accrued. Childhood and adolescence, therefore, are critical periods for skeletal mineralisation1.
Maintaining adequate calcium intake during childhood is necessary for the development of maximal peak bone mass. Increasing peak bone mass is recognised as an important way to reduce the risk of
osteoporosis in later life2.
Calcium homeostasis is tightly regulated by parathyroid hormone, phosphorous, vitamin K2 and vitamin D. Together they determine the level of calcium absorption, excretion or retention via the kidneys and control the bone remodelling process in the developing skeleton.
In addition to calcium intake, exercise is an important aspect of achieving maximal peak bone mass. There is evidence that childhood and adolescence may represent an important period for achieving long-lasting skeletal benefits from regular exercise3.
Bone growth & bone health in children
Children’s Calci Care assists healthy bone development and supports bone mineralisation and density in children.
Children’s Calci Care contains calcium which is required for the normal development and maintenance of bone.
Over 90% of the bodies total calcium levels are found in bone. Calcium is an essential mineral for bone remodelling, a life-long process in which old bone is removed from the body and replaced with new bone. The bone remodelling process involves the constant addition of calcium to the bone and removal of calcium from the bone and into circulation.
Vitamin K2 is a fat-soluble vitamin, essential for calcium distribution in the body. Vitamin K2 is crucial for bone building and bone strength, as it incorporates or binds calcium into bones, whilst driving calcium away from blood vessels.
Vitamin K2 is a group of compounds, known as menaquinones (MKs). MK-7 has high rate of absorption and bioavailability and is only obtained in the Western diet through the intake of fermented foods.
Vitamin D facilitates calcium absorption by attaching to specific vitamin D receptors (VDR) on target cells responsible for the synthesis of different proteins involved in calcium transport and utilisation.
Muscle health & function in children
Children’s Calci Care contains calcium and vitamin D, important nutrients for muscle health and muscle strength in children.
The contraction and relaxation of muscles occurs due to rapidly changing calcium concentrations within the cells of muscles, a biochemical process known as the calcium cycle. Adequate calcium is required for a balanced calcium cycle, necessary for the healthy functioning of muscles.

subsections.text:
Soothes & calms nerves in children
Relieves irritability & restlessness
Great tasting forest berry flavour
With tooth friendly xylitol
Contains Lactium® a milk protein with calming effects
Children are faced with many stressful situations within their day. When they’re unable to cope with new environments, frustration can begin to build, putting them in fight or flight mode. Once this reaction begins, chemicals including adrenaline, noradrenaline and cortisol can cause children to become overexcited, and calming them down from this physiological response can be challenging.
Children’s behavior is strongly influenced by their sleep patterns. Shorter sleep duration has been associated with inattention, impaired memory and learning, irritability, moodiness, temper tantrums and hyperactivity1. Improving children’s quality of sleep may have a positive effect on their behavior.
Ongoing stress can have secondary effects on children’s health, such as poor immunity, low energy, digestive disturbances and low appetite.
Children’s Calm Care contains Lactium®, a natural milk protein that was discovered when researchers began to investigate the calming state of babies after drinking milk. Its calming effects are due to its action on gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) pathways. GABA is a neurotransmitter with calming effects on the brain.
Children’s Calm Care contains magnesium as amino acid chelate. Magnesium bound to an amino acid allows for greater absorption through the intestinal wall.
Children’s Calm Care is naturally sweetened with tooth-friendly xylitol. Xylitol is a natural sweetener found mainly in fibrous fruits and vegetables. While sugar has a glycaemic index of 100, xylitol has
a glycaemic index of 7, so it has a negligible effect on blood sugar levels. Xylitol is alkalising which creates an unfriendly environment for bacteria detrimental to tooth enamel.
Nervous system health
Chamomile is traditionally used in Western herbal medicine for its calming effect on children. Chamomile has been found useful in children that are irritable, anxious, nervous and restless2. Its mild sedative action can also help children fall asleep.
Chamomile is considered the classic herbal remedy for restlessness and nervous irritability in children3. An archetypal children’s remedy, it has a long history of use for whining and irritated infants.
Magnesium is important for maintaining nervous system health. When stressed, magnesium is released from the blood cells and goes
into the blood plasma, where it is then excreted via urine. Ongoing stress depletes the body of its magnesium stores.
Magnesium has a protective effect on the nervous system by its action on GABA, the neurotransmitter responsible for calming the body and the mind.
Digestive discomfort
Chamomile is traditionally used in Western herbal medicine in young children to help relieve digestive complaints, such as wind, bloating, belching and burping. Chamomile is also helpful for reducing inflammation in the gastrointestinal tract and can be used in combination with probiotics for digestive discomfort.
The Commission E has approved Chamomile for internal use for gastrointestinal spasms and inflammation of the gastrointestinal tract4.

Children’s Fish-i Care comes in a delicious vanilla-berry flavoured fish-shaped chewable capsule suitable for children.
Omega-3 essential fatty acids (EFAs), such as EPA and DHA, are ‘good’ fats that must be obtained through the diet as the body cannot synthesise them. The best dietary sources of omega-3s are fish, seafood, nuts, seeds and oils. Supplementing with Children’s Fish-i Care can be beneficial for children who do not consume fish or have a diet low in fish.
EFAs are required for healthy brain function, nervous system development, healthy eyes and skin. EFAs are involved in oxygen transportation, energy storage, cell membrane integrity, intercellular communication and the control of inflammation.
Children’s Fish-i Care also contains iodine to help prevent a dietary iodine deficiency. Iodine is important for normal growth and development and to help maintain healthy brain and cognitive function.
Children’s Fish-i Care contains tooth friendly xylitol. Xylitol is a chemical-free, natural sweetener found mainly in fibrous fruit and vegetables. While sugar has a glycaemic index of 100, xylitol has a glycaemic index of 7, so it has a negligible effect on blood sugar. Xylitol is alkalising which creates an unfriendly environment for bacteria that is detrimental to tooth enamel.
Healthy brain function
DHA plays a critical role in normal brain development in children, being taken up by the brain in preference to other fatty acids. DHA is also an important structural component of the brain, playing a key role in the structural membrane lipid of nerve tissue and the retina, making it important for normal eye function.
Omega-3 fatty acids, in particular DHA, are important during periods of brain growth spurts which take place through various times of early brain development, throughout childhood and into adolescence. Omega-3s play an active role in neuronal membrane function and fluidity.
Eye health & development
DHA plays an important role in retinal development in children, as well as contributing to the structural integrity of the membrane liquid of the eye, nerve tissue and the retina.

Children’s Immune Care contains tooth friendly xylitol. Xylitol is a chemical-free, natural sweetener found mainly in fibrous fruit and vegetables. Immune system health
Children’s Immune Care contains Echinacea, vitamins C and D and zinc to maintain immune system health and support the immune system to fight illness in children. It also contains citrus bioflavonoids to support the absorption of vitamin C.
Echinacea possesses immune modulating, stimulating and enhancing effects in the body. It appears to promote the activity of the white blood cells macrophages, natural killer cells and T-lymphocytes and increases the secretion of interleukin-1 (another important component of the immune system) to help fight infection.
Vitamin D3 is the bioactive form of vitamin D, important for a healthy immune system as it enhances the activity of white blood cells.
Zinc, vitamin C, bioflavonoids and Acerola all act as antioxidants in the body to reduce free radicals and support immune system health.
Respiratory tract infections & common colds & flu
Upper respiratory tract infections (URTIs) are highly prevalent in children as their immune systems are immature, not reaching the full level of maturity until somewhere between 12-14 years of age. On average, children have 6 to 8 URTIs per year while adults have only 2-31.
Children’s Immune Care contains Echinacea, traditionally used in Western herbal medicine to reduce the occurrence of symptoms of URTIs and relieve the symptoms of common colds and flu, including upper respiratory tract congestion.
