Children’s Magnesium Care contains organically bound forms of magnesium with high bioavailability in the body.
Magnesium is an essential nutrient for over 300 enzymatic processes in the body, required for DNA replication, energy production, muscle contraction and relaxation, cardiac rhythm, vascular tone, DNA and RNA synthesis, carbohydrate, protein and fat metabolism, bone formation, cell signalling, neurological function and brain function.
Magnesium is found in green leafy vegetables, nuts, seeds, whole grains and cacao. Today’s farming and agricultural practices have led to a decline in the magnesium content in foods, with estimates that magnesium content has decreased by as much as 80-90% in vegetables such as lettuce and spinach1.
Fussy eating habits, food allergies or food intolerances can mean a child isn’t obtaining the recommended intake of magnesium each day.
Children’s Magnesium Care contains a therapeutic dose of 80mg of elemental magnesium per chewable tablet, helping to boost a child’s magnesium intake in order to meet recommended daily intakes.
Children’s Magnesium Care contains tooth friendly xylitol. Xylitol is a natural sweetener found mainly in fibrous fruits and vegetables. While sugar has a glycaemic index of 100, xylitol has a glycaemic index of 7, so it has a negligible effect on blood sugar levels. Xylitol is alkalising which creates an unfriendly environment for bacteria detrimental to tooth enamel.
Children’s Magnesium Care is suitable for children aged 4 years and up and can be used to support energy production, muscle, bone and nervous system health in growing children.
Energy production
Children’s Magnesium Care supports energy production in children. Magnesium is involved in the metabolism of carbohydrates and fats to produce energy and is critical for the manufacture of adenosine triphosphate (ATP) within cells.
Between the age of three years old and middle adolescence, the body uses approximately 1% to 2% of energy requirements for growth alone.
Nervous system health
Children’s Magnesium Care supports healthy nervous system function. Magnesium is required for nerve conduction, modulating the hypothalamic pituitary adrenal axis and reducing the release of adrenalin and noradrenalin, supporting a healthy stress response in the body.
Several studies have assessed serum magnesium levels in children displaying a range of symptoms including hyperactivity, disruptive behaviour, restlessness and difficulty focusing. In one such study, magnesium deficiency was found in 95% of children examined2.
Muscle health
Children’s Magnesium Care supports muscle health and muscle contraction function in children.
About 50% to 60% of all magnesium in the body is found in the skeleton, while the remainder is found in soft tissue, primarily muscle.
It is estimated that between 25% to 40% of normally developing children experience the discomfort associated with cramping, particularly in the legs during periods of rapid growth. Leg muscle cramping occurs as bones grow and skeletal alignment is altered, requiring the muscles to grow, stretch and accommodate to bodily changes, putting extra force on muscle fibres.
Adequate levels of magnesium can assist with cellular functioning and the relaxation of smooth muscle in periods of rapid growth.
Cardiovascular system health
Magnesium helps maintain cardiovascular system health and heart health. It is essential for cardiac muscle contraction and production of energy within the heart muscle.
Magnesium plays a role in the active transport of calcium and potassium ions across cell membranes, which is essential for nerve impulse conduction, muscle contraction and normal heart rhythm. It is also essential for the contractility of vascular smooth muscle cells in the arterial wall and influences endothelial function, thereby influencing vasodilation and vasoconstriction.
Bone health
Magnesium supports bone health and assists in the development and maintenance of bones and teeth. Up to 60% of total body magnesium stores resides in bone, binding at the surface of the hydroxyapatite crystals. Magnesium in bones serves as a reservoir of magnesium, which can be released from bone to maintain physiological extracellular concentrations when magnesium intake is low.
In a study of 63 healthy children aged 4 to 8 years, an isotope study of magnesium absorption measured bone mineral content in each of the subjects. Results showed the amount of magnesium consumed and absorbed were key predictors of the level of bone in children, even more so than calcium3.

subsections.heading: DRUG INTERACTIONS
subsections.text:
Caution with aminoglycoside antibiotics (e.g. gentamicin) - both it and magnesium affect muscle function, potentially leading to muscle weakness and side effects. Co-administration should be avoided.
Caution with quinolone and tetracycline antibiotics – magnesium forms insoluble complexes with drugs, decreasing drug absorption. Take drug 2 hours before or 6 hours after magnesium.
Caution with bisphosphonates – magnesium can form complexes with drug and reduce absorption. Separate dose by 2 hours.
Caution with potassium-sparing diuretics – these drugs also have magnesium-sparing properties which could, theoretically, lead to increased magnesium levels. Monitor.
Caution with skeletal muscle relaxants – magnesium can potentiate effects.

Adequate provision of nutrients, beginning in the early stages of life, is crucial to ensure good physical and mental development and long-term health in children. While a child’s diet should provide all the vitamins and minerals they need, often fussy eating habits or food allergies or intolerances can mean a child isn’t obtaining the recommended intake of certain vitamins and minerals each day.
Children’s Multi Care contains a blend of 21 vitamins, minerals and nutrients in a great tasting chewable tablet for easy compliance.
Children’s Multi Care contains tooth-friendly xylitol. Xylitol is a natural sweetener found mainly in fibrous fruits and vegetables. While sugar has a glycaemic index of 100, xylitol has a glycaemic index of 7, so it has a negligible effect on blood sugar levels. Xylitol is alkalising which creates an unfriendly environment for bacteria that are detrimental to tooth enamel.
Children’s Multi Care is suitable for children aged 2 years and up and can be taken once or twice a day to support general health and wellbeing.
Energy production
Children’s Multi Care contains vitamins B1, B2, B5, B6 and B12 to help in the conversion of food into energy. B vitamins are important for the production of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), a chemical form of
cellular energy used by every cell in the body for metabolic processes.
Between the age of three years old and middle adolescence, the body uses approximately 1% to 2% of energy requirements for growth alone.
Antioxidant
Children’s Multi Care contains the antioxidant nutrients vitamin C, citrus bioflavonoids, vitamin E, selenium and zinc to help reduce free radicals in the body.
Vitamin C is the most important water-soluble antioxidant, providing important protection for cells against oxidative damage. The body does not store vitamin C, meaning regular intake of adequate fruits
and vegetables is essential to maintain appropriate levels, which does not always occur in a child’s diet.
Vitamin E is the most important fat-soluble antioxidant, protecting vitamin C, vitamin A, red blood cells and essential fatty acids from free radicals.
Selenium is an important component of glutathione peroxidases
1-4, antioxidant enzymes that reduce potentially damaging reactive oxygen species (ROS). Zinc is an essential part of the antioxidant enzyme copper/zinc superoxide dismutase (Cu/Zn SOD).
Cognitive function & brain health
Children’s Multi Care contains iodine, important for supporting a child’s brain health and cognitive development.
Iodine is used by the thyroid gland to help regulate metabolism and for the development of both a child’s skeleton and brain.
To help in the management of adequate iodine levels, Australia and New Zealand introduced mandatory fortification of iodine in bread in 2009.
Nervous system
Children’s Multi Care contains vitamins B1, B2, B5, B6 and B12 to help support a healthy nervous system in children and assist in the synthesis of neurotransmitters.
Vitamin B6 is involved in the conversion of tryptophan to niacin, the synthesis of gamma aminobutyric acid (GABA) in the central nervous system as well as the metabolism of serotonin, norepinephrine and dopamine.
Vitamin B12 is required for the proper functioning and development of the brain and nerve cells. It is essential for the myelin sheath that covers and protects the nerves of the central and the peripheral nervous system, ensuring fast and effective nerve-impulse transmission.
Serotonin and dopamine are neurotransmitters that play a role in overall mood and wellbeing.

Probiotics are microorganisms proven to have health-promoting influences in humans. The term ‘probiotic’ means ‘for life’.
Compared to the more resistant adult microbiome, a child’s microbiome is less resilient and more susceptible to changes in response to diet modifications, antibiotic treatment and other events such as illness.
In order for probiotics to have a therapeutic effect, they need to have the following characteristics: gastric acid and bile salt stability; an ability to adhere to the intestinal mucosa; and an ability to colonise the intestinal tract.
Children’s Probiotic 15 Billion contains 15 different strains that survive both stomach acid and bile and adhere to the intestinal mucosa. Good adherence to intestinal mucosa is important as it prolongs the time a probiotic strain can reside in the intestine, giving it an opportunity to modulate the immune response and protect against enteric pathogens by limiting their ability to colonise the intestine.
Children’s Probiotic 15 Billion contains studied probiotic strains supplied by Danisco®, a supplier trusted by some of the world’s most recognised manufacturers. Danisco® utilises patented stabilisation technology to improve shelf-life and to stabilise the phospholipid bilayer of the probiotic cell membrane, so that all the strains are room-stable and do not require refrigeration. Children’s Probiotic
15 Billion also contains Bifidobacterium breve M16-V, a well-studied strain in infants and children.
Intestinal microbiota
The gastrointestinal microbiota plays a critical role in nutritional, metabolic and immune functions in children and infants.
The human gastrointestinal tract is populated by bacteria, archaea, yeasts and fungi, which are collectively referred to as the
gastrointestinal (GI) microbiota. The microbiota has several important functions in maintaining human health, including providing the host with nutrients and protecting from harmful microbes. It is involved in many metabolic processes, including the fermentation of undigested carbohydrates into short-chain fatty acids, lipid metabolism and vitamin synthesis.
The ecological balance of the intestinal microbiota can be disturbed by environmental or physiological factors, such as antibiotics, stress and diet.
Children’s Probiotic 15 Billion helps maintain a balanced, healthy composition of the intestinal microbiota.
Lactobacillus rhamnosus HN001, Bifidobacterium lactis HN019, Lactobacillus acidophilus La-14, Lactobacillus salivarius Ls-33, Lactobacillus paracasei Lpc-37 and Lactobacillus plantarum Lp-115 have displayed in vitro inhibition of common pathogens.
Digestive system health
Children’s Probiotic 15 Billion supports a child’s digestive health by maintaining beneficial intestinal flora, contributing to its ability to function normally.
Children can suffer from many digestive related complaints while their digestive systems strengthen. A fully functional digestive system is a delicate balance while intestinal flora builds. This balance can be disrupted by diet, colds and flu and antibiotics.
Colonisation of the gut with appropriate microflora contributes to its ability to function normally.
Specifically, Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG has been shown to relieve functional pain in children suffering from irritable bowel syndrome symptoms. A double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled study found that supplementation with 6 billion CFU/day Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG (two serves of Children’s Probiotic 15 Billion) led to
a statistically significant reduction in both frequency (p<0.01), and severity (p<0.01) of abdominal pain1.

Compared to the more resistant adult microbiome, a child’s microbiome is less resilient and more susceptible to changes in response to diet modifications, antibiotic treatment and other events such as illness.

Intestinal microbiota
The gastrointestinal microbiota plays a critical role in nutritional, metabolic and immune functions in children and infants.
The human gastrointestinal tract is populated by bacteria, archaea, yeasts and fungi, which are collectively referred to as the
gastrointestinal (GI) microbiota. The microbiota has several important functions in maintaining human health, including providing the host with nutrients and protecting from harmful microbes. It is involved in many metabolic processes, including the fermentation of undigested carbohydrates into short-chain fatty acids, lipid metabolism and vitamin synthesis.
The ecological balance of the intestinal microbiota can be disturbed by environmental or physiological factors, such as antibiotics, stress and diet.
Children’s Probiotic 15 Billion helps maintain a balanced, healthy composition of the intestinal microbiota.

Chromium is an essential trace mineral required for carbohydrate, protein and lipid metabolism.
Chromium is found in a wide variety of foods, but most sources only contain small amounts due to soil depletion, particularly in Australia.

subsections.heading: DRUG INTERACTIONS
subsections.text:
Caution with hypoglycaemic medication - chromium may have an additive effect. Monitor blood sugar levels.
Caution with thyroxine – chromium can reduce drug absorption. Seperate dose by at least 3 hours.
Food sources rich in chromium include organ meats, cheese, broccoli,
green beans, spices and wine.
The absorption of chromium from the intestinal tract is low and can be enhanced by the intake of nutrients such as vitamin C and niacin. Chromium is stored in the liver, spleen, soft tissue and bone.
Diets high in simple sugars result in increased urinary chromium excretion in adults. This effect may be related to increased insulin secretion in response to the consumption of simple sugars compared to complex carbohydrates.
Stressors, such as elevated blood sugar, strenuous physical activity or work, infection and emotional and physical trauma, may increase the excretion of chromium.
Glucose metabolism
Chromium was first identified as ‘Glucose Tolerance Factor’, however, it was later discovered to be a complex of molecules found in the body comprised of chromium bound to single molecules of glycine, cysteine, glutamic acid, and two molecules of nicotinic acid.
Chromium MAX aids the metabolism of glucose and supports the cellular uptake of glucose. Low chromium levels are associated with impaired glucose, insulin and lipid metabolism.
Chromium can improve insulin sensitivity, aiding the ability of insulin to transport glucose into cells. Chromium seems to be transported to insulin-sensitive cells by transferrin in response to increases in
plasma insulin levels. It is suspected to potentiate insulin by increasing receptor numbers and affinity as well as increasing insulin binding to cells.
Food satiety
Chromium picolinate has been suggested to impact neurotransmitters involved in the regulation of eating behaviour, mood and food cravings.
An 8-week randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled study was performed to investigate the effects of chromium on food intake, satiety and cravings. A total of 42 healthy, overweight women who reported carbohydrate cravings were randomly assigned either 1000 micrograms/day of chromium picolinate or placebo. The group receiving chromium reported decreased food intake and hunger ratings by week 8. A decrease in cravings for carbohydrates, fast foods, high-fat foods and sweet was noted over time1.

Clear Skin is a combination of traditional herbs with strong depurative actions to help relieve acne and minor skin conditions and support skin health. It also contains vitamin A, B6 and zinc to maintain skin health and wound healing.
Clear Skin contains vitamin A and zinc, potent antioxidants to reduce free radicals in the body.
Acne
Acne is a common skin condition that affects the face, back and chest and can affect self-esteem. It usually begins in the teenage years as hormone changes occur, however, it can persist into the 30s and 40s.
Acne is caused by inflammation of the hair follicles and appears as blackheads, whiteheads, pimples and cysts. In severe cases, acne can lead to permanent scarring. Acne occurs when the hair follicles get blocked by excess sebum, which is usually driven by androgens. Dead skin cells mix with the blockage and bacteria in the skin multiply which can cause pain and swelling (inflammation) beneath the blockages.
Factors that can exacerbate acne include stress, poor diet, being overweight, not getting enough exercise and hormonal shifts. It is very common for women to experience breakouts before their periods.
Skin health
Clear Skin contains Burdock and Yellow dock, herbs traditionally used in Western herbal medicine (WHM) to support skin health. These herbs are classed as depuratives. Depuratives, also known as alteratives and blood cleansers, improve detoxification and aid
elimination channels via the kidneys, skin and mucous membranes to reduce the accumulation of metabolic waste production in the body.
Burdock and Yellow dock are depuratives that work principally via the liver and digestion and also support hepatic detoxification.
Burdock is also used in WHM as a diuretic to enhance urine output and a diaphoretic to induce sweating. Thus, it helps improve elimination via both the skin and kidneys.
Yellow dock is traditionally used in WHM as an alterative and depurative herb to support waste elimination via the skin. Yellow dock also has mild laxative effects, helping to support elimination
via the bowels. The Physiomedical Dispensatory (1869) states that “the greater portion of its power is expended upon the skin; but the gall ducts, small intestines, and kidneys, feel its impressions to a fair extent”1.
Calendula is traditionally used in WHM as an anti-inflammatory and vulnerary to support wound healing.
In addition to herbs, Clear Skin contains the nutrients vitamin A and zinc to support skin health. Vitamin A supports collagen formation and epithelial cell differentiation.
Zinc is an essential mineral for skin health and is necessary for connective tissue formation and wound healing. The skin contains 6% of total body zinc2. Zinc is also required for the hepatic synthesis of retinol binding protein, which is the transport protein of vitamin A. Therefore, insufficient zinc can result in the symptoms of a vitamin A deficiency, even with adequate vitamin A intake.
Acne & minor skin conditions
Clear Skin contains Burdock, traditionally used in WHM to relieve symptoms of acne and minor skin eruptions.
Traditionally, alteratives or depuratives are used for chronic skin conditions and work by purifying the blood and detoxifying and supporting eliminatory channels to reduce the accumulation of metabolic waste products. In modern herbalism, depuratives are the main herbs used for acne. Burdock, Yellow dock and Calendula are important depuratives for acne.
It is generally recognised that depuratives in high doses can cause a temporary exacerbation of symptoms. Strong depuratives, such as Burdock, can be combined with more eliminatory herbs, such as Yellow dock, to reduce the potential for exacerbation3.
Burdock is traditionally used in WHM to support waste elimination via the skin, relieve minor skin eruptions and relieve the symptoms of mild eczema. According to eclectic texts, the herb is indicated for dry, scaly skin eruptions and recurrent boils, especially with feeble
circulation in the skin, as it gently stimulates the kidneys and promotes the elimination of waste material4. According to Grieves, Burdock root is “one of the best blood purifiers. In all skin diseases, it is a certain remedy and has effected a cure in many cases of eczema”5.

subsections.heading: DRUG INTERACTIONS
subsections.text:
Contraindicated with antineoplastic drugs (etoposide) – Echinacea may increase risk of drug toxicity.
Contraindicated with retinoids (vitamin A derivatives) e.g. Accutane – vitamin A supplementation may have additive toxic effects.
Caution with Digoxin – long term use of Yellow dock may result in potassium loss, which increases risk of drug toxicity (usually at higher doses).
Caution with immunosuppressive drugs - Echinacea has immunostimulatory effects.
Caution with cyclophosphamide – Echinacea may increase the immunostimulatory effect, which may be problematic in autoimmune conditions. Use under the supervision of a health professional.
Caution with anticoagulant/antiplatelet drugs – Burdock may theoretically increase the risk of bleeding. Monitor.
Caution with antidiabetic drugs – Burdock may theoretically have additive effects. Monitor blood sugar levels.
Caution with potassium sparing diuretics – concurrent use with long term use of Yellow dock may increase the risk of hypokalaemia.
Caution with NSAIDs, cefalexin, penacillamine and quinolone and tetracycline antibiotics – zinc interferes with absorption. Separate dose by 3 hours.

Cold & Flu Strike is a combination of immunostimulating herbs plus nutrients to support immune health and reduce the severity and duration of common colds, flu and mild upper respiratory tract infections (URTIs).
URTIs are characterised by infectious pathogens that affect the sinuses, nasal passages, pharynx and larynx and are one of the most common reasons for a doctor visit. The majority of URTIs are caused by viral infections, though some are of bacterial origin, and are highly contagious with the ability to spread from person to person via droplets from an infected person coughing or sneezing.
The common cold is a type of URTI, with more than 200 different viruses that can cause the infection. On average, an adult will get 2-4 colds every year. Symptoms can include sore throat, fever, sneezing, blocked or runny nose and cough. These symptoms are usually mild to moderately severe and usually resolve within 7-10 days.
Andrographis
Andrographis relieves the symptoms of common colds, flu and mild URTIs, including cough, sore throat and mild fever.
Andrographis reduces the severity of symptoms of the common cold and flu and decreases the duration of the common cold.
Andrographis is traditionally used in Chinese medicine to relieve symptoms of common colds, flu and mild URTIs, including cough, sore throat and fever. It is traditionally used in Ayurvedic medicine as an antipyretic to relieve mild fever.
The active constituents in Andrographis are diterpene lactones, commonly known as andrographolides, which have anti-inflammatory, antiviral and immunomodulating activity. A dose of 60mg of andrographolides per day has shown positive benefits to immune health. Cold & Flu Strike contains Andrographis standardised to contain 60mg of andrographolides per tablet.
A 2017 systematic review and meta-analysis that included 33 randomised, controlled trails, with a total of 7175 patients, found that Andrographis, either alone or plus usual care, had a statistically significant effect in improving overall symptoms of acute respiratory tract infections when compared to placebo, usual care and other
herbal therapies. The review showed that Andrographis shortened the duration of coughs, sore throat and sick leave/time to resolution when compared to usual care. Additionally, no major adverse events were reported1.
Two 2004 systematic reviews of Andrographis concluded that the herb is more effective than placebo in uncomplicated acute upper respiratory tract infections2,3. A total of 7 double-blind, controlled trails (n=896) concluded that Andrographis was superior to placebo in alleviating the subjective symptoms of uncomplicated URTIs and may help reduce the risk of mild URTI. Of the 7 studies included in the meta-analysis, 5 used Andrographis standardised to 60mg of andrographolide per day4.
Immune support
Cold & Flu Strike contains Echinacea purpurea whole plant, which helps maintain healthy immune function. Both the German
Commission E and the World Health Organisation approve the use of Echinacea purpurea herb as supportive therapy for colds and infections of the respiratory tract5,6. Beneficial effects are believed to be brought about by stimulation of the immune response. Research has found Echinacea has a nonspecific effect in stimulating the immune system, involving an overall increase in phagocytosis by macrophages and granulocytes, and can increase the number of white blood cells.
Echinacea is traditionally used in Western herbal medicine (WHM) to support immune system health. Traditional texts refer to Echinacea’s antiseptic properties and its ability to “increase bodily resistance to infection”7.
Elderberry is traditionally used in WHM to help relieve symptoms of colds and flu, such as coughs, sore throat and catarrh of the upper respiratory tract.
Elderberry’s immune benefits are mostly due to antiviral effects. Research has shown that Elderberry constituents neutralise the activity of haemagglutinin spikes found on the surface of viruses. By deactivating these hemagglutinin spikes, the viruses are no longer able to pierce cell walls or enter the cell and replicate8.

Andrographis is traditionally used in Chinese medicine to relieve symptoms of common colds, flu and mild URTIs, including cough, sore throat and fever. It is traditionally used in Ayurvedic medicine as an antipyretic to relieve mild fever.
The active constituents in Andrographis are diterpene lactones, commonly known as andrographolides, which have anti-inflammatory, antiviral and immunomodulating activity. A dose of 60mg of andrographolides per day has shown positive benefits to immune health. Cold & Flu Strike contains Andrographis standardised to contain 60mg of andrographolides per tablet.
A 2017 systematic review and meta-analysis that included 33 randomised, controlled trails, with a total of 7175 patients, found that Andrographis, either alone or plus usual care, had a statistically significant effect in improving overall symptoms of acute respiratory tract infections when compared to placebo, usual care and other
herbal therapies. The review showed that Andrographis shortened the duration of coughs, sore throat and sick leave/time to resolution when compared to usual care. Additionally, no major adverse events were reported1.
Two 2004 systematic reviews of Andrographis concluded that the herb is more effective than placebo in uncomplicated acute upper respiratory tract infections2,3. A total of 7 double-blind, controlled trails (n=896) concluded that Andrographis was superior to placebo in alleviating the subjective symptoms of uncomplicated URTIs and may help reduce the risk of mild URTI. Of the 7 studies included in the meta-analysis, 5 used Andrographis standardised to 60mg of andrographolide per day4.
Immune support
Cold & Flu Strike contains Echinacea purpurea whole plant, which helps maintain healthy immune function. Both the German
Commission E and the World Health Organisation approve the use of Echinacea purpurea herb as supportive therapy for colds and infections of the respiratory tract5,6. Beneficial effects are believed to be brought about by stimulation of the immune response. Research has found Echinacea has a nonspecific effect in stimulating the immune system, involving an overall increase in phagocytosis by macrophages and granulocytes, and can increase the number of white blood cells.
Echinacea is traditionally used in Western herbal medicine (WHM) to support immune system health. Traditional texts refer to Echinacea’s antiseptic properties and its ability to “increase bodily resistance to infection”7.
Elderberry is traditionally used in WHM to help relieve symptoms of colds and flu, such as coughs, sore throat and catarrh of the upper respiratory tract.
Elderberry’s immune benefits are mostly due to antiviral effects. Research has shown that Elderberry constituents neutralise the activity of haemagglutinin spikes found on the surface of viruses. By deactivating these hemagglutinin spikes, the viruses are no longer able to pierce cell walls or enter the cell and replicate8.

Collagen provides 400mg of bioactive hydrolysed collagen plus nutrients zinc and vitamin C in a convenient, easy-to-take capsule.
Collagen
Collagen is the body’s most abundant protein, representing approximately 30% of total body protein. Collagen is a major structural component of connective tissue that makes up skin, hair, nails, ligaments, tendons, cartilage, teeth and bone.
Collagen consists of amino acids comprised of three polypeptide chains that wrap tightly around each other to form a triple helix molecule resembling a rope-like shape. The rigid structure of collagen provides tensile strength and firmness to connective tissues around the body.
Approximately 28 types of collagen have been identified in the human body. Type I, II and III collagens are the most predominant types, each containing different proteins that serve specific roles and are distributed differently in the body:
Type I: most common type of collagen and mainly present in skin, bone, teeth, tendons, ligaments, vascular ligature and organs.
Type II: main structural component of cartilage tissue and provides flexibility and support to bone joints.
Type III: present in skin, muscle, vessels and reticular fibres of organ tissues such as the liver, spleen and lungs.
Over 90% of collagen in the body is comprised of type I and III collagen produced by fibroblasts (cells in connective tissues) and osteoblasts (cells that make bones).
The amino acids crucial for collagen synthesis and production are:
Glycine: most abundant amino acid found in collagen and synthesised by serine.
Proline: non-essential amino acid vital for collagen biosynthesis, strength and structure.
Lysine: essential amino acid involved in collagen formation.
Proline and lysine are converted into their active forms, hydroxyproline and hydroxylysine respectively via hydroxylation. Hydroxyproline and hydroxylysine are major components of
cross linkages in collagen and play a key role in collagen stability. Hydroxylation of proline and lysine is dependent upon adequate levels of vitamin C as a cofactor for collagen protein synthesis and repair.
Figure 1: Structure of collagen fibres
Collagen Molecules
Collagen vs collagen peptides
Collagen in its natural state is referred to as native collagen. It is formed from three very long chains of over 1000 amino acids twisting into a helix conformation. In its full-length, unhydrolysed form, collagen is not an effective oral supplement as it is difficult to break down during digestion and too large to cross the intestinal wall.
Collagen peptides are short chain protein building blocks characterised by high levels of specific amino acids glycine, hydroxyproline, proline and alanine. This amino acid composition provides collagen peptides their unique bioactive properties not found with other protein sources.
Native collagen undergoes enzymatic hydrolysis to break the bonds in the polypeptide chain, creating a larger number of peptides with reduced weight and size, which increases bioavailability in humans.
Hydrolysed collagen peptides are very small molecules and offer a low molecular weight with increased solubility in water and enhanced digestibility and absorption. Collagen peptides are available as small, unique peptides characterised by a Hyp-Pro containing sequence and are quickly absorbed into the blood stream after intake. They act as important signal molecules to stimulate cells and provides building blocks to support connective tissue and musculoskeletal health.

Joint health
A joint is an articulation where two bones are cushioned by cartilage and lubricated with synovial fluid. Joints are comprised of bone, muscles, synovium, cartilage and ligaments designed to bear weight and facilitate movement.
Collagen is a major component of connective tissue that makes up the cartilage, tendons and ligaments that provide structural integrity to the joints. Type II collagen is primarily found in the articular cartilage of joints.
Cartilage degradation can occur over time due to wear and tear, repeated movement and ageing.
Preclinical studies have demonstrated that hydrolysed collagen can pass the mucosal barrier in the small bowel as a complete peptide, accumulating in cartilage tissue and stimulating the production of type II collagen6.
A 12-week randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in 139 athletes with functional knee problems found a 5g dose of bioactive collagen peptides significantly improved activity-related pain intensity and reduced joint pain under resting conditions compared to placebo7.
In a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled study, administration of 10g hydrolysed collagen to athletes with activity related joint pain improved joint symptoms after 24 weeks. Statistically significant changes were seen in joint pain at rest, upon movement and when lifting heavy objects compared to placebo8.
Collagen Forte can be taken once or twice daily to support joint health.

Joint health
A joint is an articulation where two bones are cushioned by cartilage and lubricated with synovial fluid. Joints are comprised of bone, muscles, synovium, cartilage and ligaments designed to bear weight and facilitate movement.
Collagen is a major component of connective tissue that makes up the cartilage, tendons and ligaments that provide structural integrity to the joints. Type II collagen is primarily found in the articular cartilage of joints.
Cartilage degradation can occur over time due to wear and tear, repeated movement and ageing.
Preclinical studies have demonstrated that hydrolysed collagen can pass the mucosal barrier in the small bowel as a complete peptide, accumulating in cartilage tissue and stimulating the production of type II collagen6.
A 12-week randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in 139 athletes with functional knee problems found a 5g dose of bioactive collagen peptides significantly improved activity-related pain intensity and reduced joint pain under resting conditions compared to placebo7.
In a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled study, administration of 10g hydrolysed collagen to athletes with activity related joint pain improved joint symptoms after 24 weeks. Statistically significant changes were seen in joint pain at rest, upon movement and when lifting heavy objects compared to placebo8.
Collagen Forte can be taken once or twice daily to support joint health.

Collagen Gold provides 2.5g of bioactive hydrolysed collagen peptides per serve, the clinically trialled dose to support skin and nail health.
Collagen
Collagen is the body’s most abundant protein, representing approximately 30% of total body protein. Collagen is a major structural component of connective tissue that makes up skin, hair, nails, ligaments, tendons, cartilage, teeth and bone.
Collagen consists of amino acids comprised of three polypeptide chains that wrap tightly around each other to form a triple helix molecule resembling a rope-like shape. The rigid structure of collagen provides tensile strength and firmness to connective tissues around the body.
Approximately 28 types of collagen have been identified in the human body. Type I, II and III collagens are the most predominant types, each containing different proteins that serve specific roles and are distributed differently in the body:
Type I: most common type of collagen and mainly present in skin, bone, teeth, tendons, ligaments, vascular ligature and organs.
Type II: main structural component of cartilage tissue and provides flexibility and support to bone joints.
Type III: present in skin, muscle, vessels and reticular fibres of organ tissues such as the liver,
spleen and lungs.
Over 90% of collagen in the body is comprised of type I and III collagen produced by fibroblasts (cells in connective tissues) and osteoblasts (cells that make bones).
The amino acids crucial for collagen synthesis and production are:
Glycine: most abundant amino acid found in collagen and is synthesised by serine.
Proline: non-essential amino acid vital for collagen biosynthesis, strength and structure.
Lysine: essential amino acid involved in collagen formation.
Proline and lysine are converted into their active forms, hydroxyproline and hydroxylysine, respectively, via hydroxylation. Hydroxyproline and hydroxylysine are major components of cross linkages in collagen and play a key role in collagen stability.
Hydroxylation of proline and lysine is dependent upon adequate levels of vitamin C as a cofactor for collagen protein synthesis and repair.
Figure 1: Structure of collagen fibres
Collagen vs collagen peptides
Collagen in its natural state is referred to as native collagen. It is formed from three very long chains of over 1000 amino acids twisting into a helix conformation. In its full-length, unhydrolysed form, collagen is not an effective oral supplement as it is difficult to break down during digestion and too large to cross the intestinal wall.
Collagen peptides are short chain protein building blocks characterised by high levels of specific amino acids glycine, hydroxyproline, proline and alanine. This amino acid composition provides collagen peptides their unique bioactive properties not found with other protein sources.

subsections.heading: TECHNICAL INFORMATION
subsections.text:
Energy production
Naturally fermented
Maintains CoQ10 levels in the body
Soy-free formula
In rice bran oil
CoQ10 150mg contains Coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10) derived from natural fermentation by the bacteria Rhodobacter sphaeroides.
CoQ10 exists in two main forms (ubiquinone and ubiquinol), forming what is known as a redox reduction pair. This means they naturally cycle in the body from one form to the other as required by the
cell, so that both energy production and oxidative balance can be maintained.
CoQ10 150mg contains ubiquinone, the oxidised form of CoQ10. After absorption, the body converts ubiquinone into ubiquinol, the active antioxidant form. Studies over 3 decades have shown the ubiquinone supports health and general wellbeing.
While CoQ10 is manufactured in the body, the endogenous production of CoQ10 requires several vitamin coenzymes, including vitamins B2, B6, B12, C, folic acid, niacin and pantothenic acid.
CoQ10 150mg is manufactured in rice bran oil, a stable, soy-free base. Rice bran oil has a high content of tocotrienols (antioxidants in the vitamin E family), which provide greater stability from oxidation than soy oil.
CoQ10 150mg is best given with food. Ubiquinone is insoluble in water and difficult to absorb on an empty stomach. Absorption is at least twice as effective when taken with a meal1.
Antioxidant
CoQ10 is a lipid-soluble antioxidant that helps protect the body from oxidative damage. Specifically, CoQ10 protects cell membranes from oxidation, supporting cell membrane integrity and cell functioning.
As an antioxidant, CoQ10 has a sparing effect on vitamin E and helps recycle vitamin E from its oxidised form to its active (antioxidant) form.
CoQ10 increases the resistance of LDL cholesterol to oxidation. Supplementation with exogenous CoQ10 leads to an increase in the ubiquinol content of LDL cholesterol and a corresponding decrease of LDL peroxidability.
Energy production
CoQ10 supports healthy energy levels. It is an essential component of mitochondria and plays a critical role in energy production within cells.
CoQ10 is concentrated in tissues with high energy requirements, such as the heart and skeletal muscle. Physical activity increases the body’s demand for energy and, therefore, CoQ10 and reduces muscle tissue levels of CoQ10.
Physical exercise also induces muscle damage associated with a high production of free radicals and pro-inflammatory mediators. Oral supplementation of CoQ10 during exercise has been found to reduce oxidative stress, increase total antioxidant status and modulate inflammatory signalling, which reduces subsequent muscle damage2.
CoQ10 supplementation supports healthy exercise capacity. A randomised, double-blind, crossover study in healthy sedentary men found that supplementation with 100mg CoQ10 showed performance-enhancing effects during repeated bouts of supramaximal exercise3.
Cardiovascular & heart health
CoQ10 helps maintain a healthy cardiovascular system and supports heart health through antioxidant activity, inhibition of LDL cholesterol oxidation and by the maintenance of optimal mitochondrial function. The heart is one of the most metabolically active tissues in the body and, therefore, has a high requirement for CoQ10 to support energy production.
CoQ10 supports healthy endothelial function. The endothelium is the single cell layer of tissue that forms the lining of blood vessels, heart and lymphatic vessels. A 2012 meta-analysis showed that treatment with CoQ10 significantly improved endothelial function assessed peripherally by flow-mediated dilation (p<0.0001)4.
CoQ10 helps maintain healthy blood vessels by inhibiting the oxidation of LDL cholesterol.
Mild migraine
CoQ10 can help reduce the frequency of migraines and headaches as well as the associated nausea and vomiting when taken as a preventative.
Migraines are thought to result, in part, from mitochondrial dysfunction and supplementing with CoQ10 supports healthy mitochondrial function.
An open-labelled trial investigated the effects of oral CoQ10 supplementation (150mg/day) over 3 months in healthy volunteers with a history of episodic migraine. Of the 31 patients that completed the study, 61.3% had a greater than 50% reduction in the number of days with migraine headache and 93.5% of patients had at least a 25% reduction in the number of days with migraine5.
Sperm health
CoQ10 has been shown to improve sperm parameters, especially sperm motility.

Physical exercise also induces muscle damage associated with a high production of free radicals and pro-inflammatory mediators. Oral supplementation of CoQ10 during exercise has been found to reduce oxidative stress, increase total antioxidant status and modulate inflammatory signalling, which reduces subsequent muscle damage2.
CoQ10 supplementation supports healthy exercise capacity. A randomised, double-blind, crossover study in healthy sedentary men found that supplementation with 100mg CoQ10 showed performance-enhancing effects during repeated bouts of supramaximal exercise3.
Cardiovascular & heart health
CoQ10 helps maintain a healthy cardiovascular system and supports heart health through antioxidant activity, inhibition of LDL cholesterol oxidation and by the maintenance of optimal mitochondrial function. The heart is one of the most metabolically active tissues in the body and, therefore, has a high requirement for CoQ10 to support energy production.
CoQ10 supports healthy endothelial function. The endothelium is the single cell layer of tissue that forms the lining of blood vessels, heart and lymphatic vessels. A 2012 meta-analysis showed that treatment with CoQ10 significantly improved endothelial function assessed peripherally by flow-mediated dilation (p<0.0001)4.
CoQ10 helps maintain healthy blood vessels by inhibiting the oxidation of LDL cholesterol.
Mild migraine
CoQ10 can help reduce the frequency of migraines and headaches as well as the associated nausea and vomiting when taken as a preventative.
Migraines are thought to result, in part, from mitochondrial dysfunction and supplementing with CoQ10 supports healthy mitochondrial function.
An open-labelled trial investigated the effects of oral CoQ10 supplementation (150mg/day) over 3 months in healthy volunteers with a history of episodic migraine. Of the 31 patients that completed the study, 61.3% had a greater than 50% reduction in the number of days with migraine headache and 93.5% of patients had at least a 25% reduction in the number of days with migraine5.
Sperm health
CoQ10 has been shown to improve sperm parameters, especially sperm motility.

subsections.heading: TECHNICAL INFORMATION
subsections.text:
Antioxidant
Reduces the risk of cystitis
One-a-day
Vegan-friendly
Suitable for use during pregnancy
Cranberry is an antioxidant herb that supports urinary tract health and can help reduce the occurrence of medically diagnosed cystitis.
Cystitis is an inflammation of the bladder that almost always follows bacterial infection in the urine and is the most common type of urinary tract infection (UTI).
The most common symptoms of cystitis are frequent urge to urinate, burning or scalding sensation on urination, strong-smelling urine and pain in the lower abdomen. Escherichia coli (E. coli) is the most common bacterium responsible for UTIs.
UTIs are more common in women than in men, as the female urethra is only 4cm long, giving bacteria easy access to the bladder. Additionally, due to hormonal influences and changes in vaginal secretions, women are mores susceptible to infection during certain stages of the menstrual cycle, during pregnancy and during menopause.
Antioxidant
Cranberry and vitamin C are potent antioxidants that reduce free radicals formed in the body. Cranberry is also a rich source of vitamin C – it was used historically to treat scurvy due to its high vitamin C content. Vitamin C helps support healthy immune system function.
Urinary tract infections
Traditionally, Cranberry is used in Western herbal medicine to help reduce the occurrence of urinary tract infections. Native American Indians used Cranberry as both a food and a medicine for bladder and kidney problems. In the 1840s, German scientists made the connection between Cranberry and the incidence of urinary tract infections. Since then, there has been much research into Cranberry and its effects on urinary tract health.
Cranberry contains proanthocyanidins, which prevent the adherence of pathogenic bacteria, particularly E. coli, to the walls of the urinary tract. In vitro and animal studies demonstrate that Cranberry consumption inhibits the binding of bacterial strains to uroepithelial cells.
One in vitro study found that urine collected after Cranberry consumption prevented adhesion of 31 (80%) of the 39 isolates and 19 (79%) of the 24 antibiotic-resistant isolates in bioassays, while pre-consumption urine failed to prevent adhesion in any sample.
Anti-adhesion activity was seen within 2 hours and persisted for up to 10 hours following Cranberry ingestion1.
Several human clinical studies, conducted on a variety of Cranberry extracts, showed benefit in the prevention of recurrent UTIs. According to Natural Medicines, Cranberry decreases the overall risk of UTI by 33% - 38%2.
One study looked at 373 women with a history of recent UTI and the effect of 240mL Cranberry juice (equivalent to 65g Cranberry) on episodes of UTIs. During the study time, there were 39 episodes of UTI in the Cranberry group compared to 67 episodes in the placebo group (p=0.016). Cranberry also significantly reduced clinical UTI with pyuria (p=0.037)3.
Masking urinary odour
Cranberry is often used to mask urinary odour associated with incontinence. To-date, there are no studies available to support this use. However, numerous anecdotal reports suggest it can be useful when taken on a regular basis4.

subsections.text:
Caution with warfarin – possible interaction with Cranberry and vitamin C (conflicting reports). Monitor INR.
Caution with aluminium-containing compounds (e.g. phosphate binders) – vitamin C increases the amount of aluminium absorbed. Separate dose by at least 2 hours.

subsections.heading: CAUTIONS
subsections.text:
If symptoms of UTI become more severe while taking Cranberry, or if pain or irritation persists for more than 48 hours, medical advice is recommended. The presence of blood in the urine warrants immediate medical attention.
Use with caution in people with iron overload conditions, such as haemochromotosis, as vitamin C increases iron absorption.

Digest-Zymes contains a comprehensive blend of enzymes to support healthy digestive function and to aid in the digestion of fats, proteins and carbohydrates, including fibre and lactose.
Poor digestion is one of the most common health complaints today. Several factors can contribute to the development of digestive issues, including poor eating habits (eating on the run and inadequate chewing of food) and poor dietary choices, such as excessive consumption of alcohol, refined carbohydrates and fat, and a
diet low in raw foods. Raw foods contain enzymes which can help facilitate digestion.
Symptoms of poor digestion include indigestion and fullness lasting 2-4 hours after eating, bloating, excessive flatulence, abdominal cramps, alternating constipation and diarrhea, and undigested food in the stool.
Digestion
Digestion begins in the mouth where food is broken down by the salivary enzymes amylase and lingual lipase. The food (bolus) then travels down the esophagus into the stomach where gastric juices and enzymes are secreted to further breakdown macro and micronutrients.
Low stomach acid results in the pH of the stomach remaining unnaturally high, which predisposes the gram-positive flora to colonise and increases the susceptibility of the gastrointestinal tract to infection. A higher pH can impair the absorption of several vitamins and minerals, specifically, iron, vitamin B12, calcium, magnesium and zinc, which may increase the risk of deficiency.
The pancreas is comprised of an endocrine and exocrine portion. The exocrine tissue of the pancreas (the acini) produces digestive enzymes that are mixed with sodium bicarbonate and function to break down carbohydrate, proteins and fats. Problems occur
when there is a dysfunction in the ability of the pancreas to produce enzymes or the body’s demand for enzymes exceeds the supply.

Stress can have a big impact on digestion. Digestion is under the primary control of the vagal nerve and the parasympathetic nervous system and is therefore stimulated by a relaxed state. Conversely, stress causes activation of the sympathetic nervous system and can impair gastrointestinal motility and function.
Digestive enzymes
Digestive enzyme supplementation can aid in the breakdown of fats, proteins and carbohydrates and may provide benefit in disorders in which compromised digestion may be involved1.
As a large percentage of Australians have diets that are typically low in enzymes (due to a predominance of processed, refined foods), the importance of digestive enzyme supplementation is especially relevant.
Amylase is a carbohydrate-degrading enzyme that aids in the breakdown of polysaccharides, such as starch.
Protease enzymes are involved in the breakdown of proteins to oligopeptides and amino acids. Bromelains are proteolytic enzymes that aid in the digestion and assimilation of proteins. Bromelain is the general name for the family of sulfhydryl-containing, proteolytic
enzymes from the pineapple fruit and stem and has a wide pH range which allows them to be active in the stomach as well as the small intestine. The German Commission E approves the use of bromelain (combined with other digestive enzymes) for dyspepsia (indigestion)2.
Lipase is a lipid-degrading enzyme that assists in the digestion of dietary fats. Lipase hydrolyses triacylglycerols (the main lipid found in the diet) into diacylglycerols, monoacylglycerols, free fatty acids and glycerol.
Tilactase, more commonly known as lactase, is specific for digesting lactose, the primary disaccharide found in dairy products. It is involved in the breakdown of lactose to glucose and galactose.

Immune health
Relieves excess mucus
Relieves sore throat & fever

Traditional common cold support
Echinacea, commonly known as ‘purple coneflower’ is a perennial herb native to North America. It was first used by Native Americans as a remedy for snakebites and infections of the nose and throat.
Echinacea species contain water-soluble polysaccharides, alkamides, flavonoids and caffeic acid derivatives, including echinacoside
and chicoric acid. The concentration of these constituents can vary significantly depending on growing conditions, drying of the plant and the extraction process. The main active constituents are
considered to be the alkamides, which are responsible for the mouth-tingling effects of Echinacea.
Echinacea purpurea and Echinacea angustifolia contain structurally different types of alkamides.
The 2-ene alkamides present in Echinacea angustifolia protect the alkamides found in Echinacea purpurea that are rapidly broken down by the liver, leading to less degradation. A combination of both species provides a complex alkamide profile and results in greater bioavailability1.
Immune health
Echinacea 4000 Complex supports immune system function and immune health. It is traditionally used in Western herbal medicine (WHM) to support the immune system to fight illness.
Echinacea has immunomodulatory effects on the body and supports both innate and specific immunity. Administration of Echinacea enhances macrophages, phagocytosis and cytokine production in humans2.
Echinacea can stimulate specific immune responses including the activation of innate immune cells and increased levels and activity of T lymphocytes, neutrophils and natural killer (NK) cells. These effects may be due to the polysaccharides present in Echinacea3.
Recent experiments demonstrate that alkamides are detectable in human blood in relevant concentrations after oral administration of Echinacea preparations. Alkamides show structural similarity with anandamide, an endogenous ligand of cannabinoid receptors. It was found that alkamides bind significantly to CB2 receptors, which
is now considered as a possible mechanism of action of Echinacea alkamides as immunomodulatory agents4.
Echinacea angustifolia contains unique 2-ene alkamides. These are only found in Echinacea angustifolia and exhibit selective affinity to CB2 receptors found mostly in immune cells5.
Common cold
Echinacea purpurea and Echinacea angustifolia have been used traditionally in Native American medicine for centuries for respiratory tract infections and inflammatory conditions, including common cold, coughs, bronchitis and inflammation of the mouth and pharynx.
Echinacea is traditionally used in WHM to relieve the symptoms of common cold, sore throat and mild upper respiratory tract infections, including mild fever and excess mucous.
Echinacea angustifolia root is recommended as a supportive therapy for colds and upper respiratory tract infections by the German Commission E6.
Both the German Commission E and the World Health Organisation approve the use of Echinacea purpurea herb as supportive therapy for colds and infections of the respiratory tract7,8.
A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial involving 755 healthy subjects assessed the safety and efficacy of Echinacea on common cold episodes. Subjects received 2400mg/day of Echinacea purpurea whole plant extract or placebo over a 4-month period. A daily dose of 4000mg of Echinacea was also given during acute cold episodes. A reduction in total number of cold episodes, cumulated episode days and pain-killer medicated episodes was observed in the Echinacea group compared to the placebo group9.
A meta-analysis of 14 studies and 11 356 participants evaluated the effect of Echinacea extracts on common cold incidence and duration. Echinacea decreased the odds of developing the common cold by 58% and reduced the duration of a cold by 1-4 days. The studies used a dose ranging from 100mg to 2400mg/day. Published evidence supports the use of Echinacea for decreasing the incidence and duration of the common cold10.

Elderberry Echinacea & Olive Leaf is a delicious Blackcurrant flavoured liquid blend of herbs traditionally used in Western herbal medicine (WHM) to support immune system health and relieve mild fevers.
Elderberry and Echinacea are herbs traditionally used in WHM to relieve the symptoms of colds, flu and mild upper respiratory tract infections (URTIs).
For maximum benefit, start taking Elderberry Echinacea & Olive Leaf immediately at the onset of symptoms.
Colds, flu & upper respiratory tract infections
Elderberry and Echinacea have a long history of traditional use in WHM to relieve the symptoms of colds, flu and mild URTIs, including cough, sore throat and mild upper respiratory tract congestion.
Elderberry, Echinacea and Olive leaf have been used traditionally in WHM as antipyretics to relieve mild fevers. Their diaphoretic action induces sweating, acting to cool the body.
Immune health
Elderberry Echinacea and Olive Leaf supports immune health.
Echinacea maintains healthy immune function and supports the immune system to fight illness. The herb acts as a non-specific immunostimulant, acting on non-specific cellular immunity by stimulating phagocytosis and the release of cytokines and other serum factors.
Echinacea is traditionally used in WHM to support immune system health. Traditional texts refer to Echinacea’s antiseptic properties and its ability to “increase bodily resistance to infection”1.
Olive leaf is traditionally used in WHM to support immune system health and function. The primary constituent of Olive leaf is oleuropein, believed to be responsible for many of the therapeutic properties of the leaf. Olive leaf has been found to have antimicrobial properties against viruses, bacteria and yeasts in animal and
human studies. Olive leaf inhibits the assembly of viruses at the cell membrane, interfering with critical amino acid production, and stops viral shedding. Olive leaf can also inhibit bacteria, either by inactivating cellular enzymes critical for bacterial replication or via
attack on the cell membrane2.
Elderberry contains flavonoids, including quercetin and rutin, anthocyanins, cyanogenic glycosides, viburnic acid and vitamins A and C, which all contribute to its pharmacological activity. The
berries contain several anthocyanin flavonoids that have significant antioxidant activity and can regenerate alpha-tocopherol.
Elderberry’s immune benefits are mostly due to antiviral effects. Research has shown that Elderberry constituents neutralise the activity of haemagglutinin spikes found on the surface of viruses.
By deactivating these hemagglutinin spikes, the viruses are no longer able to pierce cell walls or enter the cell and replicate3.

Evening primrose oil (EPO) is extracted from the seeds of Evening primrose flowers. The seeds typically contain 14% fixed oil, which contains 65%-75% linoleic acid, 7%-10% gamma-linolenic acid (GLA) and smaller amounts of oleic, palmitic and stearic acids, campesterol and beta-sitosterol.
GLA is an omega-6 essential fatty acid. GLA is metabolised in the body to dihomo-gamma-linolenic acid (DGLA), a precursor of anti-inflammatory prostaglandin E1. Together GLA and DGLA improve the ratio of inflammatory and non-inflammatory prostaglandins and leukotrienes1.
GLA is produced in the body from linoleic acid. Preformed GLA is present in trace amounts in green leafy vegetables and nuts. EPO is a rich source of GLA.
Figure 1: Structure of GLA
Skin health
EPO supports healthy skin.
Omega-6 fatty acids are involved in maintaining the integrity of the water-impermeable barrier of the skin. EPO supports skin hydration and relieves skin dryness.
A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled study in healthy adults tested the effects of 1500mg EPO twice daily (equivalent to 3 Evening Primrose Oil Daily capsules) on skin variables. After 12 weeks, skin moisture, transepidermal water loss, elasticity, firmness, fatigue resistance and roughness significantly improved by 12.9%, 7.7%, 4.7%,
16.7%, 14.2% and 21.7%, respectively2.
A study in 21 individuals with atopic dermatitis investigated the effects of 4-6g of EPO daily (equivalent to 4-6 Evening Primrose Oil Daily
capsules) for 12 weeks. At the end of the study, there was a significant increase in plasma GLA and a significant inverse correlation between the changes in plasma GLA levels and SCORAD (p=0.008). SCORAD is a clinical tool used to objectively assess the extent and severity
of eczema. The mean total SCORAD reduced after 4 weeks (p = 0.019) and 12 weeks (p = 0.001). Specifically, EPO supplementation decreased the intensity of skin dryness from 1.8 at baseline to 1 at the last visit (p=0.003)3.
The World Health Organisation monograph on EPO states that EPO can be taken internally for symptomatic treatment of atopic eczema4.
A 2022 randomised double-blind trial evaluated the effects isotretinoin (Accutane) or isotretinoin combined with 2g of EPO per day (equivalent to 2 Evening Primrose Oil Daily capsules) in patients with acne vulgaris on skin hydration status (CORN), transepidermal water loss (TEWL) and skin oiliness (sebum) for 9 months. At the
end of the study, the isotretinoin-treated group showed statistically significantly reductions in CORN. However, in the group treated with isotretinoin and EPO, TEWL and sebum levels decreased significantly (p<0.05), while CORN levels increased from 42.0 ± 9.70 to 50.9 ± 10.4
(p = 0.017)5.

Fish Oil 1000 contains 1g of fish oil per capsule, derived from small, cold-water fish sourced from sustainable fisheries. The oil undergoes purification processes and stringent purity testing to ensure it surpasses Australian standards for heavy metals, including mercury.
Fish Oil 1000 provides fish oil in an 18:12 ratio, providing 180mg of EPA and 120mg of DHA essential fatty acids per capsule.
Fish Oil 1000 helps prevent a dietary omega-3 deficiency.
Omega-3 fatty acids
Omega-3 fatty acids are long-chain polyunsaturated essential fatty acids (EFA) that are necessary for good health and development. They are essential because the body cannot produce them, so adequate amounts must be consumed from the diet.
Satisfying omega-3 requirements through diet alone is difficult due to the increasing presence of heavy metals, polychlorinated biphenyls and other environmental toxins present in fish. Therefore,
taking a concentrated fish oil supplement that is tested for purity and freshness can be a good way to supplement omega-3s in the diet.
EPA and DHA have an anti-inflammatory action and help reduce inflammation in the body. The typical Western diet provides an overabundance of omega-6 fatty acids, which can favour an inflammatory response. Thus, higher amounts of omega-3 fatty acids in the diet or through supplementation are recommended.
Cardiovascular health
Omega-3 fatty acids support healthy cardiovascular system function and heart health. DHA is the principal fatty acid incorporated into myocardial membrane phospholipids.
Omega-3 fatty acids exert their benefit on the cardiovascular system via a number of different mechanisms, including improved myocardial oxygen efficiency and heart rate, modulation of myocardial sodium and potassium ion channel function and improved endothelial function. Studies have demonstrated that fish oils improve endothelial relaxation by enhancing vasodilation1.
Omega-3 fatty acids also inhibit platelet aggregation. EPA is the precursor to the series 3 prostaglandins (PGE3) that reduce platelet stickiness. EPA is metabolised in leukocytes to leukotriene B5, which reduces platelet adhesion, and in endothelial cells to produce prostacyclin I3, which relaxes blood vessels and reduces platelet
aggregation.
The Australian Heart Foundation recommends that adults consume about 500mg of marine-sourced omega-3 oil per day by eating 2-3 serves of oily fish a week or by taking fish oil supplements to lower their risk of coronary heart disease2.
Brain & eye health
Omega-3 fatty acids support brain function, cognitive health and memory.
Fatty acids are found in high concentrations in neuronal membranes and in the myelin sheath and play a role in neuronal membrane fluidity and function. Higher plasma omega-3 PUFA has been associated with a lower risk of age-related cognitive decline.
DHA is the major component of phospholipids in the brain and contributes to the maintenance of normal brain function.
A placebo-controlled, cross-over study evaluating the effects of five weeks omega-3 supplementation (3g/day) on cognitive
performance in 40 healthy, middle aged to elderly individuals found that supplementation improved cognitive performance, specifically resulting in better performance in the working memory test (p<0.05)3.
A study of 20 to 34-year-olds found that EPA-rich supplementation enhanced neurocognitive function and suggested that the brain worked less hard yet had better cognitive performance4.
A systematic review and meta-analysis in healthy adults aged 18 and older found that episodic memory improved with DHA and EPA supplementation. The study found that >1g/day DHA/EPA improved
episodic memory, regardless of cognitive status at baseline (p<0.04)5.
Omega-3 fatty acids support eye health, particularly retina health. DHA is the major component of phospholipids in the retina and contributes to the maintenance of normal vision.

Omega-3 fatty acids support joint health and help relieve symptoms of mild arthritis.

Folic Acid Complex contains high-strength folic acid, together with vitamins B6, B12 and iodine.
Folic acid is essential for the formation of thymidylate synthase, an enzyme required for DNA and RNA formation and cell replication and division. It is essential during foetal development and helps produce key chemicals for the brain and nervous system1.
Vitamin B12 is an important co-factor for folic acid metabolism. Both nutrients need to be present for chemical reactions to occur within the one-carbon metabolic pathway. This pathway is vital for the synthesis of DNA, RNA, neurotransmitters, membrane phospholipids, myelin and proper functioning of the central nervous system. If vitamin B12 is not present, folic acid cannot function properly regardless of sufficient intake.
Methylcobalamin is the metabolically active form of vitamin B12 that is readily used in the body. Alternative forms of vitamin B12, such as cyanocobalamin, require an additional step to achieve conversion to methylcobalamin in the body.
Vegans and strict vegetarians are at risk of vitamin B12 deficiency as they do not consume any animal products, the main dietary source of vitamin B12.
Healthy foetal development & healthy pregnancy
Folic Acid Complex contains folic acid and iodine to support healthy foetal development and a healthy pregnancy.
Adequate folic acid consumption for three months prior to conception and for the first three months of pregnancy greatly reduces the risk of serious birth defects, including spina bifida/neural tube defects.
Clinical practice guidelines recommend that women capable of becoming pregnant take a minimum of 400 micrograms of folic acid from fortified foods or supplements to prevent neural tube defects
in infants. This recommendation is based on research showing that a higher intake of folic acid from food and supplements during pregnancy reduces the primary incidence of neural tube defects by between 41% to 69%2.
Iodine sufficiency during pregnancy is critical to proper foetal development. Iodine is a component of thyroid hormones triiodothyronine (T3) and thyroxine (T4), hormones that influence growth and development. Iodine comprises 65% of the weight of T4 and 59% of the weight of T33. has been demonstrated between dietary intake of vitamin B12 and normal neurological and psychological functions4.
Nervous system health
Folic Acid Complex contains iodine and vitamins B6 and B12 for nervous system health.
Iodine is an essential trace element required to produce thyroid hormones and for the proper functioning of the thyroid gland. Thyroid hormones have a direct relationship with many metabolic processes, including the growth and development of the central nervous system (CNS).
Vitamin B6 is important for healthy nervous system function. It is involved in the synthesis of several neurotransmitters, including GABA, serotonin, norepinephrine and dopamine.
Vitamin B12 is essential for the preservation of the myelin sheath around neurons and for the synthesis of neurotransmitters.
Cardiovascular system health
Folic Acid Complex contains folic acid and vitamins B6 and B12 for cardiovascular system health.
One of the most important folate-dependent reactions in the body is the conversion of homocysteine to methionine. Elevated
homocysteine has been associated with an increased risk of adverse cardiovascular outcomes.

subsections.heading: DRUG INTERACTIONS
subsections.text:
Several medications may deplete folate status, including antacids (PPIs), trimethoprim (antibiotic), pyrimethamine (antimalarial), triamterene (blood pressure), sulfasalazine (for ulcerative colitis) and oral contraceptives. Separate dose by 2-3 hours.
Caution with methotrexate (folic acid antagonist) – co-administration with folate may reduce the effects. Patients should take folate only under the supervision of a health professional.
Caution with antiepileptic medications – folic acid may reduce serum levels of these medications. Patients should take folate only under the supervision of a health professional.
Caution with anticonvulsant medications (phenobarbital/ phenobarbitone and phenytoin) – folic acid and vitamin B6 may reduce serum levels of these medications. Patients should take this combination only under the supervision of a health professional.
Caution with cholestyramine and colestipol (hypolipidaemic agents)
- drugs may decrease the absorption of folate. Separate dose by at least 4-6 hours.
Caution with levodopa – coadministration with B6 alone should be avoided as B6 reduces drug effects. However, this effect is
prevented by the administration of a dopa-decarboxylase inhibitor (e.g. benserazide, carbidopa) with levodopa, as is common clinical practice.
Caution with drugs containing iodine, e.g. amiodarone (antineoplastic agent) – concurrent use with iodine can increase iodine levels and may affect thyroid function. Monitor thyroid function.

subsections.heading: TECHNICAL INFORMATION
subsections.text:
Memory
Healthy blood circulation
Maintains capillary health
Brain health
Cardiovascular health
Antioxidant & free radical scavenger
Sustainably sourced extract
Supports blood flow to peripheral areas of the body (legs, hands & feet)
The Ginkgo biloba tree is believed to be the world’s oldest living tree, dating back more than 250 million years. The tree is now cultivated in Asia, Europe, North America, New Zealand and Argentina. The medicinal use of Ginkgo can be traced back to 2800 BC in Chinese
medicine, where it was used for brain disorders, circulatory disorders, respiratory conditions, urinary tract conditions and as an antiparasitic.
Ginkgo contains more than 30 genuine flavonoids, of which the flavanol glycosides, found in the leaves, are the most abundant.
Ginkgo Biloba 6000 contains Ginkgo extract standardised to 28.8mg of Ginkgo flavonglycosides per capsule. Flavonglycosides have antioxidant activity and reduce free radicals formed in the body.
Cognitive function & memory
Ginkgo Biloba 6000 supports cognitive function, brain health and memory.
The brain requires large amounts of energy to function properly in the form of glucose and oxygen. Decreased or impaired circulation impacts both membrane function and energy production. By maintaining blood flow to the brain, Ginkgo enhances oxygen utilisation and improves cellular uptake of glucose, thereby restoring energy production in the brain.
Ginkgo helps to increase nerve cell transmission rate, improve synthesis and turnover of brain neurotransmitters and helps to normalise acetylcholine receptors in the hippocampus, an area of the brain involved in emotions, feelings and memory processing.
Cerebral vascular insufficiency is particularly common in the elderly due to changes within the artery walls. This can lead to impaired mental performance, such as mood disturbance, short term memory loss and decreased alertness. Ginkgo increases blood flow to the brain to help maintain cognitive function and memory during ageing.
Blood circulation
Ginkgo Biloba 6000 supports healthy blood circulation, including to the peripheral areas of the body (legs, hands and feet) and maintains blood capillary health.
Ginkgo has numerous effects on the vascular system, mainly in the vascular endothelium (lining of blood vessels) and modifies blood vessel tone. Ginkgo has a vasodilatory effect that helps to normalise circulation while inhibiting relaxation of the blood vessels.
Insufficient peripheral circulation usually occurs from obstruction or narrowing of the peripheral arteries and leads to decreased blood flow during exercise or rest. This causes ischemia (decreased oxygenated blood) to the peripheral parts of the body causing pain and dysfunction.
Ischemia can lead to the development of peripheral vascular difficulties, characterised by cold hands and feet, and intermittent claudication which causes cramp-like pain in the calf muscles.
Ginkgo inhibits platelet aggregation and adhesion of red blood cells. Platelet activating factor (PAF) is a potent inflammatory mediator and can initiate increased vascular permeability, smooth muscle contractions and decreased coronary blood flow. Ginkgo competes with PAF for binding onto PAF receptor sites and therefore inhibits PAF related events.
A meta-analysis of 5 placebo-controlled clinical trials of Ginkgo extract in patients with peripheral arterial conditions concluded that Ginkgo exerted a highly significant therapeutic effect1. Another 2 studies showed an increase in walking distance in patients with intermittent claudication after 6 months2, and an improvement of pain at rest in patients given 200mg of Ginkgo extract for 8 weeks3.
Cardiovascular health
Ginkgo Biloba 6000 supports cardiovascular system health.
Through its role as a vasodilator, Ginkgo improves blood flow through the arteries, veins and capillaries, increasing blood flow to these areas.
Ginkgo exerts its cardioprotective activity through its antioxidant, antiplatelet, antithrombotic and vasodilatory properties.
Ginkgo extract
Globally, 25 million Ginkgo trees are harvested each year to meet the demands for Ginkgo as a medicinal product. The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) lists Ginkgo as “endangered” due to the rapid decline in the number of trees around the world4.
Herbs of Gold Ginkgo Biloba 6000 uses Ginkgo extract that is 100% from sustainably sourced, plantation grown Ginkgo in order to meet the requirements of protecting endangered species.
The Ginkgo extract is prepared using an ethanol/water extraction process, undergoing filtration steps in order to create a high-strength, standardised herbal extract without the use of excipients
(see figure 1).

Synergistic blend of 5 herbs
Ginseng 4 Energy Gold contains a synergistic blend of four different ginsengs used in traditional Western and Ayurvedic medicine to support energy production and relieve weariness, fatigue and feelings of debility.
Ginseng 4 Energy Gold contains herbs known as adaptogens. Adaptogens are believed to increase resistance to emotional, chemical and physical trauma, as well as relieve weakness, mental exhaustion and fatigue. Adaptogens have been shown to improve mental and physical performance and reduce the harmful effects of stress.
Ginseng 4 Energy Gold is standardised to ginsenosides. Ginsenosides are the pharmacologically active constituents found in the Panax family. Ginsenosides form part of the defence mechanism of the plant and have antimicrobial, antifungal, anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties.
Ginsenosides are classified into 2 main categories: protopanaxadiol, including Rb1, Rb2, Rb3, Rc, Rd, Rg3, Rh2, Rs1, and protopanaxatriol, including Re, Rf, Rg1, Rg2 and Rh1. The ‘R’ stands for the root and the next letter denotes its chromatographic polarity. Ginseng 4 Energy Gold contains the seven well-recognised ginsenosides standards used to characterise ginseng: Rb1, Rb2, Rc, Rd, Re, Rf and Rg1. American ginseng has the highest content of ginsenosides of all of the ginseng species1.
Energy production & the stress response
Ginseng 4 Energy Gold contains four ginsengs plus Astragalus to support energy production.
Korean ginseng is traditionally used in Western herbal medicine to help enhance physical capacity and performance, especially in cases of physical stress. It is also used as an adaptogen to help increase energy and resistance to stress.
The Commission E has approved Korean ginseng and Siberian ginseng as tonics for invigoration and fortification in times of fatigue and debility or declining capacity for work and concentration2,3.
The activity of Korean ginseng appears to be based on whole body effects, rather than particular organs or systems, which lends support to the traditional view that Ginseng is a tonic that can revitalise the functioning of the body as a whole.
Siberian ginseng has been used for over 2000 years in China as a folk
remedy and as a tonic to restore vigour, improve general health and increase stamina.
American ginseng is traditionally used in Chinese medicine to support a healthy stress response in the body. After the USA won independence from Great Britain in 1783, the first USA-China trade ship carried 30 tons of American ginseng to China to kick-start their economy. The Chinese viewed the American ginseng as being complementary to their own native ginseng. Siberian ginseng is considered warm and ideal for people who have recovered from
illness and need to regain their strength; on the other hand, American ginseng has cooler properties and is normally used to cool down mild fevers or summer heat. Chinese medicine considers it good for people with deficient yin or excessive yang.
Ashwagandha is often referred to as ‘Indian ginseng’ because it is used in much the same way in Ayurvedic medicine as Korean
ginseng in traditional Chinese medicine, although it is considered less stimulating. Ashwagandha is a gentle adaptogen, traditionally used for improving stress adaptation responses in people who are both physically and emotionally stressed and exhausted. Ashwagandha improves the response to stress, possibly via an action on the adrenal glands, and possesses anti-inflammatory and sedative properties. Ashwagandha is used to assist with nervous exhaustion, convalescence and debility.
Both Astragalus and Korean ginseng are the principal herbs for strengthening Qi, the body’s vital force, and have been used for over 2000 years in traditional Chinese medicine to support stamina and endurance and to relieve fatigue.
Immune system health
Ginseng 4 Energy supports healthy immune system function, especially during times of stress.
Siberian ginseng, American ginseng and Astragalus have a long history of use in Western herbal medicine to aid during convalescence and as prophylactics to build resistance and reduce susceptibility to illness while promoting health.
Korean ginseng has been extensively reported to maintain homeostasis of the immune system and to enhance resistance to illness or microbial attacks through the regulation of immune system4.
