GlucoPlex contains the herbs Gymnema, Fenugreek and Cinnamon, and nutrients to help support healthy blood sugar.
GlucoPlex contains nutrients that assist carbohydrate and sugar metabolism, including alpha Lipoic acid (ALA) and chromium, which are necessary for the cellular uptake of glucose.
GlucoPlex contains antioxidant nutrients, ALA, chromium and zinc, that help reduce free radicals formed in the body. Antioxidants help offset the oxidative effects of high sugar.
Glucoplex contains nutrients that support insulin production and activity. Insulin is a hormone produced by beta-cells in the pancreas. It is released into the blood stream after a meal, where it transports glucose from the blood stream into the cells for use as energy.
Gymnema
Gymnema is a herb native to India and Sri Lanka that has a long history of use in Ayurvedic medicine.
Gymnema has wide-ranging actions on glucose metabolism. Primarily, it reduces glucose absorption in the blood and stimulates insulin secretion through increased pancreatic beta-cell numbers and improved cell function. In rabbits, Gymnema has also demonstrated improvements in glycogen synthesis, glycolysis, gluconeogenesis and hepatic and muscle glucose uptake1.
Gymnema contains triterpene saponins, known as Gymnemic acids, and Gymnema saponins, which are believed to be responsible for the herb’s pharmacological activity. GlucoPlex contains Gymnema leaf standardised to contain 25mg of Gymnemic acids.
A small study in 10 healthy young adults found that 2g Gymnema three times a day significantly reduced fasting blood sugar levels compared with baseline2.
Gymnema also has unusual activity where it supresses the perception of the sweet taste on the tongue. Because of this action, it is known
as gurmar (sugar destroyer) in Hindi. Gymnemic acids have an atomical arrangement similar in structure to sugar molecules that fill the receptors in the taste buds. Ingestion of Gymnemic acids fills the receptors in the taste buds, preventing their activation by the sugar
molecule in food. Similarly, in the intestine, Gymnemic acids attach to the receptor present in the intestine, preventing the absorption of sugar molecules into the intestines3.
Cinnamon
Cinnamon increases the uptake of glucose into cells by enhancing insulin receptor phosphorylation and translocation of the glucose transporter GLUT4 to the plasma membrane. It increases the number of GLUT4 receptors and insulin receptors, facilitating glucose entry into cells.
In a double-blind study, 79 patients with poor sugar control were randomly assigned to 1g Cinnamon or placebo three times a day for 4 months. Cinnamon significantly reduced plasma glucose by 10.3%4.
In another study, the addition of 1, 3 or 6g of Cinnamon to the diet significantly decreased serum glucose levels (18-29%) after 40 days. No significant changes were noted in the placebo groups5.
Fenugreek
Fenugreek has been used medicinally for thousands of years in Asia and the Mediterranean.
Fenugreek enhances glucose uptake into cells and the utilisation of glucose as energy. It contains 4-hydroxyisoleucine, an amino acid which increases pancreatic insulin secretion and inhibits sucrose
α-D-glucosidase and α-amylase6. This effect is glucose-dependent and only occurs in the presence of moderate to high glucose concentrations7.
A 6-week, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel trial investigated the effect of Fenugreek seed extract on eating behaviours in 39 healthy overweight males. Fenugreek consumption significantly decreased insulin/glucose ratio relative to placebo (p=0.044)8.
Another double-blind, placebo-controlled study found that 1g/day of Fenugreek seed significantly decreased area under curve (AUC) of blood glucose and insulin (p<0.001)9. Fenugreek increased insulin sensitivity and improved glycaemic control.

Caution with monoamine oxidase inhibitor (MAOIs) antidepressant medications – concurrent use with Ginsengs can interfere with drug effects. Use under supervision of a health professional.

Caution with immunosuppressant medication - concurrent use with Ginsengs and Ashwagandha may reduce their effectiveness.
Caution with antidiabetic medications - Korean ginseng may have additive hypoglycaemic effects. Separate dose by 2-3 hours and monitor blood sugar levels.
Caution with blood thinners/anticoagulants and antiplatelet medications – herbs may increase risk of bleeding. Monitor.

Caution with sedatives - concurrent use with Ginsengs and Ashwagandha may reduce their effectiveness.
Caution with hormone replacement therapy (HRT) - Korean ginseng may have additive oestrogenic effects and may interfere with HRT treatment.
Caution with thyroid medications - Ashwagandha may increase thyroxine concentrations. Monitor thyroid levels.
Caution with loop diuretics - Korean ginseng may reduce their effectiveness.

subsections.heading: DRUG INTERACTIONS
subsections.text:
Caution with hypoglycaemic medications and insulin – GlucoPlex may have additive effects. Monitor.
Caution with warfarin – ALA has reduced platelet reactivity in vitro, uncertain whether the effect is clinically significant.
Caution with anticoagulant/antiplatelet drugs – Fenugreek may have additive effects, increasing the risk of bruising and bleeding.
Caution with thyroxine – ALA may suppress the conversion of thyroxine to active T3 form and chromium can reduce thyroxine absorption. Separate dose by 3 hours.
Caution with calcium channel blockers – vitamin D may reduce the effectiveness of these drugs.
Caution with digoxin – vitamin D can elevate serum calcium levels, which increases the risk of cardiac arrhythmias with digoxin. Monitor calcium levels.
Caution with thiazide diuretics – when taken in conjunction with vitamin D, can increase the risk of hypercalcaemia. Monitor serum calcium levels during concurrent use.
Caution with cholestyramine or colestipol (lipid-lowering medication) and orlistat – these drugs may reduce the absorption of fat-soluble vitamins, including vitamin D. Take one hour before, or 4-6 hours after drug.
Caution with NSAIDs, cefalexin, penicillamine and tetracycline and quinolone antibiotics - zinc forms complexes with these drugs, interfering with absorption. Separate dose by 3 hours.
Caution with iron supplements – Fenugreek and zinc can interfere with iron absorption. Separate dose by 2 hours.
Caution with copper and manganese supplementation – ALA can bind to minerals. Separate dose by 3 hours.

Glucosamine 1500mg/day
Supports joint health
Anti-inflammatory
Glucosamine MAX contains a clinically trialled dose of glucosamine hydrochloride as well as chondroitin, MSM, silica, zinc, manganese, glycine and proline that are required for the formation of
healthy cartilage. It provides high-strength Ginger to help relieve inflammation.
Glucosamine is a component of glycosaminoglycans and proteoglycans of the cartilage matrix and is required for the production of proteoglycans, mucopolysaccharides and hyaluronic acid. These substances form joint tissue, such as articular cartilage, tendons and synovial fluid.
Exogenous glucosamine exists in two forms - glucosamine hydrochloride (HCl) and glucosamine sulfate. Glucosamine sulfate requires compound stabilisers in the form of salts and has 74% purity. Glucosamine HCl lacks the sulfate group and has 99% purity, providing a higher percentage of glucosamine compared to sulfate forms1.
Chondroitin belongs to a class of polymers known as glucosaminoglycans and act as the flexible connecting matrix between cartilage and connective tissue.
Methylsulfonylmethane (MSM) is a naturally occurring source of sulfur. Sulfur is a component of many tissues in the body and plays a role in the development and maintenance of connective tissue.
Joints
A joint is an articulation where two bones meet that allows for mobility. Joints are complex structures comprised of bone, muscles, synovium, cartilage and ligaments designed to bear weight and facilitate movement.
Joints are cushioned by cartilage and lubricated with synovial fluid to allow movement and twisting freely without pain. The principal lubricating substances in cartilage, tendons, ligaments, synovial fluid
and mucous membranes are proteoglycans and glycosaminoglycans (GAGs).
Cartilage is a type of tissue that covers the surface of a bone at a joint and helps reduce friction of movement within a joint. The synovial membrane lines the joint and seals the joint capsule by secreting synovial fluid, a clear, sticky substance that lubricates the joint.
Ligaments connect bones together and are composed of tough connective tissue surrounding the joint to provide support and limit the joint’s movement. Tendons are another type of connective tissue and connect muscle to bones.
Figure 1: Knee joint
Joint health
Glucosamine MAX helps support joint cartilage health and maintains joint health.
Glucosamine is required for the synthesis of glycoproteins, glycolipids and GAGs and stimulates metabolism of chondrocytes in the articular cartilage and synovial cells in the synovial tissues.
Chondroitin is endogenously found in cartilaginous tissues and serves as a substrate for the formation of the joint matrix structure. It can protect cartilage by inhibiting elastase and hyaluronidase enzymes that damage joint cartilage.
MSM is an organic form of sulfur that, together with glucosamine,
is required for the production of important structural components of joint cartilage by cross-linkages through disulphide bonds. GAGs, the fundamental building blocks of joint cartilage, are linked together by disulfide bonds, making cartilage firm and resilient.
Glycine and proline are amino acids required for the biosynthesis of collagen and elastin, important for healthy cartilage production and joint health. Proline is a major amino acid found in cartilage.
Silica is necessary for the normal growth and development of connective tissue and is abundant in bones, hair, skin and nails. Silica is required for the cross-linking of collagen strands, important for
the strength and integrity of the connective tissue matrix. Collagen is the most abundant protein found in the body and is responsible for maintaining the integrity of tendons, ligaments and cartilage.
Fox, B. A., & Stephens, M. M. (2007). Glucosamine hydrochloride for the treatment of osteoarthritis symptoms. Clinical Interventions in Aging, 2(4), 599–604.

Gout Relief Complex contains the propriety ingredient Ayuric® from the herb Terminalia bellirica.
Ayuric® is combined with the traditional herbs Celery and Alfalfa as well as nutrients to help maintain healthy uric acid levels in the body.
Celery has been traditionally used in Western herbal medicine (WHM) to relieve symptoms of occasional episodes of gout while also helping to promote urine output.
Gout Relief Complex can be taken daily to help maintain healthy uric acid levels and reduce the risk of a gout attack, or during an acute gout attack to help provide symptomatic relief.
Terminalia and Celery are both antioxidants, helping to help reduce free radicals in the body.
Gout
Gout is a type of arthritis caused by too much uric acid in the blood stream. Uric acid is a normal waste product in the body formed when the body breaks down purines from foods. Normally, uric acid dissolves in the blood and is eliminated via the kidneys in urine.
However, in individuals with gout, uric acid is not eliminated efficiently and can build up in the bloodstream (hyperuricaemia), forming urate crystals, which lodge in a joint.
Gout most often affects the big toe, but can occur in the feet, ankles, knees, wrists and fingers.
Symptoms of gout include intense joint pain, swelling and red and shiny skin over the joint.
While other types of arthritis develop slowly, an attack of gout happens suddenly, often overnight.
Gout affects far more men than women and may have a genetic component.
Dietary modification is important for people who suffer from gout as several foods can trigger an attack. Foods high in purines, such as red meats, yeast, poultry, organ meats, fish and shellfish and alcohol should be avoided. Spinach, asparagus, beans, lentils and mushrooms also contain moderate amounts of purines. A well-balanced diet rich in fruits, vegetables, wholegrains, low-fat dairy and adequate water intake is beneficial.
Ayuric®
Ayuric® is proprietary ingredient derived from the edible fruits of
Terminalia bellirica, an ancient Ayurvedic plant.
Ayuric® is both antioxidant and anti-inflammatory, while also having been clinically studied to lower uric acid levels in individuals with hyperuricemia. Ayuric® is postulated to work by inhibiting xanthine oxidase (XO), the enzyme responsible for synthesising uric acid in the body.
In a study, 110 eligible subjects with hyperuricemia were randomised to receive either 250mg or 500mg of Ayuric® twice daily for a duration of 24 weeks. Serum uric acid levels were measured at baseline and at the end of 4, 8, 12, 16, 20 and 24 weeks. Both active treatment groups showed a reduction in serum uric acid levels compared to baseline1.
In a further study, 59 subjects were randomised to receive either 500mg or 1000mg of Ayuric® twice-daily. Biomarkers of oxidative-stress, endothelial function, systemic inflammation, and platelet-aggregation were evaluated at baseline, 4, 8, 12 and 24 weeks. Significant improvements in oxidative stress biomarkers and systemic inflammation biomarkers were observed in both groups. The study also demonstrated both doses significantly decreased serum uric acid levels and creatinine levels, while improving glomerular filtration rate over a 24-week period2.
Celery & Alfalfa
Celery is traditionally used in WHM to relieve the symptoms of gout and help reduce the occurrence of gout attacks.
Celery is also used in traditional WHM as a diuretic to enhance urine output, and can therefore assist in the clearance of uric acid from the body.
Celery contains phthalide derivatives, tannins and phenolic compounds that contribute to its uricosuric action (increased excretion of uric acid in the urine).
Apigenin, a flavonoid found in celery, has hyperuricemic and XO inhibitory activity with reports it can interact with the XO active site and is comparable to allopurinol in vitro3.
Alfalfa is traditionally used in WHM as an anti-arthritic and diuretic to relieve fluid retention. It increases urine production, provides nutritional support and has a general tonic effect.

Nutritional antioxidant support
Grape Seed Gold is a high potency antioxidant complex containing a unique blend of herbal and nutritional antioxidants to reduce free radical production in the body and support general health and wellbeing.
Oxidation is a chemical reaction that can produce free radicals in the body. These free radicals can start a chain reaction that potentially leads to damage within DNA, proteins and lipids in cell membranes.
Free radicals are unstable, electrically charged molecules that gain stability by stealing electrons from other molecules, such as proteins, DNA and cell membranes through the oxidation process. When oxidation occurs, important components of cells become damaged and lose their ability to function normally. Oxidative damage can eventually lead to cell death and is considered to play a role in many health conditions and the acceleration of the ageing process.
Oxidation is a natural reaction within the body, but increased oxidation can be caused by several internal or external factors, including stress, environmental chemicals, cigarette smoking, alcohol, poor diet, sunlight, pollution and excessive exercise.
Antioxidants can be found in the form of nutrients from fruits and vegetables, as well as phytochemicals found in plants, particularly seeds and bark, where they help to combat free radical damage by donating one of their electrons to a free radical molecule to inhibit the oxidation process and prevent cell damage.
Grape Seed Gold supports healthy eyesight and vision and helps maintain healthy immune system function.
Grape seed quality
Grape Seed Gold contains a non-GMO Grape seed extract sourced exclusively from the Champagne region of France, well-known for its premium quality wine. Due to the high prevalence of adulterated Grape seed extracts, this extract has been validated and verified for its identity, authenticity and quality.
The Champagne grapes are cultivated and seasonally harvested in the summer and autumn months, and then either sun or air dried after harvesting. The seeds then undergo extraction, using only water and alcohol without using any harsh solvents or excipients.
Quality control process involve microbial testing and testing for environmental contaminants including pesticides and heavy metals.
Grape seed is a rich source of proanthocyanidins (PACs) also referred to as procyanidins. Proanthocyanidins are mixtures of oligomeric (2-8 molecules) or polymeric (>9 molecules) flavonoids. Oligomeric procyanidins (OPCs) are made up of dimers and trimers of (+)-catechin or (-)- epicatechin.
Specific testing methods have been developed to determine the levels of oligomeric proanthocyanidins (OPCs). Herbs of Gold utilises HPLC analytical to test for total monomers, dimers, trimers, oligomers, oligomeric procyanidins and proanthocyanidins.
Grape Seed Gold contains high-strength Grape seed and is standardised to contain 237.5mg of procyanidins per tablet.
Antioxidant
Grape Seed Gold is an antioxidant that helps reduce free radicals formed in the body.
Grape seed is a potent antioxidant. It contains the flavonoids oligomeric proanthocyanidins (OPCs), made up of polyphenol compounds catechins, epicatechin and epicatechin-3-0-gallate. OPCs from Grape seed have potent antioxidant activity, countering the negative effects of free radical damage in the body1.
Grape seed has demonstrated potent antioxidant activity in both in vitro and in vivo studies, showing significantly greater antioxidant effects than certain nutrients and demonstrating a sparing effect on vitamin E2.
Grape Seed Gold contains clinically tested Setria® glutathione (GSH), an antioxidant that is present in high concentrations in almost all cells of the body3. GSH is a protein molecule comprised of cysteine, glutamate and glycine and plays a critical role in detoxification, antioxidant protection and immune cell function.
GSH is known as the ‘master’ antioxidant as it not only protects against free radical damage, but also helps regenerate oxidised antioxidant vitamins C and E by reinstating them back to their active form to continue their antioxidant activity. GSH is important for DNA protection and cell protection in the skin, lens, cornea and retina against oxidation and radiation damage.
GSH supports both phase I and phase II liver detoxification. GSH neutralises free radicals produced by detoxification of various toxins via the phase I pathway and transforms them into smaller metabolites ready to enter the phase II pathway. In phase II, GSH

Gut Care helps maintain a healthy digestive system. It contains anti-inflammatory and demulcent herbs that relieve irritation and inflammation and promote healing in the gastrointestinal tract.
Intestinal barrier integrity
The intestinal mucosal barrier is a single layer of cells lining the gut that mainly consists of the enterocyte membranes and tight
junctions between the enterocytes. The intestinal epithelium acts as a selective barrier, allowing essential dietary nutrients, electrolytes and water from the intestinal lumen into circulation while preventing the passage of unwanted substances, such as food antigens, endotoxins and harmful microorganisms.
Loss of intestinal barrier integrity is associated with food allergies, inflammation of the bowel and irritable bowel syndrome. Stress, pathogenic organisms and infections can all weaken intestinal integrity.
Healthy intestinal barrier integrity is essential for both digestive health and immune health.
L-Glutamine
L-Glutamine is the naturally occurring form of the amino acid glutamine. Glutamine is a conditionally essential amino acid. Usually, human cells can readily synthesise the amino acid, however, under certain physiological conditions, the body’s tissues need more glutamine than can be supplied by the diet and biosynthesis and supplementation becomes necessary. Catabolic stress can deplete cellular glutamine by more than 50 percent.
L-Glutamine supports digestive health and immune health.
It is an important fuel source for the rapidly dividing cells of the gastrointestinal system and the immune system, particularly lymphocytes and monocytes. The gastrointestinal tract is the greatest user of glutamine in the body as glutamine is the principle metabolic fuel of enterocytes.
Glutamine is essential for maintaining intestinal barrier function and immune responses. In vitro and in vivo research shows that glutamine aids in the proliferation and repair of intestinal cells and is, therefore, essential for maintaining the integrity of the intestinal lining and preventing the translocation of microbes and endotoxins into
the body1. Animal studies have shown that glutamine can decrease intestinal permeability and help heal damage to the gut wall2.
Glutamine supports intestinal barrier function by regulating tight junction protein expression and intestinal immunity.
Glutamine is also involved in the synthesis of glutathione, an important antioxidant and hepatic detoxifier.
DGL Licorice
Licorice has a long history, over 3000 years, of medicinal use. In Roman times, Marcellus Empiricus (5th century AD) suggested the use of Licorice to treat many disturbances or pathologies of the stomach and intestine and indigestion3. Licorice is a demulcent to soothe gastrointestinal tract mucous membranes.
Licorice also has anti-inflammatory and mucoprotective activity. It helps protect the gastrointestinal tract by stimulating the secretion of mucin, the protective substance that lines the stomach and intestines.
Gut Care contains deglycyrrhizinated Licorice (DGL), which contains less than 3.5% glycyrrhizin. Glycyrrhizin is the active constituent that is responsible for the majority of the side effects associated with Licorice root. DGL can be consumed long-term without the side-effects associated with glycyrrhizin.
Aloe vera, Calendula & Slippery elm
Aloe vera and Slippery elm are demulcent herbs that soothe irritation and inflammation of the gastrointestinal tract. Gut Care contains Aloe vera leaf inner juice which is the clear gel or mucilage produced by the inner parenchymal cells in the central part of the Aloe vera leaf. It does not contain any latex, which contains anthraquinones and has stimulant laxative activity.
Slippery elm bark contains mucilage, which coats the surface of mucous membranes and forms a protective gel-like layer that soothes irritated and inflamed tissues. It is traditionally used to relieve gastrointestinal tract inflammation and irritation.
Calendula is traditionally used as an anti-inflammatory to help relieve inflammation of the gastrointestinal tract.
Aloe vera and Calendula are traditionally used as vulnerary herbs to help heal the upper gastrointestinal tract.

subsections.heading: DRUG INTERACTIONS
subsections.text:
Theoretically, Slippery elm may slow the absorption and reduce serum levels of orally administered drugs due to its mucilage content.
Clinical significance is unclear. Caution is warranted with drugs with a narrow therapeutic range (e.g. barbiturates, digoxin, lithium, phenytoin, warfarin). Separate dose by 2 hours.
Caution with warfarin and digoxin – Licorice may affect drug metabolism.
Caution with glucose lowering medications (including metformin) – Aloe vera given in conjunction with glucose-lowering medication may have additive effects. Potentially beneficial interaction.
Caution with thiazide diuretics, cardiac glycosides, corticosteroids (e.g. prednisolone) and stimulant laxatives - Licorice may potentiate hypokalaemia. However, the DGL form is considered safer and less likely to result in drug interactions.
Caution with cyclosporin - Licorice may reduce blood concentrations and quercetin may decrease oral bioavailability. Monitor cyclosporin levels closely.
Caution with NSAIDs, cefalexin, penicillamine and tetracycline and quinolone antibiotics – zinc forms chelates with the drugs, reducing absorption. Separate the dose by 3 hours.

Hawthorn is one of the oldest known medicinal plants used in traditional herbal medicine for its beneficial effects on the
cardiovascular system which are well supported both traditionally and scientifically.
The berries, leaves and flowers of Hawthorn are phytochemically similar, but differ in the ratio of specific flavonoids and oligomeric procyanidins (OPCs) present. The chemical constituents considered to be the primary bioactive components of hawthorn are the flavonoids and OPCs. They are potent antioxidant compounds responsible
for many of Hawthorn’s cardiovascular benefits. Hawthorn flowers contain the highest amount of flavonoids, while the leaves contain the highest amounts of OPCs.
Healthy blood circulation
Hawthorn 4500 supports blood vessel health and healthy blood circulation. The flavonoids present in Hawthorn assist in strengthening connective tissue and decreasing tissue fragility. Hawthorn
can increase membrane permeability for calcium and inhibits phosphodiesterase inhibition, which increases intracellular cAMP. Increased cAMP leads to increased coronary blood flow, vasodilation and induces endothelium-dependent arterial relaxation.
Hawthorn extracts have been shown to enhance release of nitric oxide (NO) from vascular endothelium causing vasodilation, which appears to be associated with the OPC-rich fraction of hawthorn extract3.
Hawthorn 4500 combines the flower, leaf and berry plant parts from
Crataegus monogyna (Hawthorn) and is standardised to contain 57mg of procyanidins per tablet.
Cardiovascular system
The cardiovascular system comprises three essential components: the heart, the blood and blood vessels consisting of veins, arteries and capillaries. It functions to transport nutrients, oxygen and hormones to cells throughout the body and remove metabolic waste.
Cardiovascular health
Hawthorn 4500 contains Crataegus monogyna (Hawthorn) which has been traditionally used in Western herbal medicine as a cardiotonic to support cardiovascular system health and heart health. Cardiotonics help protect the cardiac tissue from oxygen deficiency and improve the tone, vigour and strength of the cardiac muscle.
Hawthorn 4500 supports cardiovascular system health and maintains heart health. Hawthorn acts on the myocardium by increasing force of contraction and lengthening the refractory period and increases coronary blood flow and cardiac output.
The positive inotropic effect of Hawthorn and its constituents have been demonstrated both in vitro and in vivo1. Positive inotropes help the heart pump more blood with fewer heartbeats. Although the heart beats less, it also beats with more force to meet the oxygen demands of the body. These effects are generally attributed to the flavonoid and procyanidin constituents of the leaves with flowers.
Hawthorn 4500 reduces free radicals formed in the body due to its antioxidant properties. Hawthorn has direct and indirect antioxidant activity that play a role in its cardioprotective effects. It has the potential to prevent increased lipid peroxidation and increase antioxidant enzymes in the heart2. Much of Hawthorn's cardiovascular activity is attributed to its flavonoid constituents.

Caution with nitrates, calcium channel blockers and beta-blockers
- Hawthorn has vasodilatory effects and may theoretically have an additive effect. Use under medical supervision.
Caution with blood pressure lowering drugs such as viagra, cialis and levitra - Hawthorn may have an additive effect with these medications. Monitor blood pressure.

Contraindicated during pregnancy.
Hawthorn may inhibit platelet aggregation and increase the risk of postoperative bleeding. Discontinue use 2 weeks prior to surgery.

Hayfever & Sinus Ease contains Eyebright, traditionally used in Western herbal medicine (WHM) to relieve symptoms of hayfever and sinusitis. Hayfever & Sinus Ease also contains Horseradish, Garlic, Baical skullcap and vitamin C. Horseradish and Garlic have a long history of use in WHM to clear respiratory tract mucus, while Baical skullcap is used in traditional Chinese medicine to clear respiratory tract mucus.
Hayfever & Sinus Ease contains 250mg of vitamin C to support overall immune system health and reduce free radicals formed in the body.
Hayfever & Sinus Ease is recommended three times a day to provide ongoing relief from respiratory allergies but can also be taken as needed for acute allergies.
Hayfever & sinusitis
Hayfever is a commonly used term for allergic rhinitis, which is simply an allergy that affects the eyes and nose. Sinusitis occurs because of inflammation or swelling of the passages within the nose, that can also frequently be caused by allergies.
According to Allergy & Anaphylaxis Australian, 20% of Australian adults suffer from hayfever1. Hayfever occurs when the body’s natural immune defence mechanism overreacts to normal everyday substances such as pollens, grasses, dust mites, animal dander, foods or mold, identifying them as allergens. As a result of this exposure, the immune system becomes hypersensitive, triggering IgE (immunoglobulins) antibodies that secrete excessive amounts of white blood cells (basophils and mast cells), which enter the blood stream as a form of defence.
IgE antibodies bind to the mast cells which contain histamine, and as the mast cells are stimulated by the allergen, large amounts of histamine and other inflammatory mediators are released into the
blood stream producing an allergic reaction cascade with symptoms such as itching, swelling, inflammation and excessive mucus production2. Dampening the effects of histamine during an allergic reaction helps to relieve these symptoms.
Hayfever, or allergic rhinitis, is a common condition with symptoms similar to the common cold, such as sneezing, congestion, runny nose, itchy throat as well as a dry or wet, irritating cough.
Allergies are chronic in nature and may be seasonal or perennial. Seasonal allergies peak during spring and summer when pollen levels are high, whereas perennial allergies occur all year long and
may be attributed to animal dander, mold, dust mites and other allergens. Respiratory allergies tend to manifest as hayfever (allergic rhinitis) and sinusitis with nasal congestion, itchy, watery eyes and sneezing. The main objectives to reduce the duration and symptoms associated with allergies is to reduce inflammation, balance histamine levels, break down and reduce mucus congestion (allowing for better airflow) and to decrease the risk of secondary infection
as mucus congestion provides an ideal environment for secondary infections to develop.
Coughs are the result of irritation in the lining of the oesophagus. A persistent cough can be one of the most irritating symptoms of hayfever. Allergic coughs can be either dry or wet in nature. Dry coughs are caused by pollen irritating the back of the throat or air
passages, triggering the natural body reaction of coughing to clear the irritant, where as wet coughs are triggered by postnasal drip, where an allergen irritates the nasal passage and excessive fluid is produced by the inflamed membranes, resulting in increased mucus.
Hayfever & sinusitis relief
Hayfever & Sinus Ease contains Eyebright, traditionally used in WHM to relieve symptoms of hayfever and sinusitis, including reducing bronchial mucus congestion and cough.
Eyebright and Garlic are traditionally used in WHM to relieve cough. Garlic is used traditionally to enhance cough productivity.
Baical skullcap is a well-known anti-allergy herb which contains numerous flavonoids, in particular baicalin and wogonoside, that also provide anti-inflammatory activity. These flavonoids inhibit IgE antibody mediated allergic reactions by reducing the production of pro-inflammatory prostaglandins and leukotrienes, release of
histamine from basophils and mast cells, and binding of allergens to IgE3.
Vitamin C has antihistamine activity that is beneficial in allergic responses. An inverse relationship has been found between vitamin C and blood histamine levels. Increasing vitamin C status (250mg/d) over 3 weeks decreased histamine levels4.

Hormone Metabolism supports liver health and assists natural liver cleansing and detoxification processes.
Hormone Metabolism supports oestrogen metabolism in the liver. It contains herbs and nutrients that support phase I and phase II liver detoxification to support hepatic oestrogen metabolism and healthy oestrogen pathways.
Hormone Metabolism is an antioxidant and helps protect from free radical damage.
Oestrogen
Oestrogen is a sex hormone with many roles in the body. It is important for cardiovascular and bone health and for the
maintenance of healthy skin and blood vessels. In women, oestrogen is responsible for the development of secondary sex characteristics, the female pattern of body fat around the abdomen, hips and breast and the appearance of axillary and pubic hair. In men, oestrogen is essential for the regulation of testosterone and reproductive function, including sperm health. Having too much or too little oestrogen can cause a range of health problems in both males and females.
Oestrogen is an umbrella-term for three endogenous oestrogens: oestradiol (E2), oestrone (E1) and oestriol (E3). Oestradiol (secreted from the ovaries/testes) is the most biologically potent oestrogen. In contrast, oestrone (synthesised by the ovaries and peripheral tissue) and oestriol (produced by the metabolism of oestradiol and oestrone in extra-ovarian tissue) are only weakly oestrogenic.
Oestrogen levels are controlled by tightly coordinated feedback loops. In women, follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) stimulates the follicle to produce oestrogen; a rise in oestrogen shuts off the production of FSH and a fall turns it back on again. Androgens,
hormones produced by the testes, ovaries and adrenal cortex, can be converted to oestrogens via the activity of aromatase enzymes.
Oestrogen acts on tissues by binding to oestrogen receptors, found particularly in the brain, heart, breast, bone and genital tract. One of the main functions of oestrogen is to stimulate cellular proliferation in cells with oestrogen receptors. Additionally, the presence of oestrogen increases the number of oestrogen receptors on each cell. Therefore, in an oestrogen-rich environment, there are many more cells produced and they also contain more oestrogen receptors, which leads to an escalating ability for oestrogen to stimulate cell growth. Oestrogens circulate in the body bound to sex hormone binding globulin (SHBG), however, only unbound oestrogens can bind to oestrogen receptors and exert a biological effect.
Xeno-oestrogens
In addition to endogenous oestrogens (produced in the body), humans are also exposed to exogenous oestrogens in the form of phyto-oestrogens and environmental xeno-oestrogens.
Phyto-oestrogens are derived from plants and weakly mimic the activity of oestrogen in the body, with potential health benefits. Xeno-oestrogens, on the other hand, strongly mimic the activity of oestrogen in the body and are detrimental to health. Xeno-oestrogens are often referred to as ‘endocrine disrupters’ and are stored in fat cells. Exposure to environmental oestrogens begins in utero and they persist in the body for decades, with their levels continuing to accumulate over time.
Sources of exogenous oestrogens include oral contraceptives and hormone replacement therapy and environmental toxins found in pesticides, herbicides, refrigerants, industrial solvents and plastics that are structurally similar to oestrogen. One of the main sources of exogenous oestrogen is from bisphenol A (BPA), which is a chemical used in the lining of some food and beverage packaging. Small amounts of BPA can migrate from containers into food and drink. Exogenous oestrogens also include hormones used to fatten livestock and promote milk production that enter the body via the food chain.
Liver detoxification
The main route of oestrogen metabolism and elimination is via the liver, so healthy liver function is essential for the detoxification and clearance of oestrogen from the body. Liver herbs, such as St Mary’s thistle and Rosemary, may help the breakdown of excess oestrogen.
Phase I detoxification utilises cytochrome P450 enzymes and involves oxidation, reduction, hydrolysis, hydration or dehalogenation reactions. Toxins are either neutralised and excreted or transformed into intermediary metabolites that enter phase II. Phase II detoxification involves conjugation reactions (including glutathione conjugation, glycine conjugation, methylation, sulphation, glucuronidation and acetylation) to make toxic compounds water-soluble and ready for excretion in the urine or bile.
Antioxidants are an essential part of detoxification as they support phase II detoxification and reduce exposure to reactive intermediates produced during phase I.
Poor liver function and inadequate oestrogen excretion may result in excess circulating oestrogens.

subsections.text:
Nervous system health
T3 & T4 production
Healthy pregnancy	✓ Foetal & infant neurodevelopment
Iodine is an essential trace element that is required for healthy thyroid function and for normal growth and development. It also has antioxidant effects, with the ability to donate an electron to decrease damage due to oxygen free radicals.
The major food sources of iodine are of marine origin, including kelp and seafood, and fortified salt. Dietary and supplemental iodine is well absorbed, with about 90% of ingested iodine absorbed. Iodine can also be absorbed through the skin. Deficiency occurs when not enough iodine is consumed in the diet.
In Australia, many people do not consume adequate iodine. The iodine content of most foods is low, and can be affected by soil levels, irrigation and fertilisers.
Two public health measures were introduced in Australia between 2009 and 2010 to reduce iodine deficiency. Food Standards Australia and New Zealand (FSANZ) introduced mandatory fortification of iodised salt used in breadmaking and the National Health and Medical Research Council (NHMRC) released a public statement in 2010 recommending that all women who are pregnant, breastfeeding or considering pregnancy, supplement with 150 micrograms iodine daily1.
Thyroid health
Iodine supports thyroid gland health and assists thyroid hormone production. It is essential for the production of the thyroid hormones thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3), which influence growth, tissue metabolism and thermogenesis. The thyroid gland stores 80% of the body’s iodine pool and iodine comprises 65% of T4 and 59% of T3. Thyroid hormones are involved in carbohydrate and fat metabolism, in protein synthesis and regulating basal metabolic rate.
Thyroid function is regulated by thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), secreted by the pituitary gland. TSH secretion increases uptake of iodine in the thyroid and stimulates the synthesis and release of T3 and T4. Where there is insufficient iodine, TSH levels remain elevated, which can eventually lead to enlargement of the thyroid gland, known as a goitre, and symptoms of hypothyroidism.
Symptoms of hypothyroidism include:
Weakness, tiredness and sleepiness
Dry skin
Cold intolerance
Hair loss
Poor memory and concentration
Constipation
Reduced appetite and weight gain
Due to its role in thyroid hormone production, iodine supports nervous system health and is essential for the proper functioning of the brain and the entire nervous system.
Goitrogens
Goitrogens are substances that interfere with iodine utilisation, uptake into the thyroid or thyroid hormone production.
Goitrogens are present in raw cruciferous vegetables including cabbage, kale, cauliflower, broccoli, turnips and Brussels sprouts, and in linseed, cassava, millet and soy. Cooking these foods deactivates the goitrogens. Certain chemicals from industry or cosmetics can also be classed as goitrogens.
Iodine supplementation should be separated from goitrogens in order to maximise absorption. Soy, in particular, can inhibit iodine absorption and high levels of soy isoflavones, genistein and daidzein, can inhibit T3 and T4 production.
Pregnancy
Iodine is an essential nutrient during pregnancy. Adequate maternal iodine is essential for the development of the foetal brain and nervous system, as it is necessary for the growth of nerve cells, formation of synapses and myelination.
During early pregnancy, the foetal thyroid gland development is incomplete, so the foetus is entirely dependent on maternal T4, and therefore on maternal iodine intake. Thyroid hormone production increases by 50% during early pregnancy and renal excretion of iodine increases by 30-50%. In later pregnancy, iodine passes the placenta for foetal thyroid hormone production. The foetal thyroid gland develops by 10-12 weeks of gestation and is capable of thyroid hormone production by approximately 16-20 weeks2.
Dietary iodine requirements increase by approximately 50% during pregnancy, driven by increased thyroid synthetic demand,
increased renal iodine clearance and transfer of iodine to the foetus. National Health and Medical Research Council (NHMRC) guidelines recommend that the daily intake of iodine increase from 150 micrograms/day to 220 micrograms/day during pregnancy3.
In Australia, it is recommended that pregnant women take an iodine supplement of 150 micrograms/day to reduce risks to the foetus associated with iodine deficiency4. In individuals with low iodine status, periconceptional supplementation of 150-290 micrograms/ day is recommended5.
After birth, babies who are breast-fed will exclusively get their iodine from mother’s milk. Thus, it is essential that breastfeeding women maintain adequate iodine levels to support their health and that of their baby’s. Higher iodine levels are required during lactation, with recommendations between 250 and 290 micrograms/day6.
It is recommended iodine supplementation start before conception and to continue throughout pregnancy and breastfeeding in order to maintain adequate iodine levels.

subsections.text:
Liver Care contains four liver herbs plus nutrients to support healthy liver function and assist the breakdown of dietary fats.
Liver Care contains St Mary’s thistle and Curcumin, potent antioxidants to reduce free radical damage in the body.
Liver & gallbladder
The liver is the largest internal organ of the human body, weighing
1.5Kg in the average adult. Situated on the upper right side of the abdomen just below the diaphragm, it is protected by the rib cage. It has two sections, the right and the left lobe, separated by the falciform ligament.
The liver has several important functions in the body. It has a key role in detoxification, breaking down chemicals, metabolising drugs and removing toxins from the body. It also filters the blood from the
digestive system, processes nutrients from the diet and helps regulate body metabolism. It converts carbohydrates into glucose for use
as an energy source, and converts glucose into glycogen, to store energy. The liver produces bile, which is stored in the gall bladder, to break down dietary fats and assist in the absorption of fat-soluble vitamins, including vitamins A, D, E and K.
The gallbladder is a small sac that sits under the liver and stores the bile produced by the liver. It extracts water from its store of bile, concentrating the liquid. The presence of fatty foods triggers the gallbladder to release bile into the intestine to help digest the fat.
Poor diet, especially a high fat diet, and excess alcohol or medication use can affect the biliary system. Some common symptoms of poor liver function include nausea, especially after a high fat meal, fatigue, pale stools, itchy skin and jaundice.
Liver function
Liver Care contains four herbs plus nutrients to support healthy liver function and maintain liver health.
St Mary’s thistle is traditionally used in Western herbal medicine (WHM) to support healthy liver function and to protect the liver. Eclectic physicians in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries used St Mary’s thistle for “congestion of the liver, spleen and kidneys”1.
It is believed that St Mary’s thistle’s hepatoprotective effect is achieved, at least in part, via its antioxidant mechanisms.
Silymarin, the herbs main active constituent, has shown direct antioxidant activity via redox reactions and indirect antioxidant activity by inhibiting the activity of free radical producing enzymes
and upregulating endogenous antioxidant enzymes, including glutathione.
Dandelion is traditionally used in WHM to support healthy liver function and detoxification. It is said Dandelion was used for liver complaints based largely on the doctrine of signatures, because the bright yellow flowers are the colour of a bilious hue2.
Schisandra is a hepatoprotective herb which supports healthy liver function and liver detoxification processes. It induces phase I enzymes, but is also a powerful inducer of phase II detoxification processes, helping to rapidly clear potentially toxic metabolites generated by phase I.
Bupleurum is traditionally used in Chinese medicine to maintain liver health, as a hepatoprotectant and to soothe liver Qi. It is considered to dissolve liver congestion and disperse liver Qi stagnation.
Curcumin has been shown to induce phase II liver detoxification enzymes, including glutathione peroxidase, glutathione reductase, glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase and catalase.
Taurine is essential for bile acid function and absorption of lipids. Taurine is preferentially conjugated with bile acids in the liver, which supports the emulsification of dietary fat.
Choline and inositol are both components of cell membrane phospholipids and contribute to cell structure and integrity. Choline supports healthy liver function and is essential for lipid and cholesterol transport, while inositol is involved in the transport of fat out of the liver.
Gallbladder health
Liver Care supports gallbladder health and healthy bile flow.
Dandelion is traditionally considered to be both a cholagogue and choleretic, increasing bile production and flow.
Dandelion roots are also traditionally considered to be a depurative and alterative, with blood cleansing activity, indicated for chronic skin problems.
Digestive health
Liver Care contains herbs that support healthy digestion and have been used traditionally to relieve dyspeptic complaints, such as loss of appetite, poor digestion and upper gastrointestinal discomfort. Specifically, St Mary’s thistle is traditionally used in WHM to relieve symptoms of dyspepsia, including digestive discomfort, flatulence, bloating and loss of appetite. subsections.heading: DRUG INTERACTIONS
subsections.text:
Caution with any medication, as Liver Care can improve liver function, and therefore may affect how drugs are metabolised. As a general rule, take 2 hours apart from other medications.
Contraindicated with morphine – St Mary’s thistle may affect serum levels of morphine and increase or decrease its effect.
Contraindicated with sirolimus (immunosuppressant) – Schisandra increases drug concentrations in the blood, increasing the risk of adverse events.
Caution with hypoglycaemic medications – St Mary’s thistle may have additive effects. Monitor, dose adjustments may be necessary.
Caution with warfarin and other anticoagulant/ antiplatelet drugs – St Mary’s thistle may affect drug metabolism. Monitor.

Herbs & nutrients
Lung tonic
Lung Care contains the herbs Licorice, Elecampane and Adhatoda plus antioxidant nutrients to support lung health and healthy immune system function.
Anti-catarrhal herbs reduce the formation of mucus and expectorant herbs facilitate the removal of mucus and other materials from the lungs, bronchi and trachea. Traditionally, there was a strong focus
on encouraging elimination to support respiratory system health. It was believed that clearing excess mucus and catarrh would enable optimal respiratory health.
Lung health
The lungs are two cone-shaped organs that sit in the thoracic cavity and facilitate breathing. In the lungs, small air sacs, called alveoli, are covered in capillaries and allow the exchange of gasses (oxygen and carbon dioxide) between the air and the blood. The average adult lung has approximately 700 million alveoli, with a total surface area of 50-80 square metres (about the size of a tennis court) which allows rapid and efficient gas exchange. Optimal lung function is important as it allows the body to obtain the oxygen needed to meet its cellular demands for nutrients and to remove metabolic waste products.
The lungs are continually exposed to inhaled airborne irritants and environmental pollutants, such as cigarette smoke, ozone and pollution, which generate excess reactive oxygen species and are, therefore, vulnerable to the damaging effects of oxidants. To counteract this oxidative threat, the lungs are well-endowed with antioxidant defenses. The respiratory tract lining fluid acts as an
interface between the environment, toxic exposure and respiratory tract epithelial cells, and contains high concentrations of antioxidants, including vitamin C, vitamin E and the selenium-dependent enzyme systems, glutathione peroxidase1.
Inhaled air is full of particles and microorganisms that have potentially damaging effects. Mucus in the airways functions to trap particles from the air, which are then swept upwards towards the pharynx by cilia on the cells lining the trachea, bronchi and bronchioles.
Adhatoda
Adhatoda is traditionally used in Ayurvedic medicine as an expectorant, to clear respiratory tract mucus, and antispasmodic for respiratory complaints. It is also used in traditional Ayurvedic medicine to relieve coughs and mild fevers. It is known as having kāsaśvāsahara (alleviates breathing difficulties) and
udarapraśamana (anti-allergenic) actions and is indicated for clearing inflammatory pitta heat and liquefying congestive kapha, for use when there is inflammation from an allergic response to clear the lungs and nostrils.
Adhatoda is one of the best-known herbal bronchodilators and respiratory spasmolytics, to help facilitate breathing and relieve chest tightness, breathlessness, non-productive cough and wheezing.
The major active constituent in Adhatoda is the alkaloid vasicine. The drug, bromhexine (Bisolvon) was derived from vasicine and is used as an experctorant to aid the thinning and loosening of mucus.
Licorice
Licorice is traditionally used in Western herbal medicine (WHM) as a demulcent to soothe irritated tissues of the respiratory tract. It acts upon mucous surfaces, lessening irritation, and is useful in dry or catarrhal coughs with inflammation of the lungs and bronchi.
Licorice is traditionally used in WHM as an expectorant to clear mucus from the chest and respiratory tract. It is considered a relaxing expectorant as it reduces excess mucus by relaxing spasms to promote natural expectoration. The Commission E approves the use of Licorice root for catarrh of the upper respiratory tract2.
Licorice is traditionally used in WHM to relieve coughs and bronchial catarrh. Culpeper, a renowned 17th century herbalist, said of Licorice: “for those who have a dry cough or hoarseness, wheezing or shortness of breath, and for all the pains of the breast and lungs…”3. It is also used in traditional Chinese medicine to relieve coughs.
Elecampane
Elecampane is traditionally used in WHM as an expectorant, to help clear respiratory tract mucus. It is considered to be a stimulating expectorant, or ‘reflex expectorant’, that provokes increased mucociliary activity by reflex stimulation of the upper digestive wall.
Elecampane is traditionally used in WHM to relieve coughs. It has been used historically to assist expectoration, reduce respiratory catarrh and relieve respiratory difficulties, such as shortness of breath and wheezing.
Elecampane is traditionally used in WHM as a lung tonic and to support lung health. It is considered one of the best medicines for pulmonary complaints and its tonifying properties help strengthen the lungs and sustain the strength of the patient with respiratory ailments. Reduces the occurrence of facial cold sores
Relieves the symptoms of cold sores
Lysine is an essential amino acid involved in making proteins in the body and assisting with the metabolism of carbohydrates and fatty acids. Lysine is also an important amino acid required for the biosynthesis of collagen, elastin and carnitine.
The human body cannot synthesise lysine, so it must be taken through the diet. The richest sources of lysine are animal proteins, such as meat and poultry, and to a lesser extent, eggs, beans and dairy products.
Cold sores
Cold sores are painful fluid-filled lesions on or near the lips that are caused by the herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV1). This virus is part of the same family of viruses that causes chickenpox and mononucleosis (Epstein-Barr virus).
Cold sore infection is easily transmitted. The virus usually enters a person's body through a break in the skin inside or around the
mouth, thus it is often acquired through contact with saliva. Once a person is infected, the virus lays dormant in the nerve cells that supply sensation to the skin.
Following a ‘trigger’ event the virus becomes active, and travels through the nerve endings toward the skin’s surface of the lips where it multiplies, causing an outbreak. Whilst the mechanism by which the herpes virus becomes reactivated is currently unknown, cold sore triggers can include exposure to sunlight and wind (especially on
the lips), stress and fatigue, infections such as a cold or flu, as well as menstruation and pregnancy.
Lysine for cold sore occurrence & symptoms
Several double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomised controlled trials have demonstrated oral lysine supplementation decreases the frequency of HSV1 outbreaks.
Most clinical research on lysine was conducted in the 1980s. However, more recent studies continue to support the original findings.
In a small 2008 study, 12 subjects were administered 500mg of lysine daily and monitored monthly over an 8-year period. All participants recorded a reduction in the number of occurrences of lesions as well as the healing time of each lesion1.
A larger, epidemiological study done in 1983 involving 1543 subjects found that 79% of those surveyed described their symptoms as severe or intolerable without lysine. Without lysine, 90% indicated that healing took place in 6-15 days, but with lysine 83% stated the lesions healed in 5 days or less2.
Lysine works by having an inhibitory effect on the multiplication of the HSV1. It acts as an antimetabolite by competing with arginine for inclusion in the viral replicative process. Lysine then exerts its effect by retarding the viral growth-promoting action of arginine.
Lysine demonstrates greater effectiveness when used in divided doses and taken with a meal containing protein.
Collagen health
Lysine supports collagen formation and health.
Collagen is the protein that forms connective fibres in tissues such as skin, ligaments, cartilage, bones and teeth. As an amino acid, lysine combines with proline and vitamin C to form procollagen. Procollagen is then used to manufacture the four main types of collagen found in different tissues throughout the body.
Calcium absorption
Lysine supports calcium absorption.
In one study, women were given 3g of calcium (as calcium chloride) and either 400mg of lysine or placebo. Both groups demonstrated increased serum calcium levels and increased urinary excretion of calcium, however, the amount of calcium excreted in the lysine group was significantly less than the placebo group, suggesting lysine may suppress calcium excretion in healthy individuals3.
In a further study of 45 women with osteoporosis the addition of 800mg of lysine to calcium supplementation significantly increased calcium absorption4.
Immune health
Olive leaf is traditionally used in Western herbal medicine to support immune system health and function.
The primary constituent of Olive leaf is oleuropein, believed to be responsible for many of the therapeutic properties of the leaf. Olive leaf inhibits the assembly of viruses at the cell membrane, interfering with critical amino acid production, and stops viral shedding. Olive leaf can also inhibit bacteria, either by inactivating cellular enzymes critical for bacterial replication or via attack on the cell membrane5.

Supports healthy vision
Helps temporarily relieve light sensitivity
Assists eye adaptation to variations in light intensity
Macu-Guard contains Bilberry standardised to anthocyanosides and antioxidant nutrients including lutein and zeaxanthin to support eye health and healthy vision.
Eye anatomy
The eyes are complex structures made up of the cornea, iris, pupil, lens, retina, macula and the optic nerve that allow vision.
The lens sits just behind the iris and pupil and helps to focus light on the back of the eye.
The retina is the sensory portion of the eye and contains layers of photoreceptors and nerves. Rods are a particular type of photoreceptor, located near the edges of the retina, which are
responsible for peripheral and night vision. Cones are photoreceptors that are more central in the retina and are responsible for day and colour vision. Together, rods and cones allow people to see in varying light conditions and different colours.
Rod photoreceptors, which contain the visual pigment rhodopsin, lose colour when light strikes them. Pigment regeneration is important to help protect the delicate photoreceptors and maintain vision.
The macula (‘yellow spot’) is a small area within the retina that is responsible for central vision and visual acuity.
Bilberry
Bilberry has a long history of use as a food and medicine for supporting eye health all over the world.
The active constituents in Bilberry are anthocyanosides - strong antioxidant compounds that have an affinity for the retinal pigmented epithelium. Bilberry anthocyanosides reinforce the collagen structures of the retina and help protect the eyes from free radical damage. Macu-Guard contains Bilberry, standardised to 25mg anthocyanosides.
Bilberry has vasoprotective properties and supports microcirculation to the eye.
Bilberry enhances regeneration of rhodopsin in the retina, which is essential for optimal functioning of the rods, light adaptation and night vision1.
Antioxidant nutrients
Macu-Guard contains key antioxidant nutrients to protect the eyes from oxidative/free radical damage and maintain eye health.
Vitamin C, the body’s primary water-soluble antioxidant, is found in high concentrations in the eye and maintains clarity of the lens and health of the retina. Vitamin C appears to protect the lens of the eye from free radical damage, directly, due to its antioxidant activity, and indirectly, via its ability to recycle vitamin E.
Vitamin E is an important lipid-soluble antioxidant and ample vitamin E may decrease oxidative damage to the lens of the eye.
Zinc and copper are essential trace metals that are concentrated in the photoreceptors and the retinal pigment epithelium of the eye. Both zinc and copper are cofactors in a number of ocular enzymes, including copper-zinc superoxide dismutase, which functions as an antioxidant by catalysing the conversion of free radicals to hydrogen peroxide.
Long-term, high doses of zinc can reduce the bioavailability of copper. It is recommended that copper intake should also be increased with zinc supplementation. Macu-Guard contains 1mg of copper to maintain copper balance.
A 2017 systematic review found that a higher intake of antioxidants (vitamin C, vitamin E, zinc, lutein and anthocyanins) in the diet was associated with longer-term eye health2.
Lutein & zeaxanthin
Lutein and zeaxanthin are yellow-coloured, xanthophyll carotenoids that are not converted into vitamin A in the body. They are found in high quantities in the retina and macula of the eye and in the lens. Lutein is more prominent at the edges of the retina and in the rods, while zeaxanthin is primarily concentrated in the centre of the retina and the cones.
Lutein and zeaxanthin are powerful antioxidants, helping to protect the eye from oxidative and free radical damage and maintain healthy eyes.
Lutein and zeaxanthin support healthy vision by:
Assisting eye adaptation to variations in light intensity
Helping temporarily relieve light sensitivity and helping the eyes tolerate glaring light
Helping vision recovery after exposure to glaring light

Macu-Guard contains Bilberry standardised to anthocyanosides and antioxidant nutrients including lutein and zeaxanthin to support eye health and healthy vision.
Eye anatomy
The eyes are complex structures made up of the cornea, iris, pupil, lens, retina, macula and the optic nerve that allow vision.
The lens sits just behind the iris and pupil and helps to focus light on the back of the eye.
The retina is the sensory portion of the eye and contains layers of photoreceptors and nerves. Rods are a particular type of photoreceptor, located near the edges of the retina, which are
responsible for peripheral and night vision. Cones are photoreceptors that are more central in the retina and are responsible for day and colour vision. Together, rods and cones allow people to see in varying light conditions and different colours.
Rod photoreceptors, which contain the visual pigment rhodopsin, lose colour when light strikes them. Pigment regeneration is important to help protect the delicate photoreceptors and maintain vision.
The macula (‘yellow spot’) is a small area within the retina that is responsible for central vision and visual acuity.
Bilberry
Bilberry has a long history of use as a food and medicine for supporting eye health all over the world.
The active constituents in Bilberry are anthocyanosides - strong antioxidant compounds that have an affinity for the retinal pigmented epithelium. Bilberry anthocyanosides reinforce the collagen structures of the retina and help protect the eyes from free radical damage. Macu-Guard contains Bilberry, standardised to 25mg anthocyanosides.
Bilberry has vasoprotective properties and supports microcirculation to the eye.
Bilberry enhances regeneration of rhodopsin in the retina, which is essential for optimal functioning of the rods, light adaptation and night vision1.
Antioxidant nutrients
Macu-Guard contains key antioxidant nutrients to protect the eyes from oxidative/free radical damage and maintain eye health.
Vitamin C, the body’s primary water-soluble antioxidant, is found in high concentrations in the eye and maintains clarity of the lens and health of the retina. Vitamin C appears to protect the lens of the eye from free radical damage, directly, due to its antioxidant activity, and indirectly, via its ability to recycle vitamin E.
Vitamin E is an important lipid-soluble antioxidant and ample vitamin E may decrease oxidative damage to the lens of the eye.
Zinc and copper are essential trace metals that are concentrated in the photoreceptors and the retinal pigment epithelium of the eye. Both zinc and copper are cofactors in a number of ocular enzymes, including copper-zinc superoxide dismutase, which functions as an antioxidant by catalysing the conversion of free radicals to hydrogen peroxide.
Long-term, high doses of zinc can reduce the bioavailability of copper. It is recommended that copper intake should also be increased with zinc supplementation. Macu-Guard contains 1mg of copper to maintain copper balance.
A 2017 systematic review found that a higher intake of antioxidants (vitamin C, vitamin E, zinc, lutein and anthocyanins) in the diet was associated with longer-term eye health2.
Lutein & zeaxanthin
Lutein and zeaxanthin are yellow-coloured, xanthophyll carotenoids that are not converted into vitamin A in the body. They are found in high quantities in the retina and macula of the eye and in the lens. Lutein is more prominent at the edges of the retina and in the rods, while zeaxanthin is primarily concentrated in the centre of the retina and the cones.
Lutein and zeaxanthin are powerful antioxidants, helping to protect the eye from oxidative and free radical damage and maintain healthy eyes.

Assisting eye adaptation to variations in light intensity
Helping temporarily relieve light sensitivity and helping the eyes tolerate glaring light
Helping vision recovery after exposure to glaring light

subsections.heading: TECHNICAL INFORMATION
subsections.text:
Magnesium Chewable is an innovative supplement combining two organic, bioavailable forms of magnesium in a chewable tablet. Many people have difficulty swallowing large tablets
or capsules, which can limit compliance with supplements, especially minerals like magnesium that are required in higher doses. Magnesium Chewable is a delicious raspberry flavoured tablet that can be chewed to increase compliance and enable supplementation with high-dose magnesium.
Magnesium Chewable contains two organic forms of magnesium that are well absorbed in the body.
A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled study in 46 healthy volunteers compared the relative absorbability and bioequivalence of three forms of magnesium - oxide, citrate and amino acid chelate - under acute and chronic conditions. Results showed that organic forms (magnesium citrate and amino acid chelate) were better absorbed than inorganic magnesium oxide1.
Magnesium
Magnesium is an essential nutrient for over 600 enzymatic processes in the body, required for energy production, muscle contraction and relaxation, cardiac rhythm, vascular tone, carbohydrate, protein and fat metabolism, bone formation, neurological function and brain function.
Optimal magnesium intake is considered to be 320mg a day for women and 420mg a day for men2, however, many individuals are not consuming adequate amounts. According to the Australian Health Survey, one in three people aged two years and over (37% of males and 34% of females) did not meet their estimated dietary requirements for magnesium3.
Magnesium is found in green leafy vegetables, nuts, seeds, whole grains and cacao. Today’s farming and agricultural practices have led to a decline in the magnesium content in foods, with estimates that magnesium content has decreased by as much
as 80-90% in vegetables such as lettuce and spinach4. Modern dietary practices, such as cooking and bleaching grain, causes a loss of up to 80% of magnesium content. Additionally, diets high in calcium, sodium and phosphorus (found in soft drink) or low in selenium, vitamin B6 and vitamin D can reduce magnesium absorption. Foods high in phytates, polyphenols and oxalic
acid, such as rice and nuts, can bind to magnesium to produce insoluble complexes, reducing magnesium availability and
absorption. Moreover, consumption of caffeine and alcohol can lower magnesium levels by increasing renal excretion.
Under normal dietary conditions, about 30% of ingested magnesium is absorbed. Magnesium homeostasis is maintained via the intestine (facilitating magnesium absorption), the bone (magnesium storage) and the kidneys (excretion). The largest amount of magnesium is stored in bone (50-60%), muscle (20-30%) and other soft tissues (20%).
Due to magnesium’s role in energy production, cardiorespiratory function and muscle function, physically active individuals have higher magnesium requirements5. Strenuous exercise can also result in increased urinary and sweat losses of magnesium, increasing magnesium requirements by approximately 10-20%6.
Magnesium deficiency can produce non-specific symptoms, with the most common symptoms being muscle cramps, spasms or twitching. Other symptoms include fatigue, headaches, sleep disturbances, anxiety and irritability.
Magnesium Chewable helps prevent dietary magnesium deficiency.
Muscle health
Magnesium is an essential nutrient for muscle health and muscle contraction function. Magnesium works with calcium for muscle contraction and relaxation. Magnesium is a calcium antagonist, competing with calcium for binding sites. In the resting state, magnesium is present in concentrations 10 000 times higher than calcium in muscle cells. When the message comes for a muscle to contract, calcium is released from the sarcoplasmic reticulum and binds to troponin C and myosin to induce contraction. When
magnesium levels are insufficient, not as much calcium is required to displace magnesium, resulting in muscle cramps and spasms.
Magnesium Chewable can help relieve muscle cramps and reduce the occurrence of muscle cramps when dietary intake is inadequate.
Energy production & glucose metabolism
Magnesium supports energy production as it is involved in the metabolism of carbohydrates and fats to produce energy and is critical for the manufacture of adenosine triphosphate (ATP) within cells. ATP exists primarily as a complex with magnesium (MgATP).

High strength
Magnesium Forte contains high-strength magnesium, from four different sources of highly bioavailable organic magnesium, including magnesium amino acid chelate, citrate, glycinate and orotate.
A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled study in 46 healthy volunteers compared the relative absorbability and bioequivalence of three forms of magnesium – oxide, citrate and amino acid chelate – under acute and chronic conditions. Results showed that organic forms (magnesium citrate and amino acid chelate) were better absorbed than inorganic magnesium oxide1. Magnesium glycinate is a form of magnesium amino acid chelate, with the magnesium attached to the amino acid glycine, which, as the smallest amino acid, is readily absorbed across the intestinal wall. Magnesium orotate is magnesium attached to orotic acid, which carries the mineral across cell membranes.
Magnesium is an essential nutrient for over 300 enzymatic processes in the body, required for DNA replication, energy production, muscle contraction and relaxation, cardiac rhythm, vascular tone, DNA and RNA synthesis, carbohydrate, protein and fat metabolism, bone formation, cell signalling, neurological function and brain function.
Magnesium is found in green leafy vegetables, nuts, seeds, whole grains and cacao. Today’s farming and agricultural practices have led to a decline in the magnesium content in foods, with estimates that magnesium content has decreased by as much as 80-90% in vegetables such as lettuce and spinach2. Modern dietary practices, such as cooking and bleaching grain, causes a loss of up to 80% of magnesium content. As a result, magnesium deficiency is becoming increasingly prevalent. Magnesium Forte helps prevent dietary magnesium deficiency.
Under normal dietary conditions, about 30% of ingested magnesium is absorbed. Magnesium homeostasis is maintained via the intestine (facilitating magnesium absorption), the bone (magnesium storage) and the kidneys (excretion). The largest amount of magnesium is stored in bone (50-60%), muscle (20-30%) and other soft tissues (20%).
Muscle health
Magnesium is an essential nutrient for muscle health and muscle contraction function. Magnesium works with calcium for muscle contraction and relaxation. Magnesium is a calcium antagonist, competing with calcium for binding sites. In the resting state, magnesium is present in concentrations 10 000 times higher than calcium in muscle cells. When the message comes for a muscle to contract, calcium is released from the sarcoplasmic reticulum and binds to troponin C and myosin to induce contraction. When
magnesium levels are insufficient, not as much calcium is required to
displace magnesium, resulting in muscle cramps and spasms.
Energy production & glucose metabolism
Magnesium supports energy production as it is involved in the metabolism of carbohydrates and fats to produce energy and is critical for the manufacture of adenosine triphosphate (ATP) within cells. ATP exists primarily as a complex with magnesium (MgATP).
Magnesium is an important cofactor in glucose metabolism and glycaemic control. It is essential for insulin receptor phosphorylation and regulates glucose uptake in muscle3.
Nervous system health
Magnesium supports healthy nervous system function as it is required for nerve conduction. It modulates the hypothalamic pituitary adrenal axis and can reduce the release of adrenalin and noradrenalin, supporting a healthy stress response in the body.
Cardiovascular system health
Magnesium helps maintain cardiovascular system health and heart health. It is essential for cardiac muscle contraction and production of energy within the heart muscle. Magnesium plays a
role in the active transport of calcium and potassium ions across cell membranes, which is essential for nerve impulse conduction, muscle contraction and normal heart rhythm. It is also essential for the contractility of vascular smooth muscle cells in the arterial wall and influences endothelial function, thereby influencing vasodilation and vasoconstriction.
Bone health
Magnesium supports bone health and assists in the development and maintenance of bones and teeth. Approximately 50-60% of total body magnesium stores reside in the bone, where it binds at the surface of the hydroxyapatite crystals. Magnesium in bones serves as a reservoir of magnesium, which can be released from bone to
maintain physiological extracellular concentrations when magnesium intake is low.
Menstrual cramps & spasms
Magnesium Forte can help relieve symptoms of premenstrual tension including menstrual cramps and spasms and dysmenorrhoea.
Dysmenorrhoea is defined as painful uterine cramps that precede or accompany menses and is caused by hypercontractility of the myometrium and arteriolar vasoconstriction. Magnesium can help
alleviate this via its muscle relaxation and vasodilation activity as well as by inhibiting the biosynthesis of prostaglandin F2 (PGF2) alpha.

subsections.heading: DRUG INTERACTIONS
subsections.text:
Caution with quinolone antibiotics – magnesium forms insoluble complexes with quinolones, decreasing drug absorption. Take drug 2 hours before or 6 hours after magnesium.
Caution with tetracycline antibiotics – tetracyclines form insoluble complexes with magnesium, reducing absorption of both. Separate dose by at least 3 hours.
Caution with bisphosphonates – magnesium can form complexes with drug and reduce absorption. Separate dose by 2 hours.
Caution with calcium channel blockers and other hypotensive medications – magnesium may have additive effects and enhance the hypotensive effect. Monitor blood pressure.
Caution with potassium-sparing diuretics – these drugs also have magnesium-sparing properties which could, theoretically, lead to increased magnesium levels. Monitor.
Caution with skeletal muscle relaxants – magnesium can potentiate effects.

Natural cream base
Magnesium Muscle Cream is a high-strength magnesium cream in a natural cream base that is skin-friendly and free from harsh chemicals and fragrances.
Topical delivery of minerals, knowns as dermal absorption, is not new as it has been used effectively for centuries in several forms including baths, compresses and poultices. In particular, the success of topical treatments such as Epsom salt baths and Dead Sea therapy have been directly attributed to their high magnesium content.
Magnesium Muscle Cream supplies topical magnesium to support magnesium levels in the body.
Magnesium Muscle Cream is suitable for use daily as needed, or acute use after exercise for tired muscles.
For best results, apply before bed to allow the cream to remain on the skin for maximum magnesium absorption.
Magnesium
Magnesium Muscle Cream offers an alternative to oral magnesium supplementation, providing magnesium in a cream base for topical absorption.

A single-arm pilot study looked at the effects of transdermal magnesium chloride (31%) on physical function, muscle health and fatigue in 40 female patients with fibromyalgia. The magnesium chloride was applied via a spray, with 16 sprays applied twice daily, equivalent to 400mg of elemental magnesium. At 2 and 4 weeks, significant differences were noted in physical function, muscle cramp severity and joint and muscle pain2.
Absorption
The skin is the largest organ of the body, covering approximately
1.8m2 and comprises approximately 10% of total body mass3. It acts as a physical barrier between the body and the external environment, protecting against UV radiation, chemicals, allergens
and microorganisms and maintaining moisture and body nutrients.
The skin has three layers:
Epidermis (outer layer): provides a waterproof barrier and contains melanocytes that gives skin its colour
Dermis (middle layer): contains connective tissue, hair follicles and sweat glands
Subcutis (deeper layer): contains fat and connective tissue
In order for substances applied to the skin to be absorbed in the body, they must penetrate the epidermis or be absorbed via sweat glands or hair follicles.
Research shows that magnesium ions are able to penetrate the epidermis to reach the circulation, replenishing cellular magnesium levels4. Magnesium absorption is also significantly facilitated by hair follicles in the skin5.
