Magnesium is found in green leafy vegetables, nuts, seeds, whole grains and cacao. Today’s farming and agricultural practices have led to a decline in the magnesium content in foods, with estimates that magnesium content has decreased by as much as 80-90% in vegetables such as lettuce and spinach2. Modern dietary practices, such as cooking and bleaching grain, causes a loss of up to 80% of magnesium content. As a result, magnesium deficiency is becoming increasingly prevalent. Magnesium Night Plus helps prevent dietary magnesium deficiency.
Under normal dietary conditions, about 30% of ingested magnesium is absorbed. Magnesium homeostasis is maintained via the intestine (facilitating magnesium absorption), the bone (magnesium storage) and the kidneys (excretion). The largest amount of magnesium is stored in bone (50-60%), muscle (20-30%) and other soft tissues (20%).
Muscle health
Magnesium is an essential nutrient for muscle health and muscle contraction function. Magnesium works with calcium for muscle contraction and relaxation. Magnesium is a calcium antagonist,
competing with calcium for binding sites. In the resting state, magnesium is present in concentrations 10 000 times higher than calcium in muscle cells. When the message comes for a muscle to contract, calcium is released from the sarcoplasmic reticulum and binds to troponin C and myosin to induce contraction. When
magnesium levels are insufficient, not as much calcium is required to displace magnesium, resulting in muscle cramps and spasms.
Energy production
Magnesium supports energy production as it is involved in the metabolism of carbohydrates and fats to produce energy and is critical for the manufacture of adenosine triphosphate (ATP) within cells. ATP exists primarily as a complex with magnesium (MgATP).
Nervous system health
Magnesium supports healthy nervous system function as it is required for nerve conduction. It modulates hypothalamic pituitary adrenal axis and can reduce the release of adrenalin and noradrenalin, supporting a healthy stress response in the body.
Cardiovascular system health
Magnesium helps maintain cardiovascular system health and heart health. It is essential for cardiac muscle contraction and production of energy within the heart muscle. Magnesium plays a role in the active transport of calcium and potassium ions across cell membranes, which is essential for nerve impulse conduction, muscle contraction and normal heart rhythm. It is also essential for the contractility of vascular smooth muscle cells in the arterial wall and influences endothelial function, thereby influencing vasodilation and vasoconstriction.
Sleep
Sleep is an essential process that refreshes the mind and allows the body to repair. Today, many people do not get the recommended 7-9 hours’ sleep, sleeping for 6-7 hours or less.
Poor sleep leads to fatigue, poor concentration and memory, mood disturbances, impaired judgement and reaction time and poor coordination. Lack of sleep long term is associated with poor health outcomes.
Poor sleep can be caused by many factors, including shift work, travel across time zones, illness, some medications, internet and social media usage and poor sleep hygiene.
Sleep occurs in phases. Rapid eye movement (REM) sleep occurs regularly during sleep, about once every 90-120 minutes and is the time where most dreams occur. Non-REM sleep makes up about 75%

Mega B Complex contains all 8 B vitamins including B1, B2, B3, B5, B6, B12, biotin (B7) and folic acid (B9), as well as choline and inositol.
B vitamins perform essential, closely inter-related roles in the body to support cellular functioning and act as co-enzymes in a vast array of catabolic and anabolic enzymatic reactions. Their most important role is to convert carbohydrates, protein and fat into energy.
Choline and inositol are both members of the B vitamin family. Choline is necessary for the structure and function of cells and inositol is involved in the transport and metabolism of fats.
B vitamins are not synthesised by the body and therefore must be taken through the diet.
In terms of their origins, B vitamins are typically synthesised by plants. However, humans obtain most of their B vitamins from higher up the food chain in foods of animal origin, such as meat, dairy and eggs.
B vitamins are water soluble, meaning the body is unable to store them in large amounts. As such, regular daily intake is required to support general health.
B vitamins work synergistically in the body, so are best when taken together.
Mega B Complex is suitable for preconception, pregnancy and breastfeeding, when increased vitamins are required. Mega B Complex provides a daily dose of 400 micrograms of folinic acid to support healthy foetal development.
Folinic acid (5-formlyTHF), is a more active form of folate than folic acid as it by passes the di-hydrofolate reductase step in the folic acid metabolism pathway. Individuals with a MTHRF gene mutation have difficulty producing the enzyme which converts folic acid to the active forms folinic acid and methylfolate. Providing folinic acid as an active form of folate bypasses this step.
Energy production
The B vitamins collectively function as coenzymes involved in mitochondrial energy production, supporting normal digestion and the conversion of food into energy.
B vitamins are essential to the proper functioning of the Krebs cycle in the mitochondria. The Krebs cycle is responsible for producing
adenosine triphosphate (ATP), the primary energy carrier in all cells.
Nervous system health
Mega B Complex supports healthy nervous system function.
Vitamins B1, B5, B6, B12 and folinic acid play an important role in the synthesis of neurotransmitters to support the function and health of the nervous system.
Vitamin B1 is essential for the metabolism of acetylcholine, gamma aminobutyric acid (GABA) and serotonin.
Vitamin B5, commonly called the anti-stress vitamin, is involved in the synthesis of the neurotransmitter acetylcholine. Acetylcholine plays an important role in adrenal function and is required for the proper functioning of the adrenal cortex and the synthesis of steroid hormones, namely cortisone.
Vitamin B6 is involved in the conversion of tryptophan to niacin, the synthesis of GABA in the central nervous system as well as the metabolism of serotonin, norepinephrine and dopamine.
Folate and vitamin B12 play an important role in the development, differentiation and functioning of the CNS through methionine-homocysteine metabolism. Methionine becomes activated to
S-adenosylmethionine (SAMe), which is indispensable for numerous reactions involving methylation, for example, the synthesis of nucleic acids (DNA and RNA), proteins, neurotransmitters and hormones.
Serotonin and dopamine are neurotransmitters that play a role in an individual’s mood and wellbeing. Dopamine plays a role in
controlling the movements a person makes, as well as their emotional responses. Serotonin is used to transmit messages between nerve cells and contributes to feelings of wellbeing and happiness.
Vitamin B12 is also required for the proper functioning and development of the brain and nerve cells. It is essential for the myelin sheath that covers and protects the nerves of the central and the peripheral nervous systems, ensuring fast and effective nerve-impulse transmission.
Cardiovascular health
Mega B Complex maintains cardiovascular system health and blood health.

subsections.heading: DRUG INTERACTIONS
subsections.text:
Contraindicated with pyrimethamine (antimalarial) – folate may reduce drug effectiveness.
Caution with tetracycline antibiotics - concurrent administration with B2 and B12 may decrease the effectiveness of the medication. Separate dose.
Caution with chloramphenicol (broad spectrum antibiotic) – folinic acid and B12 may impact drug metabolism. Separate dose.
Caution with anticholinergic drugs – may reduce absorption of vitamin B2. Separate dose.
Caution with carbamazepine and primidone – vitamin B3 and folate may impact drug metabolism, resulting in increased drug levels in the body. Monitor.
Caution with levodopa – vitamin B6 may reduce drug effects. However, this effect is prevented by the administration of a dopa-decarboxylase inhibitor (e.g. benserazide, carbidopa) with levodopa, as is common clinical practice.
Caution with phenobarbital/phenobarbitone and phenytoin (anticonvulsants) - vitamin B6 and folate may reduce serum concentrations of these drugs.

Antioxidant support
Memory & Cognition Gold contains a combination of herbs and nutrients to support cognitive function and memory recall.
Brahmi, Ginkgo and Rosemary are herbs that provide antioxidant support to help reduce free radical damage in the body. The brain is particularly susceptible to oxidative stress as it is metabolically active, possesses high levels of pro-oxidant iron, and is composed of unsaturated lipids prone to lipid peroxidation. The blood-brain barrier prevents many exogenous antioxidants from quenching reactive oxygen species (ROS) in the brain.
Memory & Cognition Gold contains methylcobalmin (mecobalamin), the metabolically active coenzyme form of vitamin B12 that is ready for use in the body.
Memory & Cognition Gold contains methylfolate as Quatrefolic®, the glucosamine salt of (6S)-5-methyltetrahydrofolate. Quatrefolic® is an active form of folate, immediately available for its biological action without being metabolised in the body.
Brahmi
Brahmi is a well-known herb in India with a long history of use in Ayurvedic herbal preparations. The Ayurvedic action for Brahmi in Sanskrit is 'medhya rasayana', which translates to 'herbs which rejuvenate the mind1.
Brahmi is traditonally used in Ayurvedic medicine as a brain tonic to enhance brain health and improve memory and cognitive performance. It is noted in traditional texts to increase memory, learning ability and concentration.
Memory & Cognition Gold contains BacoMind®, a patented extract of Brahmi clinically researched for memory and cognition enhancing properties. It is a unique full-spectrum phytochemical composition containing 9 different bio-actives. BacoMind® is standardised
for bacoside A, bacopaside I, bacopaside II, bacopasaponin C, jujubogenin isomer of bacopasaponin C, bacosine, luteolin, apigenin and β-sitosterol D glucoside.
Brahmi enhances cognitive performance and supports mental concentration and focus. BacoMind® has been clinically trialled for its memory and cognitive enhancing properties in children, adolescents and elderly individuals.
A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluated the used of BacoMind® on 65 elderly individuals with memory impairment without cognitive deficit. Subjects were given 450mg/day BacoMind® extract for 12 weeks. Results showed improved cognitive functions such as attention and verbal memory in the BacoMind® group1.
Another randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled study assessed the use of BacoMind® on 98 healthy elderly subjects. Participants were randomised to receive 300mg/day of BacoMind® extract or an identical placebo. Significant improvements in memory acquisition, memory retention and verbal learning were achieved after 12 weeks compared to baseline in the BacoMind® group2.
In an open-labelled study, 28 children and adolescents aged 4-18 years received a 225mg of BacoMind® for 4 months. A significant improvement (p<0.05) was seen in immediate and working memory as well as visual and auditory memory from baseline3.
Ginkgo
Memory & Cognition Gold contains Ginkgo standardised to Ginkgo flavonglycosides to support brain health and cognitive function.
The brain requires large amounts of energy to function properly in the form of glucose and oxygen. Decreased or impaired circulation impacts both membrane function and energy production. By maintaining blood flow to the brain, Ginkgo enhances oxygen utilisation and improves cellular uptake of glucose, thereby supporting energy production in the brain.
Ginkgo helps increase nerve cell transmission rate, improve synthesis and turnover of brain neurotransmitters and helps normalise acetylcholine receptors in the hippocampus, an area of the brain involved in emotions, feelings and memory processing4.
Ginkgo helps maintain cognitive function and memory during aging.
In a 30-day randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial, 61 participants aged 18 to 40 years were administered a battery of validated neuropsychological tests before and after treatment with either placebo or 6g Ginkgo daily for 30 days. Statistical analysis indicated significant improvements in speed of information processing, working memory speed (p<0.05) and memory consolidation (p<0.001)5.

subsections.text:
Hot flush relief
Formulated for women
No Black cohosh
High-strength Sage
Hormone balance
Female rejuvenating tonic
Menopause Relief contains a therapeutic dose of Sage that has been clinically studied to reduce the frequency and severity of hot flushes associated with menopause1. It also contains Ziziphus and Shatavari to assist in the relief of menopausal symptoms, and Chaste tree for healthy hormone support.
Menopause
The word menopause means ‘stopping menstruation’ and is comprised of the Greek meno (monthly) and pausis (to stop). Menopause can only be diagnosed retrospectively, when the last menstrual period has occurred 12 months or more previously. Menopause occurring between the ages of 45–55 is considered normal, with the average age of menopause being 50–51 years.
Menopausal symptoms are experienced in varied combinations by different women, with some women experiencing severe symptoms while others experience none. It is estimated 20% of women have no symptoms, 60% have a few or mild symptoms, and the other 20% experience change across the spectrum. Symptoms last from
a few months to ten years or more. Twenty-five percent of women experience symptoms for greater than five years and 10% experience symptoms for more than ten years2.
Perimenopause refers to the period before menopause, when menopausal symptoms begin. Menopausal transition occurs from the two to six years preceding cessation of menses to the twelve months after the final menstrual period. This is the period when symptoms are generally most prevalent.
The typical symptoms of peri-menopausal transition include irregular menses, hot flushes, sleeplessness or sleep difficulties, night sweats, weight gain, mood changes, joint pain and stiffness, lowered libido and vaginal dryness. These symptoms are the result of fluctuations in oestrogen and progesterone, rather than declining oestrogen.
The most well recognised symptom of menopause is hot flushes. The individual experience of hot flushes varies greatly among women. While some experience transient episodes of feeling slightly hot and sweaty, others may be drenched in perspiration, go red in the face and be troubled by palpitations. Bothersome hot flushes have been shown to be significantly related to oestrogen decline and elevated FSH levels.
Sage
Sage has a long history of traditional use in Western herbal medicine for treating sweating and menopausal hot flushes, as well as to alleviate associated menopausal symptoms and as a general tonic.
A trial was conducted in Switzerland in 2011 on 71 peri-menopausal women who were treated with a once-daily tablet of fresh Sage
leaves for 8 weeks. Efficacy was evaluated based on the change in intensity and frequency of hot flushes, and total score of the mean number of intensity-rated hot flushes (TSIRHF). There was a
significant decrease in the TSIRHF by 50% within 4 weeks and by 64% within 8 weeks (p<0.0001). The mean total number of hot flushes per day decreased significantly each week from week 1 to 8. The mean number of mild, moderate, severe and very severe flushes decreased by 46%, 62%, 79% and 100% over 8 weeks, respectively3.
Sage binds to complex GABA benzodiazepines receptors in the brain, helping to increase oestrogen levels in the body and improve symptoms of spontaneous sweating and night sweats.
Sage naturally contains thujone, an essential oil that can be toxic when taken at high doses. The Sage used in Menopause Relief is a low thujone extract that is suitable for longer term use if required.
Ziziphus
Ziziphus possesses anxiolytic and mild sedative qualities and is used in traditional Chinese medicine for relieving sleeplessness and spontaneous sweating.
Shatavari
Shatavari is traditionally used in Ayurvedic medicine for relieving menopausal symptoms, such as hot flushes. Shatavari contains steroidal saponins, a key constituent thought to give Shatavari its subtle oestrogen modulating activity.
Shatavari means ‘she who possesses a hundred husbands’ and refers to the rejuvenating effect on the female reproductive organs.
Vitex
Vitex maintains dopamine activity. Dopamine is a neurotransmitter that improves feelings of relaxation and mental alertness and is involved in maintaining normal body temperature and healthy moods.

Sage has a long history of traditional use in Western herbal medicine for treating sweating and menopausal hot flushes, as well as to alleviate associated menopausal symptoms and as a general tonic.
A trial was conducted in Switzerland in 2011 on 71 peri-menopausal women who were treated with a once-daily tablet of fresh Sage
leaves for 8 weeks. Efficacy was evaluated based on the change in intensity and frequency of hot flushes, and total score of the mean number of intensity-rated hot flushes (TSIRHF). There was a
significant decrease in the TSIRHF by 50% within 4 weeks and by 64% within 8 weeks (p<0.0001). The mean total number of hot flushes per day decreased significantly each week from week 1 to 8. The mean number of mild, moderate, severe and very severe flushes decreased by 46%, 62%, 79% and 100% over 8 weeks, respectively3.
Sage binds to complex GABA benzodiazepines receptors in the brain, helping to increase oestrogen levels in the body and improve symptoms of spontaneous sweating and night sweats.
Sage naturally contains thujone, an essential oil that can be toxic when taken at high doses. The Sage used in Menopause Relief is a low thujone extract that is suitable for longer term use if required.
Ziziphus
Ziziphus possesses anxiolytic and mild sedative qualities and is used in traditional Chinese medicine for relieving sleeplessness and spontaneous sweating.
Shatavari
Shatavari is traditionally used in Ayurvedic medicine for relieving menopausal symptoms, such as hot flushes. Shatavari contains steroidal saponins, a key constituent thought to give Shatavari its subtle oestrogen modulating activity.
Shatavari means ‘she who possesses a hundred husbands’ and refers to the rejuvenating effect on the female reproductive organs.
Vitex
Vitex maintains dopamine activity. Dopamine is a neurotransmitter that improves feelings of relaxation and mental alertness and is involved in maintaining normal body temperature and healthy moods.

Mind Ease is a combination of a clinically studied Ashwagandha extract and Lavender formulated to support a healthy stress response in the body.
Ashwagandha comes from Sanskrit, meaning “horse-like smell”. The name refers not only to the smell of the herb but also to its strengthening and aphrodisiac qualities. Ashwagandha is often referred to as “Indian ginseng” because it is used in much the same way as Panax ginseng in traditional Chinese medicine, although
Ashwagandha is considered less stimulating. In traditional Ayurvedic medicine, Ashwagandha is considered a “rasayana”, used to promote physical and mental health and improve vitality.
Mind Ease is suitable to use during breastfeeding. In Ayurvedic medicine and the traditional medicine of South-East Asia, Ashwagandha is commonly used to promote lactation.
KSM-66® Ashwagandha
KSM-66® is a unique, full spectrum extract of Ashwagandha standardised to >5% withanolides. Withanolides are the active component in Ashwagandha and are derived from the root only, not the leaf. The leaves are high in the withanolide withaferin A, which is considered to be cytotoxic. KSM-66® also contains alkaloids,
amino acids (threonine, valine, methionine, isoleucine, lysine, aspartic acid and arginine), flavonoids, choline, vitamin A, calcium, iron, oligosaccharides and fructo-oligosaccharides (prebiotic).
KSM-66® is produced using a unique proprietary extraction process, based on “Green Chemistry” principles, without using alcohol or any other chemical solvent.
KSM-66® was awarded the “Sports Nutrition Ingredient of the year” by The NutraIngredients Asia 2018 and is the recipient of “SFEHerbal Industry Leader Award” 2016, Frost & Sullivan 2014 “Product Innovation in Botanicals” award, “Best Botanical Ingredient” award for 2013 at Natural Products Expo West and “Innovative Ingredient of the Year” award for 2012 at Panacea.
Stress & mild anxiety
Stress is the body's normal way of responding to demands or pressures. It can be caused by both good and bad experiences and helps people cope with life’s challenges. When stress is experienced, the adrenal glands release adrenaline, a hormone which activates the body’s defence mechanisms causing the heart to pound, blood pressure to rise, muscles to tense and the pupils of the eyes to dilate.
These physical changes should occur only for a short period of time. However, when stress becomes prolonged and this defence mechanism continues, it can have negative effects on health.
1 Beyond Blue. (2019). The facts – Anxiety. www.beyondblue.org.au/the-facts/anxiety
Anxiety on the other hand, is stress that continues after that stressor is gone. Anxiety may trigger both emotional responses and physical symptoms including, apprehension, uncertainty, fear, worry, over-
excitability, distress and stomach upsets, nausea, sweating, increased heart rate, feeling short of breath, restlessness, sleep problems, trembling and fatigue.
High circulating levels of epinephrine and cortisol, due to long-term stress, can create an imbalance within the brain chemistry including imbalances in serotonin, gamma aminobutyric acid (GABA), dopamine and norepinephrine (noradrenaline). This can lead to overactivity of the sympathetic nervous system (SNS) and hyperactivity of the ‘fight or flight’ response and anxiety.
The precise cause of anxiety is not fully understood. However, imbalance in brain chemistry, nutritional deficiencies, medications, trauma and medical conditions have been implicated.
Anxiety is the most common mental health condition in Australia. On average, one in four people – one in three women and one in five men – will experience anxiety at some stage in their life. In a 12-month period, over two million Australians experience anxiety1.
KSM-66® for mild anxiety
Mind Ease relieves symptoms of mild anxiety and supports a healthy stress response in the body.
KSM-66® has been clinically trialled to reduce stress and anxiety and improve general wellbeing in adults. In one randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled study, 64 healthy adults with a history of chronic stress were assigned to either KSM-66® (300mg, twice daily after food) or placebo for a period of 60 days. The KSM-66® group exhibited a significant reduction in scores on all stress-assessment scales (75.6% for anxiety and 64.2% for stress) on day 60, relative to the placebo group (-4.3% for anxiety and 10.4% for stress) respectively. Serum cortisol concentrations were also significantly reduced in the KSM-66® group2.
Ashwagandha is traditionally used in Ayurvedic medicine to help the body adapt to stress and helps to relieve the symptoms of mild anxiety. Ashwagandha is an adaptogenic herb, helping to support adrenal function during periods of stress and support the body during times of physical and mental stress.
Lavender has a long history of traditional use in Western herbal medicine (WHM) as a relaxant and carminative and is used to decrease sleeplessness. Lavender contains 1%-3% of volatile essential oil. Lavender oil is considered the active component of the plant, which explains its popularity as a relaxant in aromatherapy.
2 Chandrasekhar, K., Kapoor J., & Anishetty, S. (2012). A prospective, randomised double-blind, placebo-controlled study of safety and efficacy of a high-concentration full-spectrum extract of ashwagandha root in reducing stress and anxiety in adults. Indian Journal of Psychological Medicine, 34(3), 255-62.

Muscle Resuscitation contains two well-absorbed forms of magnesium: magnesium citrate and magnesium amino acid chelate (as glycinate). A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled parallel intervention study of 46 volunteers compared the relative absorbability and bioequivalence of three forms of magnesium: oxide, citrate and amino acid chelate under both acute (24 hour) and chronic (2 month) conditions. Results showed that supplementation with 300mg of the organic forms of magnesium (citrate and amino acid chelate) showed greater absorption (p±0.033) at 60 days than magnesium oxide1.
Magnesium glycinate (also known as magnesium bisglycinate or diglycinate) is magnesium attached to two glycine molecules and is a well-absorbed form of magnesium. Glycine is the preferred molecule for creating organic chelated minerals as glycine is the smallest amino acid and is readily identified and absorbed across the intestinal wall2.
Magnesium
Magnesium is an essential co-factor for more than 300 enzymes in the body and, therefore, has multiple functions:
Energy: Magnesium is essential for energy production in every cell. It helps the body metabolise carbohydrates, proteins and fats.
Muscles: Magnesium helps maintain normal muscle function and is involved in contraction and relaxation of muscles.
Cardiovascular system: Magnesium helps maintain a healthy cardiovascular system and healthy heart muscle function.
Magnesium is a physiologic calcium-channel blocker and, through its role in ion transport systems, can affect the normal rhythm of the heart.
Nervous system: Magnesium helps maintain a healthy nervous system. It regulates nerve depolarisation and transmission by controlling the movement of ions through ion channels in nerves.
Bones and teeth: Magnesium helps maintain healthy bones and teeth. Together with calcium and phosphorus, it is important for
bone strength and structure.
High dose magnesium can help reduce the frequency of mild migraines. In a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled study, 600mg of elemental magnesium reduced the frequency of migraines by 42% in 9-12 weeks (p<0.05). Magnesium supplementation also decreased the number of days with migraine and drug consumption for symptomatic treatment3.
Magnesium supplementation relieves symptoms of PMS. One study found 200mg magnesium reduced mild premenstrual symptoms related to fluid retention, such as weight gain, swelling of extremities, breast tenderness and abdominal bloating4. Another study found that the combination of 200mg magnesium and 50mg B6 reduced anxiety-related premenstrual symptoms, such as nervous tension, mood swings, irritability and anxiety (p=0.04)5.
Magnesium helps relieve menstrual cramps and dysmenorrhoea (painful periods). A systematic review found that magnesium was more effective than placebo for the relief of pain and reduced the need for additional medication6.
Muscle Resuscitation may assist in the prevention and management of a dietary magnesium deficiency. Signs and symptoms of magnesium deficiency include:
Muscle cramps and spasms
Muscle fatigue and weakness
Irritability, low mood, difficulty concentrating
Headaches or migraines
Increased calcium and potassium losses leading to hypocalcaemia and hypokalaemia
Sodium and water retention

Medicinal mushrooms are edible fungi with a long history of medicinal use across many cultures worldwide. Traditionally associated with health-supporting properties, mushrooms have been used for centuries for an array of ailments and to support longevity, particularly in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) and Eastern European traditions.
Mushroom extracts are derived from the fruiting body or mycelium. Mycelium is the main body and feeding membrane of a mushroom and grows underground or within the host plant, acting as a root system. A mushroom fruiting body is the flesh part of the mushroom which grows above ground or on the surface of its host and contains spores. Whole plant mushroom extracts contain a combination of both the fruiting body and mycelium.
Mushrooms contain biologically active polysaccharides, including beta-glucans, proteoglycans and related compounds in their fruiting bodies. Polysaccharides form the major class of immunologically active molecules in mushrooms and other fungi.
Mushroom fruiting bodies are considered “full spectrum” as they provide a wide array of nutritional components and compounds. Mycelium and fruiting bodies share similar cell wall structures and contain the polysaccharide complexes. However, concentrations vary, and beta-glucans are considered to be present in higher concentrations in the fruiting body compared to the mycelium.
Mushroom 5 Complex contains a combination of five medicinal mushrooms including Shiitake, Reishi, Cordyceps, Snow fungus and Turkey tail, derived from fruiting bodies and whole plant extracts.
Immune health
Mushroom 5 Complex maintains healthy immune system function and supports immune system health.
The effect on the immune system can be attributed to the bioactive polysaccharides, such as beta-glucans, which can affect innate and adaptive immune responses.
Shiitake mushrooms contain lentinan which has immunostimulatory effects. Lentinan appears to enhance T-helper cells and stimulate
interferon and various cytokines. It also increases the activity of natural killer cells and macrophages.
A 4-week randomised parallel trial studied the effects of 5 or 10g of Shiitake mushrooms on 52 healthy individuals. Regular consumption resulted in improved immunity demonstrated by an increased expression of immune cell markers. Increased serum IgA implied improved gut immunity and a reduction in C reactive protein (CRP) suggested lowered inflammation1.
Reishi contains polysaccharides, such as β-D-glucans, heteropolysaccharides and glycoproteins, which can affect immune and immune-related cells and show immunomodulatory effects.
Cordyceps contains a high amount of polysaccharides, ranging from 3-8% of total weight, and these are responsible for its pharmacological properties2.
Cordyceps polysaccharides have antioxidant and immunomodulatory activity. In vitro studies show Cordyceps enhances the production of proinflammatory cytokines, TNF-α, and IL-6, as well as the anti-inflammatory cytokine, IL-10, in human peripheral blood3.
Turkey tail contains precursors to the proteoglycans polysaccharide peptide (PSP) and polysaccharide-K (Krestin, PSK), the constituents responsible for the immunological effects known to enhance innate and adaptive immune responses4.
Lung health
Cordyceps, Reishi and Snow fungus are used in TCM as lung tonics to enhance lung health and relieve cough. Reishi is considered to tonify and replenish qi (the body’s vital energy), while Snow fungus strengthens lung-yin.
Reishi and Cordyceps are used in TCM to loosen chest phlegm and clear respiratory tract mucous.
Antioxidant
Mushroom 5 Complex contains mushrooms that have antioxidant and free radical scavenging properties.

Medicinal mushrooms are edible fungi with a long history of medicinal use across many cultures worldwide. Traditionally associated with health-supporting properties, mushrooms have been used for centuries for an array of ailments and to support longevity, particularly in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) and Eastern European traditions.
Mushroom extracts are derived from the fruiting body or mycelium. Mycelium is the main body and feeding membrane of a mushroom and grows underground or within the host plant, acting as a root system. A mushroom fruiting body is the flesh part of the mushroom which grows above ground or on the surface of its host and contains spores. Whole plant mushroom extracts contain a combination of both the fruiting body and mycelium.
Mushrooms contain biologically active polysaccharides, including beta-glucans, proteoglycans and related compounds in their fruiting bodies. Polysaccharides form the major class of immunologically active molecules in mushrooms and other fungi.
Mushroom fruiting bodies are considered “full spectrum” as they provide a wide array of nutritional components and compounds. Mycelium and fruiting bodies share similar cell wall structures and contain the polysaccharide complexes. However, concentrations vary, and beta-glucans are considered to be present in higher concentrations in the fruiting body compared to the mycelium.
Mushroom 5 Complex contains a combination of five medicinal mushrooms including Shiitake, Reishi, Cordyceps, Snow fungus and Turkey tail, derived from fruiting bodies and whole plant extracts.
Immune health
Mushroom 5 Complex maintains healthy immune system function and supports immune system health.
The effect on the immune system can be attributed to the bioactive polysaccharides, such as beta-glucans, which can affect innate and adaptive immune responses.
Shiitake mushrooms contain lentinan which has immunostimulatory effects. Lentinan appears to enhance T-helper cells and stimulate
interferon and various cytokines. It also increases the activity of natural killer cells and macrophages.
A 4-week randomised parallel trial studied the effects of 5 or 10g of Shiitake mushrooms on 52 healthy individuals. Regular consumption resulted in improved immunity demonstrated by an increased expression of immune cell markers. Increased serum IgA implied improved gut immunity and a reduction in C reactive protein (CRP) suggested lowered inflammation1.
Reishi contains polysaccharides, such as β-D-glucans, heteropolysaccharides and glycoproteins, which can affect immune and immune-related cells and show immunomodulatory effects.
Cordyceps contains a high amount of polysaccharides, ranging from 3-8% of total weight, and these are responsible for its pharmacological properties2.
Cordyceps polysaccharides have antioxidant and immunomodulatory activity. In vitro studies show Cordyceps enhances the production of proinflammatory cytokines, TNF-α, and IL-6, as well as the anti-inflammatory cytokine, IL-10, in human peripheral blood3.
Turkey tail contains precursors to the proteoglycans polysaccharide peptide (PSP) and polysaccharide-K (Krestin, PSK), the constituents responsible for the immunological effects known to enhance innate and adaptive immune responses4.
Lung health
Cordyceps, Reishi and Snow fungus are used in TCM as lung tonics to enhance lung health and relieve cough. Reishi is considered to tonify and replenish qi (the body’s vital energy), while Snow fungus strengthens lung-yin.
Reishi and Cordyceps are used in TCM to loosen chest phlegm and clear respiratory tract mucous.
Antioxidant
Mushroom 5 Complex contains mushrooms that have antioxidant and free radical scavenging properties.

Vitamin E is a general term for a group of compounds with vitamin E activity. Alpha-tocopherol is the most abundant and biologically active form of vitamin E.
D-alpha-tocopherol is the naturally occurring isomer of vitamin E (known as ‘natural vitamin E’) and has the highest bioavailability of the forms of vitamin E.
Vitamin E, which is absorbed in the small intestine and stored in the liver, is relatively non-toxic. It is not stored as readily as the other fat-soluble vitamins with up to 60-70% of a daily dose excreted.
Requirements for vitamin E are increased by exposure to pollution, pesticides, additives and radiation. As vitamin E is a fat-soluble vitamin, fat malabsorption (e.g. Crohn’s disease, chronic pancreatitis, liver disease) can reduce its absorption.
Natural Vitamin E 500IU helps prevent vitamin E deficiency.
Antioxidant
Vitamin E is the most important lipid-soluble antioxidant. It protects polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) within the phospholipid layer of each cell membrane from free-radical damage and is, therefore, important for the maintenance of membrane integrity of all cells in the body.
Vitamin E works together with vitamin C and selenium (as glutathione peroxidases) to limit free radical damage and is recycled by
vitamin C and glutathione peroxidase so it can be reused by tissues. Consequently, deficiencies in vitamin C or selenium can increase the need for vitamin E.
Vitamin E is required to protect dietary PUFAs from oxidation. Thus, the need for vitamin E increases with increased intake of PUFAs. A typical Western diet is high in PUFAs.
Cardiovascular health
Vitamin E helps maintain cardiovascular health. As an antioxidant, it inhibits platelet aggregation and adhesion, is anti-inflammatory, improves endothelial function and decreases lipid peroxidation.
Vitamin E assists blood circulation by decreasing platelet aggregation and adhesion.
Epidemiological studies show that higher intakes of vitamin E are associated with lower cardiovascular risk1.
Skin health
Vitamin E supports healthy skin, both internally and topically, and supports wound healing.
As an antioxidant, it helps protect the skin from oxidative damage.
The skin is exposed to numerous chemical and physical agents, such as ultraviolet light, that can cause oxidative stress and result in
adverse effects such as erythema, oedema, skin thickening, wrinkling and photo-ageing2. Vitamin E is the major naturally-occurring lipid-soluble antioxidant that protects the skin from the adverse effects of oxidative stress, including photo-ageing.
Vitamin E helps relieve symptoms of mild eczema and dermatitis, especially itchy skin. A 2015 randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled study found that 400IU vitamin E given to 70 patients with mild to moderate eczema significantly improved symptoms including itching, sleep disturbance and extent of lesions. Overall SCORAD index improved significantly (p<0.05) in those taking vitamin E3.
Another study using 400IU of vitamin E in 96 subjects with eczema found that eczematous lesions healed more quickly in patients receiving vitamin E as a result of decreased pruritus4.
Immune
Vitamin E helps maintain healthy immune function. It protects white blood cells from oxidative damage, enhances antibody production by white blood cells and enhances their ability to phagocytise bacteria.
PMS
Vitamin E can help reduce the symptoms of premenstrual syndrome. An early randomised, double-blind study found that 400IU d-alpha-tocopherol daily for 3 cycles significantly improved certain affective and physical symptoms of PMS5.
Specifically, vitamin E relieves menstruation pain. Two randomised, placebo-controlled studies using either 200IU vitamin E twice daily or 500IU daily, starting 2 days before menstruation and continuing for the first 3 days of bleeding, found that vitamin E reduced menstrual pain severity and duration. Beneficial effects were seen after 2 months and reached maximal effect after 4 months6,7.
Sperm health
Vitamin E helps support sperm health and motility.
Antioxidants are important for sperm health as the membranes of germ cells and spermatozoa are very sensitive to oxidation and high levels of oxidation can reduce sperm motility. Some
research in humans has shown that vitamin E decreases the levels of malondialdehyde, an organic compound used as a marker of oxidative stress, and improves sperm motility8.

Nicotinic acid (vitamin B3)	✓ 8-hour release	✓ Skin health	✓ Low risk of flushing

Niacin is a water-soluble vitamin required for the function of over 200 enzymes throughout the body. It is well-absorbed after oral administration and metabolised in the liver to nicotinamide
adenine dinucleotide (NAD) and nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADP). NAD and NADP are essential for energy metabolism, oxidation-reduction reactions and ADP-ribose transfer reactions involved in DNA repair and calcium mobilisation.
Niacin can be formed in the body from the amino acid tryptophan. It takes 60mg of tryptophan to make 1mg niacin. Poor protein intake, especially inadequate tryptophan, increases the risk of deficiency.
Niacin helps convert food into energy and assists in the metabolism of carbohydrates and dietary fats. It is a component of the glucose tolerance factor (GTF) that supports sugar metabolism.
Niacin supports skin health. It can dilate small blood vessels, improving blood flow of nutrients and oxygen to the skin, heart and brain.
Niacin is often used in high doses to maintain cardiovascular health and a healthy lipid profile. Niacin can reduce fibrinogen
concentrations in plasma and may stimulate fibrinolysis. It inhibits the mobilisation of free fatty acids from peripheral tissues and reduces hepatic synthesis of triglycerides and the secretion of low density lipoproteins and very low-density lipoproteins1.
Niacin vs nicotinamide
Two main forms of vitamin B3 are found in foods: nicotinic acid (niacin) and nicotinamide (niacinamide). Both can be converted into active forms of vitamin B3 in the body.
Both niacin and nicotinamide can perform all the essential biochemical functions of vitamin B3 in the body and prevent a deficiency, however, niacin has additional actions, such as cardiovascular effects and blood vessel dilation.
Nicotinamide does not cause the flush that is a common side effect of niacin supplementation.
Niacin flush
Niacin supplementation is commonly associated with flushing of the skin, known as the ‘niacin flush’, caused by the dilation of the capillaries. Although this effect is transient and harmless, it can be uncomfortable and concerning if people do not expect it.
The body usually adapts to niacin intake overtime and side-effects lessen in severity. Skin flushing is worse when niacin is taken on an empty stomach.
Flushing is usually caused by higher doses and immediate release niacin. Niacin 100mg Extended Release is unlikely to cause flushing.
Extended release
Niacin 100mg Extended Release is an extended-release product that releases niacin into the body over an 8-hour period. Extended-release forms are less likely to cause flushing than immediate-release forms.
It is important to differentiate extended-release from sustained-release forms. Sustained-release niacin preparations release niacin into the body over a 24-hour period and are associated with a higher risk of hepatotoxicity and gastrointestinal intolerance than unmodified niacin preparations. This may be because the liver is not given a break.
Extended-release niacin allows the vitamin to be absorbed over 8 hours, which reduces the incidence of flushing seen with immediate-release forms, and hepatotoxicity, seen with sustained-release forms, as it still allows the liver to have a break. Increased risk of hepatotoxicity is not seen with extended-release niacin2.

subsections.heading: DRUG INTERACTIONS
subsections.text:
Caution with anticoagulant or antiplatelet medication - niacin may increase the risk of bleeding in some patients.
Caution with bile acid sequestrants (e.g. cholestyramine) – drugs bind to niacin and decrease absorption. Separate dose by 4-6 hours.
Caution with statin medication. Co-administration of statins and niacin may increase the risk of developing myotoxicity,
however, usually in much higher doses. Co-administration is often recommended for dyslipidaemia; it is recommended to use the lowest possible dose of both agents and monitor patient for signs of myotoxicity during concurrent use.

subsections.heading: CAUTIONS
subsections.text:
Not recommended during pregnancy or lactation due to insufficient safety data on high doses of niacin.
Avoid consuming with alcohol. Alcohol can exacerbate the flushing associated with niacin.
Contraindicated in people with gout. Niacin can reduce urinary excretion of uric acid, potentially resulting in hyperuricemia.
Caution in people with blood sugar imbalance. High doses of niacin can impair glucose tolerance. However, doses under 1.5g daily have minimal effects on blood glucose.

subsections.heading: SIDE EFFECTS
subsections.text:
Extended-release niacin is less likely to cause a niacin flush, however, it is still possible in sensitive individuals and may occur several hours after supplementation. Take on a full stomach to reduce risk of flushing.
Other unwanted effects (usually seen in immediate release forms and in high doses) include itching, mucous membrane irritation and diarrhoea.

The Olive tree has a long history of medicinal use to promote health. The leaves were widely used as a remedy for the relief of fevers in Greece, Spain, Italy, France, Turkey, Palestine, Morocco and Tunisia.
Olive leaf is made up of secoiridoids (oleuropein and its derivatives), hydroxytyrosol, polyphenols, triterpenes, including oleanolic acid, and flavonoids, which function to provide the Olive tree with resistance
to damage from pathogens and insects. The primary constituents, oleuropein and hydroxytyrosol, are believed to be responsible for many of the therapeutic properties of the Olive leaf.
Herbs of Gold Olive Leaf contains 8g of fresh Olive leaf per
7.5mL dose, standardised to 44mg of oleuropein and 2.85mg of hydroxytyrosol. While oleuropein is the better-known polyphenol in Olive leaf, hydroxytyrosol is derived from the hydrolysis of oleuropein and has one of the highest know ORAC (oxygen radical absorbance capacity) scores for any natural antioxidant. Hydroxytyrosol has also demonstrated an ability to cross the blood brain barrier, allowing it to have a significant action to scavenge free radicals in the
nervous system1.
Figure 1: Olive leaf processing flow chart
Olive leaf has demonstrated numerous health benefits including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial, while having positive effects on the cardiovascular system2.
Herbs of Gold Olive Leaf extract
Herbs of Gold Olive Leaf contains an Olive leaf extract that is 100% Australian grown and manufactured. The fresh Olive leaves are harvested and processed within 6 hours of being picked, ensuring maximum freshness and quality, occurring just a stone throw from the Olive groves themselves in Boundary Bend, Victoria.
Olive Leaf is prepared using a unique water and glycerine extraction process to ensure the purest alcohol-free extraction, while maximising the active components of the Olive leaf. The leaves are picked and processed whilst still fresh using only purified water and glycerine, retaining the volatile constituents of the leaf and minimising heat damage to the antioxidants that can occur during other processing methods.

subsections.heading: TECHNICAL INFORMATION
subsections.text:
Immune health
Cardiovascular health
Antioxidant
Relieves mild fevers
One-a-day
Vegan-friendly
The Olive tree is native to the Mediterranean region and has a long history of medicinal use to promote health. The leaves were widely used as a remedy for the relief of fevers in Greece, Spain, Italy, France, Turkey, Palestine, Morocco and Tunisia.
Olive leaf is made up of secoiridoids (oleuropein and its derivatives), hydroxytyrosol, polyphenols, triterpenes, including oleanolic acid, and flavonoids, which support the tree’s resistance to damage
from pathogens and insects. The primary constituent, oleuropein, is believed to be responsible for many of the therapeutic properties of the leaf.
Herbs of Gold Olive Leaf 7500 is high-strength, with each tablet containing the equivalent of 7.5g Olive leaf, standardised to 180mg of oleuropein.
Antioxidant
Olive Leaf 7500 acts as an antioxidant to reduce free radicals formed in the body.
Free radicals are unstable molecules that are naturally formed during exercise and when the body converts food into energy. The body is also exposed to free radicals from a variety of environmental sources, such as cigarette smoke, air pollution and sunlight. Free radicals can cause “oxidative stress,” a process that can trigger cell damage.
Antioxidants are substances that help to prevent or delay cell damage.
Numerous phenolics from Olive leaf have been shown to have strong antioxidant activity. According to in vitro tests, the flavonoids, rutin, catechin and luteolin exert antioxidant effects almost 2.5 times more potent than vitamin C and E, and at levels comparable to that of lycopene1.
Olive leaf has been shown to have the highest free radical-scavenging activity of 55 herbs when studied – more than twice of that of Green tea and St Mary’s thistle2.
Immune support
Olive Leaf 7500 supports healthy immune system function.
Olive leaf has been found to have antimicrobial properties against viruses, bacteria and yeasts in animal and human studies. Olive leaf inhibits assembly of viruses at the cell membrane, interfering with critical amino acid production, and stops viral shedding. Olive leaf can also inhibit bacteria, either by inactivating cellular enzymes critical for bacterial replication or via attack on the cell membrane3.
Olive leaf is used in traditional Western herbal medicine as a febrifuge to relieve mild fevers.
Cardiovascular support
Olive Leaf 7500 supports cardiovascular system function.
Olive leaf contains polyphenols, particularly oleuropein, which are associated with cardioprotective activity. The herb has demonstrated vasodilatory, anti-platelet aggregation, anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties that help support a healthy cardiovascular system.
In particular, oleuropein supports cardiovascular health by protecting membranes from lipid oxidation, affecting coronary blood vessel dilation, exerting antiarrhythmic action and improving lipid metabolism3.
A double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled cross-over acute intervention trial investigated the influence of Olive leaf extract containing 51.12mg oleuropein on vascular function and inflammation. A single dose of Olive leaf resulted in a significant
reduction in IL-8 and reduced arterial stiffness compared to controls.

subsections.heading: TECHNICAL INFORMATION
subsections.text:
Highly bioavailable organic iron
Gentle on digestion
Assists blood health
Supports energy production
Activated forms of folate and vitamin B12
With vitamin C to boost iron absorption
With Spirulina and Spinach
Iron is an essential mineral found in the body that plays a pivotal role in oxygen transportation and storage, immune health, as well as a multitude of enzyme reactions. Iron levels are tightly controlled within the body and levels are regulated by absorption rather than excretion. Many factors can hinder the amount of iron absorbed within the gastrointestinal tract.
There are two forms of dietary iron: haem and non-haem. In the diet, haem iron is derived from animal sources and is readily absorbed
by the body. Non-haem iron is mainly derived from plant sources and is poorly absorbed when compared to haem iron. Non-haem iron is easily inhibited by dietary factors such as tea and coffee (polyphenols), wholegrains (phytic acid), chocolate, spinach and berries (oxalic acid), calcium, zinc and manganese, leading to poor solubility and absorption.
Organic Iron MAX contains 250mg of vitamin C to assist iron absorption. Vitamin C helps to solubilise non-haem iron, so it helps to increase iron absorption. Vitamin B2 also assists the body in absorbing iron.
Organic Iron MAX also contains cofactors vitamins B1, B2, B6, B12 and folate, important to assist iron metabolism and maintain healthy blood.
Organic Iron MAX contains the active forms of folate, methylfolate, and vitamin B12, methylcobalamin, that are ready for use in the body, without requiring metabolic conversion.
Spirulina, a blue-green alkaline algae, and spinach are rich sources of iron.
FerrochelTM
Albion’s FerrochelTM (ferrous bisglycinate amino acid chelate) is an organic form of non-haem iron with greater bioavailability that is well-tolerated and gentle on the digestive system. FerrochelTM has been shown to have up to 90% bioavailability in clinical studies1.
FerrochelTM consists of one molecule of ferrous iron bound to two molecules of glycine, creating small organic chelated iron molecules (similar to a dipeptide or small protein) that can easily pass through the intestinal wall. This chelation means that the iron remains intact
and electrically neutral, so doesn’t break down in the stomach acid and is therefore delivered intact to the small intestine where it is easily absorbed.
The European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) states that ferrous bisglycinate has been used in numerous field trials and that in all cases, substantial improvements in iron status indicators (serum levels of haemoglobin and ferritin, total iron binding capacity and iron stores) have been reported in the groups supplemented with ferrous bisglycinate compared to the controls. Moreover, there was no evidence of iron overloading in non-iron deficient individuals and ferrous bisglycinate was well tolerated by adult males, pregnant females, non-pregnant females with normal iron status, as well as in iron deficient young children2.
Studies have shown iron from FerrochelTM to be better absorbed and better tolerated than other forms of iron.
Iron salts, such as ferrous sulfate, become electrically charged when stomach acid breaks down the iron salt molecule, creating oxidation of vitamin E and blocking calcium uptake. This unbound iron is easily inhibited by other dietary factors and further impacts the mucous membranes of the gastrointestinal tract leading to gastric upset and digestive discomfort.
One study testing the absorption of iron added to fortify foods found that iron absorption from Ferrochel™ was about twice the absorption as from ferrous sulfate (p<0.05)3.
A double-blind study compared the absorption of Ferrochel™ with polymaltose iron in 20 children aged 1-13 years. Both treatments resulted in significant increases in haemoglobin levels, Mean Corpuscular Volume (MCV) and Red Cell Distribution Width (RDW) and a reduction of transferrin levels. However, only iron bisglycinate significantly increased ferritin (p<0.05). Ferritin is considered the most efficient indicator of a response to iron treatment. The study concluded that iron bisglycinate was more effective in replenishing iron stores, favouring a reduction in required supplementation time4.

subsections.heading: DRUG INTERACTIONS
subsections.text:
Caution with ACE inhibitors (hypertension), cimetidine (hyperacidity),
L-dopa and carbidopa (movement disorders e.g. Parkinson’s disease), penicillamine, sulfasalazine (antidiarrheal) - iron supplementation may reduce drug absorption. Separate dose by at least 2 hours.
Caution with quinolone and tetracycline antibiotics - iron supplementation may reduce drug effect. Take drugs 2 hours before or 4-6 hours after iron.
Caution with thyroxine - iron supplementation can reduce drug effects. Separate doses by at least 2–4 hours and monitor thyroid levels.
Caution with antacids - coadministration may reduce iron absorption and vitamin C may increase the amount of aluminium absorbed from these medications. Separate doses by at least 2 hours.
Caution with methotrexate – folate may affect drug efficacy. Use only under the supervision of a health professional.

Medicinal uses for Oregano date back to the ancient Greek and Roman empires, where the leaves were used to treat different conditions such as skin sores, aching muscles and as an antiseptic.
The major active components of Oregano are phenolic monoterpenes, which constitute approximately 90% of the total composition of Oregano essential oil. Carvacrol is considered the predominant compound, followed by thymol (an isomer of carvacrol), p-cymene and γ-terpinene1.
Carvacrol is believed to be responsible for most of Oregano oil’s purported health benefits. Several in vitro an in vivo studies
support antifungal, anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, antimicrobial, anitbacterial, antiparasitic, anit-allergenic, antiviral and immune-stimulant properties, as well as exerting positive effects on digestive health2.
Oregano oil
The Oregano oil in Herbs of Gold Organic Oregano Oil is sourced from Spain, where the climate provides the ideal growing conditions for the plant to thrive.
The essential oil from Oregano is obtained by steam distillation, a process using a mixture of hot steam and gentle pressure which allows microscopic protective sacs to release the essential oil. The process does not use alcohol or any harsh chemicals.
The Oregano Oil is certified organic, meaning it is free from human-made fertilisers, pesticides, growth regulators and genetically modified organisms.
The Oregano oil is in a certified organic extra virgin olive oil base which assists in preserving the essential oil from the Oregano. Not only does this act as an effective dilutant and carrier of the oil, the emulsified oil helps to reduce any potential gastrointestinal effects that may be experienced using the essential oil.
Antioxidant
Oregano oil is a strong antioxidant.
Oregano oil has been studied for its potential scavenging activity towards reactive species and capacity to neutralise oxidative stress and prevent oxidative damage.
Among the essential oils from different parts of the Oregano, the leaf-flower oils have demonstrated the best antioxidant activity3.
*As this is a natural ingredient, minor variation between batches is possible
Immune health
Organic Oregano Oil supports immune system health.
Oregano oil has demonstrated strong antimicrobial action when the body encounters harmful organisms and outside invaders.
One in vitro study demonstrated that Oregano oil had the highest and broadest antimicrobial activity when compared with other essential oils, with carvacrol showing the highest antimicrobial action of the tested constituents4.
Carvacrol has also been shown to have activity against vaginal candidiasis in an animal model. Treatment with carvacrol for 7 consecutive days eradicated the fungal overgrowth in 7 of 9 infected rats, further reducing the number of colony forming units of the remaining 2 rats by 98%5.
In a study of 14 adult patients whose stools tested positive for enteric parasites Blastocystis hominis, Entamoeba hartmanni and Endolimax nana, Oregano oil was supplemented for 6 weeks. Emulsified oil of Oregano was given at 600mg daily. Following treatment there was complete disappearance of Entamoeba hartmanni (four cases), Endolimax nana (one case), and Blastocystis hominis in eight cases. Also, Blastocystis hominis scores declined in three additional cases. Gastrointestinal symptoms improved in seven of the 11 patients who had tested positive for Blastocystis hominis6.

Carvacrol has also been shown to have activity against vaginal candidiasis in an animal model. Treatment with carvacrol for 7 consecutive days eradicated the fungal overgrowth in 7 of 9 infected rats, further reducing the number of colony forming units of the remaining 2 rats by 98%5.
In a study of 14 adult patients whose stools tested positive for enteric parasites Blastocystis hominis, Entamoeba hartmanni and Endolimax nana, Oregano oil was supplemented for 6 weeks. Emulsified oil of Oregano was given at 600mg daily. Following treatment there was complete disappearance of Entamoeba hartmanni (four cases), Endolimax nana (one case), and Blastocystis hominis in eight cases. Also, Blastocystis hominis scores declined in three additional cases. Gastrointestinal symptoms improved in seven of the 11 patients who had tested positive for Blastocystis hominis6.

Acute or chronic pain
Pain Relief PEA has been formulated with high-strength PEA for acute or long-term use to help manage a variety of pain states, including mild joint pain, nerve pain and symptoms of mild arthritis.
Palmitoylethanolamide (PEA) is an endogenous fatty acid amide with neuroprotective, anti-inflammatory and analgesic actions. PEA is produced naturally in the body in response to injury and stress.
PEA is found in many plant and animal food sources, as well as in the cells and tissues of mammals. Food sources of PEA include peas, tomato, alfalfa, corn, soybean and peanut. It was first isolated from purified lipid fractions of soybeans, egg yolk and peanut meal1.
Decades of research show that PEA is a well-tolerated therapeutic strategy for the management of chronic pain in different conditions2.
The therapeutic dose of PEA used in clinical trials for pain relief is between 300mg and 1200mg daily. Pain Relief PEA contains PEA as Levagen®+, a well-absorbed form of PEA, so it is reasonable to
expect similar results at a lower dose, with efficacy shown at between 300mg and 600mg (2 to 4 capsules) daily.
Levagen®+
PEA is a lipophilic (fat-loving) substance and has traditionally shown poor absorption in animal models. Levagen®+ utilises LipiSperse® technology to increase bioavailability in the body. LipiSperse® enables PEA to easily disperse in the watery gastrointestinal tract and prevents the PEA crystals from agglomerating, increasing the surface area for superior absorption.
Levagen®+ solubility and particle size are checked by Dynamic Light Scattering analysis and Laser Light Obscuration to enable optimal dispersion and efficacy.
A parallel, double-blind study compared the absorption of 300mg of Levagen®+ and a standard PEA in 28 healthy adults. Levagen®+ significantly increased plasma PEA concentration above baseline concentrations and by 1.75 times that of standard PEA (p<0.05) (see figure 1)3.
Figure 1: PEA plasma concentrations
Levagen®+ has an acute onset of action, with pharmacokinetic studies showing rapid absorbtion, with peak plasma concentrations occurring 45 minutes post ingestion4.
Pain
Pain is a complex mechanism that exists to protect the body from danger and harm.
There are two main types of pain: acute pain, the normal response to an injury that is usually sudden and short-lived, and chronic pain that continues beyond the time expected for healing.
When pain becomes chronic, it can severely impact day-to-day functions and quality of life. Common causes of chronic pain include arthritis, musculoskeletal ailments, nerve pain and surgery.
Chronic pain is prevalent in Australia, with one in five Australians aged 45 and over living with persistent, ongoing pain5. In 2020, over
3.37 million Australians were living with chronic pain and the total financial cost of chronic pain in Australia was estimated to be $144.1 billion6.
Conventional pain medications generally work by either downregulating prostaglandins, and therefore the inflammatory response, or by changing the pain messages in the brain. PEA has multiple mechanisms of action that differ from conventional steroidal and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), giving it the potential to relieve pain without the common side-effects seen with other medication and the ability to be used in conjunction with other pain medications.
Mechanism of action
PEA acts via multiple mechanisms, acting directly or indirectly on several molecular targets to produce a therapeutic effect in both the central and peripheral nervous systems.
The analgesic activity appears to be achieved via two different mechanisms: direct receptor-mediated and an indirect “entourage effect”.
PEA directly targets nuclear peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha (PPAR-α), which is a master-switch for a number of genes activating the inflammatory cascade, and cannabinoid-like G-protein-coupled receptors (GPR55).
PEA works indirectly on a number of molecular targets by potentiating the activity of other endogenous compounds or by inhibiting the metabolic degradation of these molecules, known as the “entourage effect”. It acts indirectly on cannabinoid (CB) receptors, particularly CB2 receptor, and indirectly activates transient receptor potential vanilloid type 1 (TRPV1) channels7. subsections.text:
To break the life cycle of worms: Take for 14 days, then take a break for 14 days, then take again for 14 days. Repeat if necessary.
Adults and children over 12 years – Take 2 tablets, three times a day, with food.
Children – 3-4 years: Take 1 tablet daily; 5-9 years: Take 1 tablet, twice daily;
10-12 years: Take 1 tablet, three times a day. Take crushed in food or swallowed. Or take as directed by your health professional.
Not to be used long-term. Do not use if pregnant or likely to become pregnant.

subsections.heading: TECHNICAL INFORMATION
subsections.text:
Suitable for children & adults
Traditionally relieves dyspepsia
Traditionally used to support liver function
With Thyme & Oregano essential oils
ParaStrike contains high-strength European wormwood (Wormwood), Black walnut and Barberry, combined with essential oils to help rid the body of intestinal worms.
ParaStrike contains Thyme and Oregano essential oils. These oils are microencapsulated and spray dried onto the tablet to help protect the naturally occurring active compounds which are highly susceptible to changes caused by external factors such as light, oxygen and heat.
ParaStrike is formulated for both children and adults with different dosing requirements based on age. The lifecycle of an adult worm means it may live for up to 6 weeks. As such, the treatment regime needs to cover a 6-week period to ensure adult worms and newly hatched eggs are destroyed and eliminated, reducing the risk of reinfestation. While a child is more likely than an adult to become infested, the risk of passing infestation from a child to an adult is high, so treatment for the whole family is commonly recommended.
Worms
A parasite is any organism that lives in or on another organism and steals nutrition from the host at the host’s expense. Parasites are generally grouped into three categories: helminths (parasitic worms and flukes), protozoa (single celled organisms such are giardia, toxoplasma, plasmodium and cryptosporidium) and arthropods (associated with vector diseases carried by mosquitos, fleas, ticks, mites and lice).
Parasitic infections occur due to many factors: urbanisation (crowding together); intensive farming systems; greater movement and relocation of animals; land and marine development; inadequate effluent disposal; parasitic drug resistance and the spread of vector insecticide resistance.
Parasites typically infect the digestive system, although they can invade other tissues and organs and can cause a broad range of symptoms, the most significant of which are gut and digestive dysfunction.
Pinworms are the most common type of worm infection found in Australia. Children, particularly pre-school and school-aged children,
are more susceptible to pinworm infections, although adults can easily become infected. Usually, if one person in the household has a worm infection, it is more than likely that other members of the family will also become infected. A female pinworm can lay up to
15 000 eggs a day1.
Worms are spread directly by children (or adults) who scratch their bottoms and then carry the worm eggs back to their mouth with their hands or indirectly, in food, dust or other articles of bedding or clothing. The eggs can survive for up to two weeks outside the body.
Around 4 weeks after the eggs are swallowed, they hatch in the small intestine and the female travels down the digestive tract and exits the body via the anus to lay a new batch of eggs on the surrounding skin, often at night.
Anthelmintic activity
ParaStrike contains Wormwood and Black walnut, both traditionally used in Western herbal medicine to help remove intestinal threadworms and pinworms.
Wormwood has a long history of use (going back to 1550 BC) as a vermifuge to help remove intestinal worms, which is reflected in its common name. Key constituents include intensely bitter sesquiterpene lactones (including absinthin), phenolic acids and flavonols.
The key constituents of Black walnut thought to be responsible for its therapeutic action include naphthoquinones (juglone & plumbagin) and tannins2.
Barberry contains the alkaloid berberine, a signature component of Barberry with antimicrobial (bacteria and fungi) and antiparasitic properties giving berberine a broad-spectrum action. The root bark contains the highest number of alkaloids when compared to the stem bark. Barberry also has a mild laxative effect so helps eliminate waste and toxins, an important element to cleansing the body of parasites.
ParaStrike also contains the essential oils of Thyme and Oregano. The active components of Thyme, thymol and carvacrol, give Thyme its antibacterial and antimicrobial action. Oregano essential oil

subsections.heading: DRUG INTERACTIONS
subsections.text:
Contraindicated with anticoagulant and antiplatelet medications such as warfarin – Wormwood may increase bleeding risk and Thyme essential oil may interact by inducing phase I and phase II liver enzymes.
Contraindicated with fluoroquinolone and tetracycline antibiotics, and anti-infective medications – Barberry may reduce their effectiveness.

subsections.heading: CAUTIONS
subsections.text:
Contraindicated in pregnancy and lactation – the thujone in Wormwood can have a contraction effect on the uterus, while berberine can be harmful to the developing brain of the unborn child.
Contraindicated in gastric or duodenal ulcers – Wormwood can increase gastric fluid potentially making these conditions worse.
Caution in high blood pressure - Thyme essential oil may theoretically increase blood pressure. Monitor.
Caution in acute/severe hepatocellular disease, liver cancer, intestinal spasm or ileus - Wormwood and Barberry can impact liver function when liver health is poor.
Wormwood may cause allergic reactions in people sensitive to the Asteraceae family.
This product is not suitable for long-term use. Use only at the dose and directions indicated on the bottle.

subsections.heading: SIDE EFFECTS
subsections.text:
Thyme oil may cause mild gastrointestinal irritation, such as heartburn, diarrhoea, nausea and vomiting.
Mild gastrointestinal symptoms, headaches or fatigue may occur as a result of parasitic die-off. These symptoms are a common detox reaction to the toxins released when the parasites start to die and, when mild, should resolve within a few days.

subsections.text:
Helps meet increased demands of pregnancy & breastfeeding
Mother & infant health
Contains both folinic acid and methylfolate
With methylcobalamin
Healthy foetal development
Vanilla flavour for improved taste & smell
Herbs of Gold Pregnancy Plus 1-2-3 provides nutritional support for both mother and baby during all stages of natal development: preconception, pregnancy and breastfeeding.
Pregnancy Plus 1-2-3 contains 22 important vitamins and minerals to help meet the increased demands of pregnancy and breastfeeding and help maintain healthy foetal development.
Pregnancy Plus 1-2-3 comes in a vanilla-coated tablet to improve taste and smell.
Preconception is the period of time before conception occurs. The minimum period of preconception care is around 3 months for both males and females. It takes approximately 3 months for an ovum
to become ready for conception and approximately 3 months for healthy sperm maturation. Preconception care helps provide an optimal environment for conception to occur.
Pregnancy is the gestational period between conception and birth and is approximately 40 weeks in length. Foetal development occurs rapidly after conception, with most organs being formed in the first 8-10 weeks of pregnancy – a time when the embryo is particularly vulnerable to nutritional deficiencies. During pregnancy, the nutritional needs of a woman are increased by up to 50-200%1 and
optimum nutrition is essential for maternal well-being and for healthy foetal growth and development.
Breastfeeding increases the need for micronutrients. A healthy infant can double its weight in the first 4-6 months after birth and can rely on breastmilk for the micronutrients that support its rapid growth. Optimal nutrient intake also supports maternal health by replenishing nutrient stores that may have been depleted during pregnancy and milk production.
Preconception health
Pregnancy Plus 1-2-3 contains nutrients to support preconception health.
Folate is considered the primary nutrient in preconception health.
Iodine is essential to produce maternal and foetal thyroid hormones
that regulate the development of the foetal brain and nervous system. A female’s iodine requirements increase substantially during pregnancy to ensure adequate supply to the foetus.
Zinc is involved in numerous pathways within the body, including those that affect reproductive health and function. Zinc is required for reproduction and ovulation as well as DNA synthesis for the development of the oocyte in females.
Healthy foetal development
Pregnancy Plus 1-2-3 contains nutrients to support healthy foetal development and the healthy development of the foetal brain and central nervous system (CNS).
Folate is necessary for the early development of the CNS.
Iodine is required in adequate amounts during pregnancy for healthy thyroid hormone production, essential for myelination of the CNS and for normal foetal brain development.
Both folate and vitamin B12 are important for DNA replication, cell division and growth. The need for these vitamins is increased
during foetal development as cell turnover is increased. Biotin is also important for DNA replication, cell division and growth.
Vitamin D is important for the healthy development of bones and teeth and maintenance of skeletal health. Vitamin D helps in the absorption of calcium and phosphorous and increases mineral deposition into the skeleton.
Adequate maternal vitamin D during the second half of pregnancy is needed for normal foetal brain development. Maternal vitamin D status directly correlates with an infant’s vitamin D status, intrauterine
growth of long bones, infant skeletal growth and bone mineralisation.
Zinc is a key element for growth and development, playing a crucial role in the first phase of life, including embryogenesis and foetal life. Functionally, zinc participates in cell division and growth, intestinal electrolyte absorption, neurotransmission, immune response, thymus activity and vision2.

enteric pathogens by limiting their ability to colonise the intestine. The current understanding is that probiotics typically take between 10 and 14 days to colonise the gastrointestinal tract1.
Probiotic + SB contains studied probiotic strains supplied by Danisco®, a supplier trusted by some of the world’s most recognised manufacturers. Probiotic + SB contains 6 billion colony forming units (CFU) Saccharomyces boulardii (SB), a live yeast with probiotic activity that helps maintain a healthy digestive tract and supports healthy immune function. SB, when given orally, achieves steady-state concentrations within three days and is cleared within 3 to 5 days after it is discontinued2.
Intestinal microbiota & digestion
The human gastrointestinal tract is populated by bacteria, archaea, yeasts and fungi, which are collectively referred to as the
gastrointestinal (GI) microbiota. The microbiota has several important functions in maintaining human health, including providing the host with nutrients and protecting from harmful microbes. It is involved in many metabolic processes, including the fermentation of undigested carbohydrates into short-chain fatty acids, lipid metabolism and vitamin synthesis.
The ecological balance of the intestinal microbiota can be disturbed by environmental or physiological factors, such as antibiotics, stress and diet.
Probiotic + SB helps maintain a balanced, healthy composition of the intestinal microbiota by re-establishing friendly intestinal bacteria and inhibiting the growth of unwanted intestinal bacteria. Strains of
lactic acid bacteria such as Lactobacillus sp. and Bifidobacterium sp. inhibit pathogenic bacteria through competition for nutrients and adhesion sites, production of antimicrobial substances, and enhancement of the immune system3.
Lactobacillus acidophilus La-14 and Lactobacillus plantarum Lp-115 have displayed in vitro inhibition of common pathogens.
Probiotic + SB supports healthy digestive function and intestinal health. Specifically, SB supports gut integrity by enhancing the integrity of the tight junction between enterocytes, thus preserving intestinal integrity and function.
Immune health
Probiotic + SB helps maintain healthy immune function as the intestinal microbiota is one of the key elements in the body’s immune defence system. Probiotics have an ability to modulate both cellular and humoral immunity and can stimulate various aspects of the immune system, including the phagocytic function of macrophages, natural killer cells, monocytes and neutrophils4.
Bifidobacterium lactis BI-04 reduces the risk of mild upper respiratory tract infections. A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled parallel trial in healthy, active adults found that Bifidobacterium
lactis BI-04 2 billion CFU significantly reduced the risk of an upper respiratory illness episode compared to placebo (p=0.022)5.
Saccharomyces Boulardii (SB) & diarrhoea
SB has been investigated in numerous trials and been shown to reduce the incidence of antibiotic associated diarrhoea (AAD) as well as traveller’s diarrhoea.
The mechanism of action is not fully understood, however, it is thought that within the intestinal lumen, SB may interfere with pathogenic toxins, preserve cellular and intestinal physiology, interfere with pathogen attachment, interact with normal microbiota or assist in re-establishing short chain fatty acid levels. SB also acts as an immune regulator, both within the lumen and systemically.

The chosen strains show resistance to certain antibiotics and may be beneficial when taken with antibiotic therapy to minimise side-effects. Probiotic + SB should be taken during and for several weeks after antibiotic treatment. Several studies have shown that AAD can be delayed for up to two months in up to 38% of patients after antibiotics are discontinued11.
Oxalate-degrading ability
Oxalate is a common component of the human diet and is capable of collecting in the renal tissues and binding to calcium to form calcium oxalate crystals.
Probiotic strains in Probiotic + SB have shown the ability to degrade oxalate. The oxalate-degrading activity of Lactobacillus acidophilus La-14 was found to be 100%, while the oxalate-degrading activity of Lactobacillus plantarum Lp-115 was 40%.
