Several medications may deplete folate status, including antacids, PPIs, trimethoprim (antibiotic), pyrimethamine (antimalarial), triamterene (blood pressure), sulfasalazine (for ulcerative colitis) and oral contraceptives.
Caution with antiepileptic and anticonvulsant medications – folinic acid, methylfolate and vitamin B6 may reduce serum levels of these medications. Patients should take folate or any derivatives of folate such as folinic acid or methylfolate only under the supervision of a healthcare professional.
Caution with blood thinning medications – selenium and vitamin E may increase the risk of bleeding. Monitor.
Caution with penicillamine (detoxifying agent) – minerals can reduce absorption and efficacy. Separate doses by 2-3 hours.
Caution with quinolone and tetracycline antibiotics (e.g. Ciprofloxacin) – these drugs may form complexes with minerals which can reduce absorption of both. Take the drug at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after mineral supplements.
Caution with levothyroxine or antithyroid medications – minerals reduce the absorption and efficacy. Separate dose by at least 4 hours and monitor thyroid function.
Caution with sulfasalazine (antidiarrheal) – may bind with iron, reducing absorption of both. Separate dose by 2 hours.
Caution with lithium – concurrent administration of iodine and lithium can increase risk of toxicity. Monitor thyroid function.
Caution with cyclosporin (immunosuppressant) – vitamin E may increase or decrease serum drug levels. Monitor - drug dose may need to be adjusted accordingly.
Caution with aluminium-based antacids – vitamin C increases the amount of aluminium absorbed. Separate doses by at least 2 hours.

Co-administration with antibiotics may reduce side-effects – beneficial interaction likely.
Caution with antifungal medication – may decrease effectiveness of SB. Seperate dose.

Prostate Pro contains Flowens™, a unique, full-spectrum proprietary blend of Cranberry fruit (Vaccinium macrocarpon) that has been clinically studied to improve lower urinary tract symptoms typically associated with an enlarged prostate.
Prostate Pro contains Phytopin®, a pure and natural beta-sitosterol extract of phytosterols of exceptional quality. Phytopin® is derived from Pinus pinaster trees and standardised to 70% beta-sitosterol.
Beta-sitosterols work by binding to the prostate gland helping to reduce swelling and inflammation often seen in an enlarged prostate.
Prostate Pro also contains zinc to support prostate health and the powerful antioxidants selenium and lycopene to reduce free radical damage in the body.
Prostate
The prostate is a walnut-sized gland that is shaped like a donut. It surrounds the upper (prostatic) part of the urethra in men, just below the bladder. The main function of the prostate gland is secretory, producing an alkaline fluid that comprises approximately 70% of seminal fluid.
Enlargement of the prostate gland in ageing men is extremely common. It is estimated up to 50% of males have some enlargement by the age of 50 and the incidence increases at around 10% per decade, with up to 90% of males experiencing symptoms by the age of 851.
Prostate enlargement is influenced by a metabolite of testosterone
- dihydrotestosterone (DHT), a crucial mediator of prostatic growth. DHT is synthesised in the prostate gland from the circulating testosterone by the enzyme 5-alpha-reductase. DHT sticks to the androgen receptors and triggers a release of growth factors which are mitogenic to epithelial cells, initiating multiplication of cells ultimately leading to an enlarged prostate.
In effect, the enlarged prostate gland strangles the male urethra, leading to progressive and characteristic urinary tract disturbances and urinary symptoms.
Prostate health is commonly assessed using the International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS). The IPSS is an eight-question written screening tool for prostate health. The IPSS assesses urinary symptoms such as incomplete bladder emptying, urinary frequency, intermittency, urgency, weak stream, straining and nocturia (increased night waking to urinate), as well as overall quality of life.
Prostate health
Prostate Pro contains Flowens™, Phytopin® and zinc to support healthy prostate function and prostate health.
Flowens™ was clinically assessed in a 6-month randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled study in 124 male volunteers over the
age of 45 experiencing lower urinary tract symptoms, a prostate specific antigen (PSA) level <2.5ng/mL and an International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS) of between 8 and 19. Subjects in the study received either 250mg or 500mg of Flowens™ or placebo daily. At the completion of the study, both the 250mg and 500mg Flowens™ groups showed a significant, clinically meaningful reduction in lower urinary tract symptoms, demonstrated by a reduction of IPSS at the end of treatment versus baseline. Flowens™ delivered improvements in as little as 30 days with no side effects observed, also including sexual side effects2.
A 6-month randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial assessed the efficacy and safety of 130mg beta-sitosterol or placebo daily in 177 men with enlarged prostate. The primary symptoms and quality of life outcome measure were assessed using the IPSS scale, with peak urinary flow rate and post-void residual urinary volume also recorded. Significant improvements in IPSS symptoms were seen in the beta-sitosterol group compared to placebo, while a decrease in peak urinary flow rate and post-void residual urinary volume were noted3.
Zinc is highly concentrated in the prostate, and prostatic androgen metabolism is modified by the intracellular concentration of zinc, making this nutrient important in maintaining the physiological function and normal tissue structure of the prostate.
Urinary tract health
Prostate Pro supports urinary tract health in men.
In a randomised, double-blind placebo controlled trial, forty-two men aged 45 to 70 years experiencing lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) and elevated PSA were given a dried Cranberry extract
and evaluated at baseline, 3 and 6 months. At the conclusion of the study, all parameters of urination, average urinary flow rate,
prostate bladder voiding and post-void residual urine volumes were significantly improved in at least 70% of participants in the Cranberry group, while PSA scores improved in over 80% of participants compared to placebo4.

Prostate Pro contains Flowens™, a unique, full-spectrum proprietary blend of Cranberry fruit (Vaccinium macrocarpon) that has been clinically studied to improve lower urinary tract symptoms typically associated with an enlarged prostate.
Prostate Pro contains Phytopin®, a pure and natural beta-sitosterol extract of phytosterols of exceptional quality. Phytopin® is derived from Pinus pinaster trees and standardised to 70% beta-sitosterol.
Beta-sitosterols work by binding to the prostate gland helping to reduce swelling and inflammation often seen in an enlarged prostate.
Prostate Pro also contains zinc to support prostate health and the powerful antioxidants selenium and lycopene to reduce free radical damage in the body.
Prostate
The prostate is a walnut-sized gland that is shaped like a donut. It surrounds the upper (prostatic) part of the urethra in men, just below the bladder. The main function of the prostate gland is secretory, producing an alkaline fluid that comprises approximately 70% of seminal fluid.
Enlargement of the prostate gland in ageing men is extremely common. It is estimated up to 50% of males have some enlargement by the age of 50 and the incidence increases at around 10% per decade, with up to 90% of males experiencing symptoms by the age of 851.
Prostate enlargement is influenced by a metabolite of testosterone
- dihydrotestosterone (DHT), a crucial mediator of prostatic growth. DHT is synthesised in the prostate gland from the circulating testosterone by the enzyme 5-alpha-reductase. DHT sticks to the androgen receptors and triggers a release of growth factors which are mitogenic to epithelial cells, initiating multiplication of cells ultimately leading to an enlarged prostate.
In effect, the enlarged prostate gland strangles the male urethra, leading to progressive and characteristic urinary tract disturbances and urinary symptoms.
Prostate health is commonly assessed using the International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS). The IPSS is an eight-question written screening tool for prostate health. The IPSS assesses urinary symptoms such as incomplete bladder emptying, urinary frequency, intermittency, urgency, weak stream, straining and nocturia (increased night waking to urinate), as well as overall quality of life.
Prostate health
Prostate Pro contains Flowens™, Phytopin® and zinc to support healthy prostate function and prostate health.
Flowens™ was clinically assessed in a 6-month randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled study in 124 male volunteers over the
age of 45 experiencing lower urinary tract symptoms, a prostate specific antigen (PSA) level <2.5ng/mL and an International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS) of between 8 and 19. Subjects in the study received either 250mg or 500mg of Flowens™ or placebo daily. At the completion of the study, both the 250mg and 500mg Flowens™ groups showed a significant, clinically meaningful reduction in lower urinary tract symptoms, demonstrated by a reduction of IPSS at the end of treatment versus baseline. Flowens™ delivered improvements in as little as 30 days with no side effects observed, also including sexual side effects2.
A 6-month randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial assessed the efficacy and safety of 130mg beta-sitosterol or placebo daily in 177 men with enlarged prostate. The primary symptoms and quality of life outcome measure were assessed using the IPSS scale, with peak urinary flow rate and post-void residual urinary volume also recorded. Significant improvements in IPSS symptoms were seen in the beta-sitosterol group compared to placebo, while a decrease in peak urinary flow rate and post-void residual urinary volume were noted3.
Zinc is highly concentrated in the prostate, and prostatic androgen metabolism is modified by the intracellular concentration of zinc, making this nutrient important in maintaining the physiological function and normal tissue structure of the prostate.
Urinary tract health
Prostate Pro supports urinary tract health in men.
In a randomised, double-blind placebo controlled trial, forty-two men aged 45 to 70 years experiencing lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) and elevated PSA were given a dried Cranberry extract
and evaluated at baseline, 3 and 6 months. At the conclusion of the study, all parameters of urination, average urinary flow rate,
prostate bladder voiding and post-void residual urine volumes were significantly improved in at least 70% of participants in the Cranberry group, while PSA scores improved in over 80% of participants compared to placebo4.

With vitamin C & bioflavonoids
Quercetin Complex contains high-strength quercetin with vitamin C and bioflavonoids to support quercetin absorption and activity within the body.
Dietary flavonoids are divided into six subclasses according to their structural features: flavonols, flavones, isoflavones, flavanones, anthocyanidins and flavanols.
Quercetin is a flavone with potent antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activity. It is found in onions, apples, broccoli and berries, particularly in the fruit skins. Biosynthesis of quercetin is stimulated by light. Typical dietary intake of quercetin is 5-40mg per day.
Quercetin Complex contains rutin (also known as rutoside or quercetin-2-rutinoside), a flavonol abundant in plants such as Passionflower, buckwheat, tea and apples, and hesperidin, a flavanone found almost exclusively in citrus.
Quercetin Complex is a potent antioxidant to reduce free radicals formed in the body.
Allergy
An allergy occurs when the body overreacts to an allergen that is typically harmless to most people. An allergen enters the body
and is mistaken by the immune system as a dangerous substance, triggering the release of immunoglobulin E (IgE). When IgE antibodies come into contact with the allergen, they trigger a cascade of immune reactions, including the release of mast cell chemicals, particularly histamine. In small amounts, histamine causes itching and reddening of the local area; in larger amounts it can dilate blood vessels and cause swelling.
Mast cells mediate inflammatory and allergic responses. They store different chemical mediators, including histamine, interleukins and proteoglycans. Mast cells are located at the boundaries between body tissue and the external environment, including mucosal surfaces of the gut and lungs, in the skin and around blood vessels. Upon stimulation by an allergen, mast cells release chemicals into the surrounding tissues (degranulation), which produce the allergic reaction – increased permeability of blood vessels, inflammation and swelling and increased mucus production.
Allergic reactions are characterised by a disruption of helper T cell type 1 and 2. Th2 cytokines, especially IL-4, IL-5 and IL-13 play a major role in the development and maintenance of allergic responses.
Common allergies include allergic rhinitis (hayfever) and skin allergy.
Antihistamine
Quercetin is a potent antihistamine and exerts an anti-allergic effect in the body through the stabilisation of mast cell membranes and by inhibiting the release of histamine and other allergic and
inflammatory substances. The antihistamine activity of quercetin has been well documented in in vitro studies.
One study showed that quercetin inhibited histamine released from chemically and immunologically induced rat peritoneal mast cells by 95% and 97%, respectively1.
A study on nasal scrapings from 123 Japanese individuals suffering from allergic rhinitis found that exposure to quercetin inhibited histamine release by 46% to 96%2.

subsections.text:
Contraindicated with digoxin – quercetin may (theoretically) increase drug bioavailability.
Quercetin may induce CYP3A4, therefore caution is advised with medications chiefly metabolised by CYP3A4.
Caution with midazolam – quercetin may decrease blood concentrations of the drug. Use under professional supervision.
Caution with cyclosporin – quercetin may increase blood concentrations of the drug. Use under professional supervision.
Caution with antihypertensive drugs – quercetin may have additive effects. Monitor blood pressure.
Caution with diclofenac – quercetin may increase plasma levels and prolong the half life of the drug, which may increase effects and side-effects of the drug.
Caution with paclitaxel (antimetabolite) and pioglitazone (hypoglycaemic) – quercetin may increase bioavailability of drugs. Use under professional supervision.
Caution with quinolone antibiotics – quercetin may compete with quinolone antibiotic binding sites.
Caution with aluminium-based antacids – vitamin C increases the amount of aluminium absorbed. Separate dose by at least 2 hours.
Caution with warfarin – Quercetin Complex may increase the risk of bleeding (theoretical).
Caution with iron supplements – quercetin is an iron chelator. Seperate dose by 2 hours.

subsections.heading: TECHNICAL INFORMATION
subsections.text:
Raspberry leaf, taken during the third trimester of pregnancy, has been used for centuries in traditional herbal medicine to prepare the uterus for labour.
Raspberry is a popular fruit grown in Eastern Europe and suited to Polish climatic conditions1. Herbs of Gold Raspberry Leaf contains Raspberry leaf sourced from Poland. It is processed via a 100% water extraction method, leaving a pure, alcohol-free extract suitable for pregnant and lactation women.
Herbs of Gold Raspberry leaf contains 2g of herb per tablet and is suitable for women to take from the 30th week of pregnancy and during breastfeeding.
Raspberry leaf has a high tannin content, between 13% and 15% which gives it an astringent action, making it useful in diarrhoea. It also contains phenolic compounds including the flavonoids rutin and quercetin.
Prepare the uterus for childbirth
Raspberry leaf is traditionally used in Western herbal medicine to prepare the body for labour. To date, no high-quality studies exist, but evidence from in vitro and in vivo studies have supported the traditional use. Raspberry leaf has demonstrated variable effects on uterine muscle tone acting as both a stimulant and a relaxant to
uterine musculature. Antispasmodic activity helps to relax the uterine wall while smooth muscle stimulant activity may help to promote regular contractions2.
It is also hypothesised that Raspberry leaf may increase blood flow to the uterus and aid the uterine muscle fibres with more organised contractions.
In a double-blind trial of 92 women, Raspberry leaf consumed from 32 weeks gestation until labour was associated with a lower rate of interventions with no adverse effects noted for both mother or baby. Whilst Raspberry leaf did not shorten the first stage of labour, it did significantly reduce the second stage (mean difference 9.59 minutes) and produce a lower rate of forceps delivery (19.3% versus 30.4% in placebo)3.
In another study, Raspberry leaf shortened the 1st stage of labour with no identifiable side effects for mother or child. The percentage of normal births in the Raspberry leaf group (77.2%) was slightly larger than the percentage in the control group (66.7%). The authors determined that women who ingest Raspberry leaf might be less likely to receive an artificial rupture of their membranes, or require a caesarean section, forceps or vacuum birth than the women in the control group4.
Raspberry leaf has been traditionally used in Western herbal medicine as a uterine tonic for centuries.

Resveratrol is a phenolic phytochemical that is present in Grape skin, red wine, berries and peanuts. The highest level of naturally occurring resveratrol is found in the roots of Japanese knotweed, a traditional herb used in Chinese medicine.
Resveratrol can exist as one of two isomers: trans-resveratrol and
cis-resveratrol. Trans-resveratrol is commonly seen as the active form of resveratrol and many actions seen from trans-resveratrol are not seen with cis-resveratrol. Both forms are bioactive, however, most
of the research focuses on trans-resveratrol. Resveratrol AdvantAGE contains 250mg of trans-resveratrol sourced from Japanese knotweed.
Resveratrol is a potent antioxidant with the ability to act as a direct antioxidant and an indirect cellular antioxidant system inducer through modulation of several cellular antioxidant pathways. Antioxidants are molecules that inhibit oxidation of other molecules. Direct antioxidants bind directly to free radicals, whereas indirect antioxidants recycle direct antioxidants and help cells produce antioxidant enzymes.
Oxidation is a chemical reaction that can produce free radicals in the body. These free radicals can start a chain reaction that potentially leads to damage within DNA, proteins and lipids in cell membranes.
Resveratrol is thought to be the nutrient responsible for the ‘French Paradox’ hypothesis. Resveratrol intake is high in the Mediterranean diet. The Mediterranean diet is linked to improved cardiovascular health, and the high intake of resveratrol may contribute to this.
Resveratrol AdvantAGE contains vitamin C and zinc to support healthy immune system function.
Healthy ageing
Free radicals are thought to contribute to the ageing process and are linked to ageing in various tissues where there is increased oxidative stress.
Resveratrol has the potential to support healthy ageing by stimulating the SIRT1 (silent information regulator two) gene. SIRT1 is an enzyme involved in cellular regulation and promotes the long-term survival of irreplaceable cells.
Blood vessel health
Resveratrol AdvantAGE supports blood vessel, capillary and cardiovascular health. Oxidative stress is a key player in the pathogenesis of vascular dysfunction and the inactivation of nitric oxide (NO) by reactive oxygen species (ROS) is known be a crucial factor in reducing NO bioavailability and the development of
endothelial dysfunction. Resveratrol helps maintain blood vessel dilation.
Resveratrol has been shown to induce major cellular antioxidant enzymes, such as glutathione peroxidase, heme oxygenase and superoxide dismutase in cardiovascular cells, leading to a marked decrease in oxidative stress1.
In vitro studies and studies in preclinical models demonstrated vasculoprotective effects of resveratrol. Positive effects of resveratrol were seen in both experimental animals and in humans, including alleviation of oxidative stress and inflammation, enhancement of metabolic capacity, increased NO synthesis, suppression of vascular smooth muscle cell proliferation and increased autophagy2.
Vitamin C is required for the synthesis of collagen, an important structural component of blood vessels.
Rutin is a flavonoid with antioxidant activity that helps increase the bioavailability of vitamin C in the body. Rutin helps to maintain the health and strength of capillaries by decreasing fragility and permeability.
Skin health
Resveratrol AdvantAGE contains vitamin C and zinc to maintain collagen, connective tissue and skin health.
Vitamin C is a potent free radical scavenger and a physiological part of the antioxidant system in human skin.
Vitamin C is required as a cofactor in the synthesis of collagen. It is involved in the conversion of proline and lysine to hydroxyproline and hydroxylysine which are components of collagen structures. Collagen is an essential component of connective tissue and skin.
Zinc is an essential trace element abundant in connective tissues. It is involved in connective tissue and collagen formation to help maintain healthy skin. Both zinc and vitamin C support wound healing.
Lysine, proline and glycine are important amino acids that form collagen structures in the body.

Resveratrol is thought to be the nutrient responsible for the ‘French Paradox’ hypothesis. Resveratrol intake is high in the Mediterranean diet. The Mediterranean diet is linked to improved cardiovascular health, and the high intake of resveratrol may contribute to this.
Resveratrol AdvantAGE contains vitamin C and zinc to support healthy immune system function.
Healthy ageing
Free radicals are thought to contribute to the ageing process and are linked to ageing in various tissues where there is increased oxidative stress.
Resveratrol has the potential to support healthy ageing by stimulating the SIRT1 (silent information regulator two) gene. SIRT1 is an enzyme involved in cellular regulation and promotes the long-term survival of irreplaceable cells.
Blood vessel health
Resveratrol AdvantAGE supports blood vessel, capillary and cardiovascular health. Oxidative stress is a key player in the pathogenesis of vascular dysfunction and the inactivation of nitric oxide (NO) by reactive oxygen species (ROS) is known be a crucial factor in reducing NO bioavailability and the development of
endothelial dysfunction. Resveratrol helps maintain blood vessel dilation.
Resveratrol has been shown to induce major cellular antioxidant enzymes, such as glutathione peroxidase, heme oxygenase and superoxide dismutase in cardiovascular cells, leading to a marked decrease in oxidative stress1.
In vitro studies and studies in preclinical models demonstrated vasculoprotective effects of resveratrol. Positive effects of resveratrol were seen in both experimental animals and in humans, including alleviation of oxidative stress and inflammation, enhancement of metabolic capacity, increased NO synthesis, suppression of vascular smooth muscle cell proliferation and increased autophagy2.
Vitamin C is required for the synthesis of collagen, an important structural component of blood vessels.
Rutin is a flavonoid with antioxidant activity that helps increase the bioavailability of vitamin C in the body. Rutin helps to maintain the health and strength of capillaries by decreasing fragility and permeability.
Skin health
Resveratrol AdvantAGE contains vitamin C and zinc to maintain collagen, connective tissue and skin health.
Vitamin C is a potent free radical scavenger and a physiological part of the antioxidant system in human skin.
Vitamin C is required as a cofactor in the synthesis of collagen. It is involved in the conversion of proline and lysine to hydroxyproline and hydroxylysine which are components of collagen structures. Collagen is an essential component of connective tissue and skin.
Zinc is an essential trace element abundant in connective tissues. It is involved in connective tissue and collagen formation to help maintain healthy skin. Both zinc and vitamin C support wound healing.
Lysine, proline and glycine are important amino acids that form collagen structures in the body.

Sea buckthorn has a long history of medicinal use in Asia, India and Europe. In modern times, the oil of Sea buckthorn is popularly used cosmetically for skin and nutritionally in supplements for its ample source of health-promoting constituents.
Its genus name, Hippophae, originates from the Greek words, hippo, which means horse, and phasos, meaning to shine, due to the fact that its leaves and young branches were used as fodder for racehorses to improve the shininess of their coat1.
Sea buckthorn oil is derived from the fruit or seed and is highly nutritional, enriched with unsaturated fatty acids such as omega-3 (alpha-linolenic acid), omega-6 (linoleic acid), omega-7 (palmitoleic) and omega-9 (oleic acid) as well as vitamin E (tocotrienols
and tocopherols), carotenoids (betacarotene, lycopene, lutein and zeaxanthin), plant sterols (campsterol and beta-sitosterol) and flavonoids (quercetin and kaempferol), all of which work synergistically to exert anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects2.
The bioactive constituent profiles of the fruit and seed oil vary considerably. The seed oil is particularly rich in omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acids whereas the fruit oil is predominantly high in carotenoids and omega-7, a rare fatty acid found in nature. Sea buckthorn contains the highest amount of omega-7 of any plant in nature and is found exclusively in the fruit3.
Herbs of Gold Sea Buckthorn oil combines fruit and seed oil to capture its comprehensive nutritional profile and align with
compositions used in clinical studies to ensure potency and efficacy.
Omega 3, 6, 7 and 9 fatty acids
Herbs of Gold Sea Buckthorn Oil contains a balance of omega-3, 6, 7 and 9 fatty acids to maintain beneficial fatty acid levels in the body and support general health and wellbeing.
Omega-3 and omega-6 are polyunsaturated fatty acids that are necessary for good health and development, particularly for maintaining skin barrier health and mediating the inflammatory
response. They are essential because the body cannot produce them, so adequate amounts must be consumed in the diet.
Omega-3 is responsible for ameliorating inflammatory processes in the skin by spurring the generation of anti-inflammatory compounds.
Omega-6 has a specific and unique role in the structural integrity of the skin as it is a direct precursor of ceramides. Ceramides
are another lipid species predominantly found in the epidermis (outermost layer) of the skin that play a major role in moisturising and strengthening the protective barrier of the skin4.
A greater ratio of omega-6 to omega-3 increases the risk of a pro-inflammatory state. Therefore, it is recommended that omega-6 and omega-3 is consumed in a 1:1-2:1 ratio for optimal health5. Sea
buckthorn oil provides an omega-3:omega-6 ratio of 1:1, representing an ideal balance for health.
Omega-7 and omega-9 are monounsaturated fatty acids and, unlike omega-3 and omega-6, can be synthesised by the body. Omega-9 is necessary for mediating cholesterol synthesis, supporting good eye health and is an important component of the lipid-rich myelin sheath surrounding nerves6. Omega-7 serves as a fundamental structural component of skin and mucous membranes7,8.
Omegia™ Sea buckthorn oil
Omegia™ Sea buckthorn oil is a high-grade, proprietary ingredient containing a specific blend of fruit and seed oil to provide a balance of omega-3, 6, 7 and 9 fatty acids to guarantee therapeutic efficacy. This is important as its bioactive constituents are greatly influenced by growing conditions, time of harvest, fruit colour, post-harvest processing and storing procedures.
Omegia™ Sea buckthorn oil is derived from wild-harvested and sustainably sourced Sea buckthorn grown on the pristine region of the Tibetan Plateau. The Tibetan Plateau is regarded as one of the cleanest and most well-preserved ecosystems in the world, an environment ideal for growing Sea buckthorn.
Omegia™ Sea buckthorn oil is extracted using supercritical carbon dioxide (CO2). Supercritical CO2 extraction is the cleanest, most environmentally-friendly and efficient means to extract Sea buckthorn oil, while preserving its therapeutic integrity.
Omegia™ Sea buckthorn oil is certified organic and GMO-free.

subsections.heading: TECHNICAL INFORMATION
subsections.text:
Selenium is an essential trace mineral that is required for the proper functioning of several selenium-dependent enzymes known as selenoproteins.
Selenium plays an integral role in the body’s antioxidant systems. It is a component of the five glutathione peroxidase enzymes: GPx1-4 and GPx6. The glutathione peroxidases are involved in catalysing, reducing and deactivating free radicals and other potential oxidants. Turnover and loss of selenium is accelerated during times of increased oxidative stress. Strenuous exercise, cigarette smoking, increased exposure to environmental chemicals and chronic illness increase selenium requirements.
Selenium absorption
Selenium can be found naturally in a variety of foods, including wheatgerm, meats, seafood, Brazil nuts and garlic. However, there is a large variation in the selenium content in food, as it is dependent on the amount of selenium present in the soil used to grow the food. Humans can absorb approximately 55-70% of selenium in foods1.
There are two primary forms of supplemental selenium – an organic selenium (including selenomethionine) and inorganic selenium. Sodium selenite and sodium selenate are inorganic forms of selenium. These forms are found in soil and water and are used by plants and animals to synthesise the organic forms of selenium that then enter the human food chain. Other forms of selenium, including malt selenium and selenium yeast, take inorganic selenium (usually sodium selenite) and bio-transform it into organic selenium.
Generally, organic forms of selenium are better absorbed in the body than inorganic forms. The human body can absorb more than 90%
of selenomethionine, but only about 50% of selenium from selenite2. A supplemental trial in a low-selenium area of China found that selenium as selenomethionine had nearly twice the bioavailability of selenium as selenite3.
Herbs of Gold Selenium 150 MAX contains selenomethionine, an organic form of selenium where the selenium is bound to the amino acid methionine. Selenomethionine is synthesised by plants and is the major form of selenium in the human diet. Selenomethionine is known to be very well-absorbed. In one study in selenium-replete individuals, supplementation with 158 micrograms of selenium from selenomethionine increased plasma selenium concentrations by 71%4.
Thyroid hormones
Selenium is an essential element for normal development, growth and metabolism through the regulation of thyroid hormones.
Selenium plays a major role in the synthesis and metabolism of thyroid hormones. The thyroid gland has a higher concentration of selenium than any other organ in the body. Selenium is an essential
component of the enzyme iodothyronine deiodinase, which converts thyroxine (T4) to triiodothyronine (T3).
Immune function
Selenium 150 MAX supports healthy immune system function.
Selenium is found in high amounts in immune tissues, including the liver, spleen and lymph nodes and substantial evidence shows selenium deficiency is associated with loss of immunocompetence. Both cell-mediated immunity and B-cell function is impaired by selenium deficiency5.
Selenium supplementation may enhance Th1-type immune responses to a greater extent than Th2-type responses. Studies in humans suggest that supplementation may enhance immunity, including both humoral and cell-mediated responses6.
Sperm health
Selenium 150 MAX maintains male reproductive health by supporting sperm health. Selenium is required for testosterone synthesis, normal sperm maturation and sperm motility.
Proper spermatogenesis requires two selenoproteins: phospholipid peroxide glutathione peroxidase (PHGPx) and selenoprotein P7.
In the testes, a high concentration of selenium occurs mainly in the form of GPx4, where it acts as an antioxidant to protect developing sperm cells from oxidative DNA damage8.

Hair, Skin & Nails
The skin is the largest organ of the human body and is a good indicator of general health. The skin functions as a waterproof wrapping for the entire body and is the first line of defence against bacteria and other organisms. It helps to cool the body, via sweat, and provides information about pain, pleasure, pressure and temperature.
The skin is made up of three layers: the epidermis, dermis and subcutis. The epidermis is the outermost layer and contains melanin, the pigment that gives skin its colour. The dermis is made up of elastin, for suppleness, and collagen, for strength. It contains sweat glands, sebaceous glands, hair follicles, blood vessels and nerves. The subcutis is the layer of fat that sits under the dermis, proving insulation and mechanical protection.
Hair and nails are manufactured by cells in the epidermis. They work with the skin to protect the body from injury and help regulate temperature. Hair, nails and the outer layer of skin are made up of a protein called keratin.
Hair grows approximately one centimetre every month. It grows in cycles, with each follicle producing hair for a few months to years, before the bulb undergoes spontaneous involution and the hair is shed. Hair length is determined by the duration of the growth phase.
Nails are made from skin cells. The nail bed and the nail matrix under the cuticle are live cells, but the nail itself is made from dead cells.
Silica
Silica is the general term for inorganic compounds containing silicon and oxygen. Silicon rarely occurs as a free element in nature as it forms strong bonds with oxygen and generally exists as silica or silicate compounds.
Silicon is the second most abundant element in the earth’s crust, following oxygen, and the third most abundant trace element in the
human body. Silicon is present in all body tissues but the tissues with the highest concentration of silicon are connective tissues including bone, skin, hair, arteries and nails.
To-date there has been no Recommended Dietary Intake (RDI) set for silicon. This is due to a lack of data on the metabolic role and the consequences of restriction in the diet of both laboratory animals and humans. However, this mineral is increasingly recognised for its beneficial effect on connective tissues and bone health.
Dietary sources of silica include whole grains, beer and green beans. Although plant foods contain high levels of silicon, the bioavailability of this mineral can be quite low due to poor solubility. The average silicon update from foods is estimated to be 41% 1, however, it varies significantly depending on the food source. Interestingly, beer is a good source of highly bioavailable silicon as the silicon in barley and hops is solubilised during the beer-making process. One study found that the absorption of silicon from beer was 64% compared to only 44% from green beans and just 4% from bananas2.
The daily intake of silicon in the Western world is approximately 20-50mg/day, although it is lower in women and decreases with
age3. Diets high in animal fat and protein and low in plant foods are generally low in silicon. Low silicon intake can lead to poor hair, nail and skin quality and skeletal abnormalities.
Water-soluble forms of silicon are absorbed in the intestinal tract and any excess is eliminated by the kidneys within 4-8 hours of ingestion. Therefore, it is unlikely that silicon will accumulate in excessive amounts in healthy individuals. To-date, no evidence of adverse effects from silicon have been found.
Skin
Silica Hair Skin & Nails contains key nutrients to support skin health.
Silica is important for skin health, supporting skin structure, elasticity and integrity. It is bound to glycosaminoglycans and is involved in the formation of cross-links between collagen and proteoglycans.
An open, uncontrolled study found that colloidal silicic acid internally and applied topically to the face improved the thickness and turgor of the skin. After 90 days, the mean epidermal thickness increased by 0.03mm (19%) and the dermal thickness by 0.26mm (29%) and skin elasticity index increased from 55% to 60%4.

subsections.heading: DRUG INTERACTIONS
subsections.text:
Contraindicated with retinoid medication (including acitretin, isotretinoin, accutane or roaccutane) - vitamin A supplements should not be taken concurrently due to potential vitamin A toxicity.
Caution with oral contraceptives - concurrent use may increase vitamin A levels.
Caution with eltrombopag - zinc may form chelates with and reduce the absorption of the drug. Separate dose by at least 4 hours.
Caution with NSAIDs, cefalexin, penacillamine and quinolone and tetracycline antibiotics – zinc interferes with absorption. Separate dose by 3 hours.
Caution with aspirin and paracetamol – zinc and vitamin A may reduce their effectiveness. Separate dose by 2 hours.
Caution with calcium supplements – zinc and calcium compete for common intestinal absorption sites. Separate supplements by at least 2 hours.
Caution with chemotherapeutic agents – evidence regarding the use of vitamin C in conjunction with chemotherapy treatment is still emerging. Use only under medical supervision.
Caution with aluminium based antacids – vitamin C increases the amount of aluminium absorbed. Separate dose by 2 hours.

subsections.heading: CAUTIONS
subsections.text:
Not recommended in pregnancy or breastfeeding due to the high dose of vitamin A and silica.
Individuals with liver or renal disease, or alcoholism should use vitamin A supplements with caution.
Caution in iron overload conditions, such as haemochromatosis, as vitamin C can increase iron absorption.
Biotin shares the sodium-dependent multivitamin transporter (SMVT) with vitamin B5. Theoretically, this may reduce vitamin B5 absorption due to competitive inhibition of the transporter.

subsections.heading: SIDE EFFECTS
subsections.text: Zinc may cause gastrointestinal disturbance, including nausea, when taken on an empty stomach (usually only seen in higher doses). Taking the product with food reduces this likelihood.

Skin health
Connective tissue health
Silica Hair Solution combines high-strength silica and biotin with antioxidants selenium and zinc to support healthy connective tissues, including hair, skin, nails and bone.
Silica Hair Solution contains selenium and zinc, potent antioxidants to reduce free radicals formed in the body. Selenium is an important component of antioxidant enzymes glutathione peroxidases, thioredoxin reductase and iodothyronine deiodinases. Zinc contributes to the antioxidant enzyme superoxide dismutase, which forms the front line of defence against reactive oxygen species (ROS)-mediated injury1.
Zinc and selenium support healthy immune system function and are involved in mediating both innate and acquired immunity. Zinc is important for mediating non-specific immunity (including neutrophils, monocytes and natural killer cells) and for the development of acquired immunity.

Hair health
Silica Hair Solution supports hair health and helps maintain hair strength and thickness.
Silicon is present in 1-10 ppm in hair and in the epicuticle of hair. It has been suggested that strands of hair with higher silicon content tend to have lower falling rate and higher brightness4.
An open, uncontrolled study investigated the effects of 10mL of colloidal silicic acid in women with thin hair. Thin hair was observed in 17 patients before treatment (mean score 1.8) and in seven after treatment (mean score 0.9), the difference is statistically significant (p<0.01)5.
A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled study found that 10mg of choline-stabilised orthosilicic acid for 9 months positively affected tensile strength, including elasticity and break load, and resulted in thicker hair6.

subsections.heading: TECHNICAL INFORMATION
subsections.text:
Relieves restlessness
Synergistic formula
Relieves mild anxiety
Sedative herbs
Flexible dosing
Sleep Ease contains four herbs from Western and Eastern traditional medicine systems to promote sleep and relieve symptoms of mild anxiety.
The herbs in Sleep Ease work on the gamma aminobutyric acid (GABA) receptors. GABA is a naturally occurring amino acid that works as an inhibitory neurotransmitter in the brain. GABA inhibits certain brain signals and decreases activity in the nervous system, producing a calming effect.
Sleep
Sleep is an essential process that refreshes the mind and allows the body to repair. Today, many people do not get the recommended 7-9 hours of sleep each night, sleeping for 6-7 hours or less.
Poor sleep leads to fatigue, poor concentration and memory, mood disturbances, impaired judgement and reaction time and poor coordination. Lack of sleep long term is associated with poor health outcomes.
Poor sleep can be caused by many factors, including shift work, travel across time zones, illness, some medications, internet and social media usage and poor sleep hygiene.
Sleep occurs in phases. Rapid eye movement (REM) sleep occurs regularly during sleep, about once every 90-120 minutes and is the time where most dreams occur. Non-REM sleep makes up about 75% of sleep time and is broken down into stages:
Stage 1 – drowsiness, somewhere between asleep and awake
Stage 2 – loss of awareness of surroundings, body temperature drops and breathing and heart rate slow
Stage 3 & 4 (deep sleep/‘delta sleep’) – heart rate and breathing slow, muscles relax. This is the time body growth and repair takes place.
Promoting sleep
Sleep Ease contains traditional herbs to promote sleep and relieve sleeplessness.
Sleep Ease contains high-strength Ziziphus, traditionally used in Chinese medicine (TCM) to calm the mind, to decrease disturbed or restless sleep and to promote refreshing sleep. It has been used for more than 2500 years in Chinese medicine as a sedative and
Chen, J. K. & Chen, T. T. (2004). Chinese Medical Herbology and Pharmacology. Art of Medicine Press.
hypnotic agent. In Chinese medicine, it is considered to calm the heart and spirit.
The Chinese Medical Herbology and Pharmacology states that Ziziphus is good for both difficulty falling asleep and staying asleep as well as for excessive dreaming and shallow sleep with a tendency to wake easily1.
Ziziphus is believed to exert its effects by decreasing the monoaminergic system activity. The active components of the herb have been identified as alkaloids, flavonoids and saponins, in particular jujubosides. An animal study found that the flavonoids and saponins of Ziziphus significantly reduced waking time and prolonged sleeping time in mice2.
Sleep Ease also contains Magnolia. Much research has focused on the combination of Ziziphus spinosa and Magnolia officinalis.
Magnolia has been used in Chinese medicine for over 2000 years and is regarded as a potent herb with a wide range of biological and pharmacological effects. However, only recently has there been interest in its potential sedative and anxiolytic effects.
Animal studies have shown that Magnolia may have sleep-promoting properties. The active constituents in Magnolia stem bark are magnolol and honokiol. It has been reported that magnolol increases the number of binding sites and affinity of the GABAA receptor for GABA and enhances chloride influx. Therefore, it is hypothesised that magnolol may enhance the inhibitory action of GABA on GABAA receptors by binding to the sites in GABAA receptors3.

Passionflower is traditionally used in WHM to promote sleep quality and deep sleep and to enhance refreshing sleep. It is indicated specifically for sleeplessness due to mental worry or overwork.
The King’s American Dispensatory (1898) describes Passionflower as “a rest-producing agent…specifically useful to allay restlessness and overcome wakefulness, when these are the result of exhaustion, or the nervous excitement of debility…It gives sleep to those who are

Sleep Ease contains four herbs from Western and Eastern traditional medicine systems to promote sleep and relieve symptoms of mild anxiety.
The herbs in Sleep Ease work on the gamma aminobutyric acid (GABA) receptors. GABA is a naturally occurring amino acid that works as an inhibitory neurotransmitter in the brain. GABA inhibits certain brain signals and decreases activity in the nervous system, producing a calming effect.
Sleep
Sleep is an essential process that refreshes the mind and allows the body to repair. Today, many people do not get the recommended 7-9 hours of sleep each night, sleeping for 6-7 hours or less.
Poor sleep leads to fatigue, poor concentration and memory, mood disturbances, impaired judgement and reaction time and poor coordination. Lack of sleep long term is associated with poor health outcomes.
Poor sleep can be caused by many factors, including shift work, travel across time zones, illness, some medications, internet and social media usage and poor sleep hygiene.
Sleep occurs in phases. Rapid eye movement (REM) sleep occurs regularly during sleep, about once every 90-120 minutes and is the time where most dreams occur. Non-REM sleep makes up about 75% of sleep time and is broken down into stages:
Stage 1 – drowsiness, somewhere between asleep and awake
Stage 2 – loss of awareness of surroundings, body temperature drops and breathing and heart rate slow
Stage 3 & 4 (deep sleep/‘delta sleep’) – heart rate and breathing slow, muscles relax. This is the time body growth and repair takes place.

Slippery elm has been used medicinally for many years by the Native American tribes and European settlers. It was often mixed with
water and applied topically to wounds and skin irritation, and taken internally for coughs and gastrointestinal complaints.
Slippery elm has not been significantly investigated in clinical studies, so most information comes from traditional usage and known constituents in the herb.
Slippery elm contains mucilage, glucose, polyuronides, tannins, galacturonic acid, L-rhamnose, D-galactose, starches, fat, phytosterols, sesquiterpenes, oxalate acid, flavonoids, salicyclic acid, capric acid, caprylic acid, decanoic acid and cholesterol. The bark is highly nutritious, containing a variety of nutrients including calcium, iron, vitamin C, thiamine, zinc, magnesium and potassium. Traditionally, it was used as a nutritious gruel and nutritive tonic.
The name Slippery Elm refers to the slippery consistency of the herb when it is mixed with water.
Slippery Elm 400mg contains Slippery elm in a vegetarian capsule. Capsules are a better option than tablets, which can bind with water and swell, making ingestion difficult. The capsules are broken down in the stomach, releasing free Slippery elm powder, allowing it to exert its effect over the stomach and intestines (lower digestive system).
Demulcent
Slippery elm is a demulcent to soothe irritated tissues. The inner stem bark of Slippery elm is highly mucilaginous.
Mucilages are hydrophilic (water loving) and can trap water in their structure to form a gel. Consequently, when mucilage is mixed with water it swells to many times its original volume as it absorbs water. Slippery elm mixed with water forms a thick gel-like substance, which coats the digestive system, forming a protective barrier.
Slippery elm is traditionally used in Western herbal medicine as a demulcent to sooth irritated tissues, including gastro-intestinal tract mucous membranes.
Grieves (1931) says of Slippery elm, it “has a most soothing and healing action on all the parts it comes in contact with” and “makes an excellent drink in cases of irritation of the mucous membrane of the stomach and intestines”1.
Digestion
Slippery elm supports digestive system health and maintains healthy mucous linings of the digestive system.
When taken internally, Slippery elm mucilage forms a physical barrier, protecting the lining of the GIT and soothing irritation or inflammation of mucous membranes in the digestive tract.
Preliminary evidence shows that Slippery elm may cause reflex stimulation of nerve endings in the gastrointestinal tract, leading to increased mucous secretion, which helps protect the GIT against excess acidity.
Slippery elm also acts as a fibre and prebiotic, encouraging the growth of healthy bacteria in the gut and acting as a bulk laxative.

subsections.text: The mucilage content of Slippery elm may (theoretically) slow the absorption of oral drugs and reduce serum levels. Caution is needed with drugs with a narrow therapeutic index (including barbiturates, digoxin, lithium, phenytoin and warfarin). Separate dose by 2 hours.

Clinical research shows hyperforin and its structural analogue adhyperforin have an inhibitory effect on the neuronal uptake of serotonin, noradrenaline and dopamine, as well as gamma

Extensive research has been conducted on St John’s wort and its medicinal powers continue to be of great interest to modern science and medicine.
Nervous system & mild anxiety
St John's wort is traditionally used in Western herbal medicine to relieve symptoms of mild anxiety. It is also used traditionally to reduce nervous tension, relive restlessness, support a healthy nervous system, relieve irritability and as a calmative to soothe and calm the nerves.
St John’s wort has been considered a medicinally valuable plant for over 2000 years, prescribed for use in overexcitation and commonly referred to as the “arnica for the nerves”.
Healthy mood & emotional wellbeing
St John’s wort is well recognised for its role in supporting healthy mood balance and emotional wellbeing.
While the exact mode of action of St John’s wort is still being investigated, St John’s wort has demonstrated to be a weak inhibitor of monoamine oxidase A and B activity, inhibiting the synaptosomal uptake of serotonin, dopamine and noradrenaline (norepinephrine) with approximately equal affinity. In vitro binding assays carried out using St John’s wort extract have also demonstrated significant affinity for adenosine, GABAA, GABAB and glutamate receptors. In vivo, St John’s wort extract shows a downregulation of β-adrenergic receptors and an upregulation of serotonin 5-HT2 receptors in the rat frontal cortex, causing changes in neurotransmitter concentrations in brain areas that are implicated in low mood2.
A systematic review of the efficacy of St John’s wort was conducted in 2016. Thirty-five studies including a total of 6993 patients met inclusion criteria; with eight of those studies evaluating a hypericum

subsections.heading: DRUG INTERACTIONS
subsections.text:
St John’s wort, particularly hyperforin, induces the CYP450 enzyme system, and should not be used with drugs metabolised through this pathway, including indianvir, cyclosporin, oral contraceptives, digoxin, theophylline, HIV protease inhibitors, HIV non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors, methadone, antineoplastic drugs, anticonvulsants (phenobarbiton, phenytoin), antidepressants, tacrolimus, omeprazole, midazolam, alprazolam and carbamazepine (tegretol).
Contraindicated with anticoagulants warfarin (coumadin, marevan) and phenprocoumon - St John’s wort may decrease pro-thrombin time and international normalised ratio (INR) values. Monitor.
Contraindicated with oral contraceptives. St John’s wort may decrease efficacy and increase risk of ovulation and pregnancy.

Contraindicated during pregnancy and lactation.
Discontinue use at least one week prior to any general anaesthetic.
Avoid St John’s wort in combination with tyramine-rich foods and beverages – coadministration may cause elevated blood pressure and rapid heart rate. Tyramine-rich foods include aged cheeses, cured meats, fermented foods, dried fruits, beer and red wine.

St Mary’s thistle, also referred to as Milk thistle, is a plant native to the Mediterranean region belonging to the Asteraceae family and has been used for centuries as a medicinal herb for liver health.
Silymarin is extracted from the dried seeds of the St Mary’s thistle plant. Silymarin is the active constituent present and consists of a complex of seven flavanolignans (silybin A, silybin B, isosilibin A, isosilibin B, silichristin, isosilichristin, silidianin) and one flavonoid, (taxifolin). Together, silybin A and silybin B make up 50-70% of silymarin.
St Mary’s Thistle 35 000 is a standardised extract containing 80-88% flavanolignans calculated as 400mg of silybin per tablet.
Liver
The liver is located in the upper right quadrant of the abdomen and is responsible for numerous biochemical functions in the body, including the synthesis of clotting factors, metabolism of alcohol and other drugs, detoxification, conjugation and secretion of bilirubin, synthesis of bile salts and cholesterol and fatty acid metabolism.
The gallbladder is a small sac that sits under the liver and stores the bile produced by the liver. It extracts water from its store of bile, concentrating the liquid. The presence of fatty foods triggers the gallbladder to release bile into the intestine to help digest the fat.
Poor diet, especially a high fat diet, and excess alcohol or medication use can affect the biliary system. Some common symptoms of poor liver function include nausea, especially after a high fat meal, fatigue, pale stools, itchy skin and jaundice.
Liver health
St Mary’s thistle has a long history of use as a liver herb and is well-documented in traditional texts for treating “congestion of the
liver, spleen and kidneys”1. Traditionally, in Western herbal medicine (WHM), it is considered a hepatoprotective, to help protect the liver from damage, and as a trophoresorative to repair and regenerate liver cells.
St Mary’s thistle is also traditionally considered to be a choloretic and chologague to stimulate bile production in the liver and bile secretion from the gallbladder.
St Mary’s thistle supports healthy liver function and maintains liver health.
St Mary’s thistle is suitable to be taken long-term to support liver health. Health Canada recommend a minimum of three weeks use to see beneficial effects2, however, studies are done over a longer period of time, usually 8 weeks to 6 months.
The hepatoprotective effects are attributed to silymarin, which acts primarily as an antioxidant. Silymarin reduces the production of reactive oxygen species and lipid peroxidation, while increasing the concentration of antioxidant enzymes. Silymarin helps protect the liver as it binds to receptors on liver cells, stabilising cell membranes and preventing the entry of toxic substances into the cells.
Silymarin has been shown to accelerate the regeneration of hepatocytes after liver damage in an in vivo animal study. Silymarin enhanced liver regeneration by accelerating the cell cycle in rats after a partial hepatectomy3.
A meta-analysis of 8 randomised clinical trials involving 587 patients concluded that 210-1120mg/day of silymarin can improve liver function by lowering aminotransferase (AST) and alanine transaminase (ALT) enzymes4.
In an 8-week randomised, placebo-controlled study, 64 subjects were divided into either the case group receiving 210mg/day of silymarin (n=33) or placebo group (n=31). Results showed a decrease in liver enzymes in the silymarin group compared to placebo group and baseline levels, with a statistically significant reduction (p≤0.05) in AST and ALT5.
In another randomised, placebo-controlled trial, 50 subjects received 280mg/day silymarin or placebo. Liver function tests were evaluated every 4 weeks. Although no significant differences were found between silymarin and placebo in decreasing the mean ALT level after therapy, a significantly greater number of subjects had normal ALT after receiving silymarin for 6 months: 52% versus 18% (p<0.001). AST normalisation was more significant in the silymarin group (62% vs. 20% in the placebo group, (p<0.0001)6.
Digestive health
St Mary’s thistle is traditionally used in WHM to relieve symptoms of dyspepsia such as flatulence, bloating, abdominal discomfort, feelings of fullness and loss of appetite.
The German Commission E approves the use of Milk thistle preparations for dyspeptic complaints7.

Stress Ease contains herbs that support a healthy stress response in the body and can help relieve symptoms of stress such as fatigue, debility and poor memory and concentration.
Rhodiola is an antioxidant herb to help reduce the effects of oxidative stress in the body.
Stress & the adrenal glands
Stress is a common phenomenon that occurs when people feel that the demands made on them exceed their ability to cope. Short-term stress can be beneficial - it can increase alertness, energy and
productivity - however, long-term stress can deplete the body’s ability to cope and adversely affect health.
Stress triggers the ‘fight or flight’ response in the body, where the body prepares to take action against a potential danger and
hormones (adrenaline and cortisol) are released, causing the heart rate, metabolism and breathing rate to increase. Simultaneously, the activity of the parasympathetic nervous system, responsible for digestion, relaxation and sleep, is suppressed. Physical stressors directly stimulate the hypothalamus, while mental and emotional stress stimulate the hypothalamus via the limbic system.
The adrenal glands are two triangle-shaped endocrine glands that sit on the top of each kidney and produce hormones involved in the stress response, including adrenaline, noradrenaline and cortisol. Prolonged stress can lead to high or low levels of cortisol and adrenal fatigue.
Hans Seyle, a Hungarian endocrinologist, was the first to give a scientific explanation for “stress”. He developed the three phases of the General Adaption Syndrome (GAS):
Stage one (alarm): characterised by hormonal changes and increased sympathetic nervous system activity (fight or flight), noradrenaline secretions and up-regulated cortisol
Stage two (resistance): the body has adapted to the stressor and the above symptoms disappear and body metabolism returns to normal
Stage three (exhaustion): if the stressor(s) continue beyond the body’s capacity, body resources become exhausted.
Common symptoms of stress and adrenal fatigue include anxiety, low mood, poor memory and concentration, fatigue, poor immunity, sleep problems and increased reliance on stimulants, such as caffeine and sugar.
Healthy stress response
Stress Ease supports adrenal gland health and a healthy stress response in the body.
The herbs in Stress Ease are considered to be adaptogens, which help the body adapt to stress.
Rhodiola is traditionally used in Western herbal medicine (WHM) to relieve symptoms of stress, including fatigue and poor memory and concentration.
The active constituents in Rhodiola are salidroside and rosavin, which modulate the HPA axis and prevent depletion of adrenal catecholamines induced by acute stress. Rhodiola influences monoamines, including serotonin, dopamine and norepinephrine, in the cerebral cortex, brain stem and hypothalamus. It is believed to inhibit the activity of enzymes responsible for monoamine degradation and facilitate neurotransmitter transport within the
brain1. Stress Ease contains Rhodiola standardised to 2mg salidroside and 3mg rosavin.
Ashwagandha is traditionally regarded as a tonic and sedative, used to strengthen an exhausted nervous system, and has the dual action of energising while calming.
In Ayurvedic medicine, Ashwagandha is considered to be rasayana (rejuvenating tonic) to enhance vitality and relieve general debility, especially during convalescence or old age. It is also used to balance aggravated Vata (nervine activity), and as a vajikarana (reproductive tonic and aphrodisiac).
Ashwagandha is traditionally used in Ayurvedic medicine to promote sleep, where it acts as a nourishing nervine rather than a heavy sedative.
Ashwagandha supports a healthy stress response in the body by having a regulatory effect on the HPA axis. Research shows
Ashwagandha decreases cortisol and can reduce the tendency of dopamine receptors in the brain to activate under stress2.
Licorice and Rehmannia are traditionally considered adrenal tonics to support healthy adrenal gland function. They slow cortisol breakdown and, therefore, have a cortisol-sparing effect. Licorice
contains glycyrrhizic acid, which is metabolised to glycyrrhetinic acid, a potent inhibitor of 11 beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase. This enzyme converts active cortisol to inactive cortisone, thus increasing the amount of circulating cortisol.
Stress Ease contains the amino acid tyrosine, an essential precursor to hormones involved in the stress response: dopamine, noradrenaline and adrenaline.

subsections.heading: DRUG INTERACTIONS
subsections.text:
Caution with cyclosporin – Licorice may lead to reduced blood concentrations of the drug (based on animal studies). Take only under the care of a health professional and monitor cyclosporin levels.
Caution with corticosteroid medications – Licorice can potentiate the effects of oral and topical corticosteroids. Monitor.
Caution with digoxin – Licorice (in high doses) may increase digoxin toxicity. Monitor.
Caution with diuretic medication (loop, thiazide and potassium-depleting) – concurrent administration with Licorice may increase risk of hypokalaemia and hypertension due to increased potassium excretion. Monitor potassium levels.
Caution with blood pressure medication – Licorice may increase blood pressure (usually in much higher doses) and Rhodiola may (theoretically) have an additive effect with antihypertensive drugs and increase the risk of hypotension. Monitor blood pressure.
Caution with hypoglycaemic medication – Ashwagandha, Rhodiola and Rehmannia may have additive effects and increase the risk of hypoglycaemia (theoretical). Monitor.
Caution with thyroid hormones – Ashwagandha can increase T3 and T4 and reduce serum TSH. Concomitant use may cause additive effects. Monitor.
Caution with sedatives – Ashwagandha may potentiate the sedative effects of barbiturates, benzodiazepines and other anxiolytics (theoretical). Adverse reaction unlikely.
Caution with immunosuppressant therapy – Ashwagandha and Rhodiola may have immunostimulating effects and decrease the effectiveness of medication (theoretical). Adverse reaction unlikely.

Sublingual tablet

Vitamin B12 or cobalamin is an essential water-soluble vitamin required for DNA synthesis, cell reproduction and fatty acid and amino acid metabolism. The primary source of vitamin B12 is from animal products such as meat, fish, eggs, dairy and organ meats.
Cyanocobalamin is the form of vitamin B12 commonly used in nutritional supplements and is readily converted to
5-deoxyadenosylcobalamin and methylcobalamin, the active forms of vitamin B12 in the body.
Oral supplementation of cyanocobalamin is dependent on stomach acid and intrinsic factor (IF) for absorption into the body. Sublingual administration is beneficial for those who have low stomach acid and is an alternative to oral (swallowed) tablets and injections.
Gastric acid secretions and IF diminish as part of the ageing process, therefore many elderly people are at risk of a vitamin B12 deficiency. The long-term use of certain medications, such as inhibitors of stomach acid secretion, can adversely affect vitamin B12 absorption.
Vegans and strict vegetarians are also at risk of vitamin B12 deficiency as they do not consume any animal products, the main dietary source of vitamin B12.
Signs & symptoms of B12 deficiency
Fatigue, weakness and shortness of breath
Poor concentration, memory and muscular coordination
Irritability
Numbness and tingling in hands and feet
Poor immunity
Inflammation of mucous membranes in the mouth or sore tongue
Sublingual vs intravenous B12
Sublingual administration of vitamin B12 overcomes the challenges of intramuscular (IM) injections and can be considered as a first line option. Sublingual tablets are a non-invasive, pain-free and cost-effective form of B12 supplementation. IM injections can be painful and costly and require administration by a health professional.
A large retrospective study involving 4281 participants compared the efficacy of sublingual versus standard IM administration of vitamin B12 in restoring B12 levels. 830 patients (19.3%) were given 1000 micrograms B12 IM injections and 3451 patients (80.7%) were given 1000 micrograms sublingual tablets, both containing
cyanocobalamin. The mean standard deviation difference between serum B12 levels before and after supplementation was statistically significantly higher in the sublingual group vs IM injection group (p<0.001). The sublingual tablet significantly increased the odds ratio of an increase of serum B12 levels compared to the IM group (p<0.001). In a sub-group of people with serum vitamin B12 levels
<300mg/L (borderline deficiency), the sublingual preparation was superior to IM injections in raising serum vitamin vitamin B121.
Energy production
Sublingual B12 1000 supports energy production and aids the metabolism of carbohydrates, protein and fats. Vitamin B12 is involved in the synthesis of the citric acid cycle intermediate, succinyl-CoA. Succinyl-CoA plays an important role in the production of energy from lipids and proteins.
Nerve & brain health
Sublingual B12 1000 supports nervous system function and nerve health. Adequate intake of vitamin B12 is essential for normal neurological function. It plays a vital role in the synthesis and maintenance of myelin, the protective sheath surrounding nerves.
Sublingual B12 1000 supports brain health and cognitive function. The European Food Safety Authority concluded that a cause-and-effect relationship has been established between the dietary intake of vitamin B12 and contribution to normal neurological and psychological functions2.
Cardiovascular system
Sublingual B12 1000 maintains cardiovascular system health. Vitamin B12 participates in the synthesis and regeneration of methionine from homocysteine, helping to maintain healthy homocysteine levels. Methionine donates ‘methyl groups’ required for the methylation reactions to occur. Homocysteine is an amino acid-like compound that has been linked to an increased risk of adverse cardiovascular outcomes when levels are elevated.
Sublingual B12 1000 supports red blood cell health. Vitamin B12, along with B6 and folic acid, is an important co-factor required to activate enzymes that are essential for the formation of the haem components that form haemoglobin, a protein abundant in red blood cells and responsible for transporting oxygen around the body3.

Bacopa monnieri is a traditional Indian herb that has been used in Ayurvedic medicine for 3000 years and is commonly known as Brahmi or Bacopa.
Brahmi is well-known for its beneficial effects on memory and cognition and has a reputation as a brain tonic. The pharmacological activity of Brahmi is attributed to the saponin bacoside and bacopasaponin constituents.
Super Brahmi 6000 contains an extract of Brahmi standardised to bacosides, known as BacoMind®. BacoMind® is a patented extract of Brahmi, clinically researched for memory and cognition enhancing properties. It is a unique full-spectrum phytochemical composition containing 9 different bio-active derivatives.
BacoMind® is standardised to contain bacoside A, bacopaside I, bacopaside II, bacopasaponin C, jujubogenin isomer of
bacopasaponin C, bacosine, luteolin, apigenin and β-sitosterol D glucoside.
Traditional use
Brahmi is a well-known herb in India with a long history of use in Ayurvedic herbal preparations. The Ayurvedic action for Brahmi in Sanskrit is ‘medhya rasayana’, which translates to ‘herbs which rejuvenate the mind’.
Brahmi is traditionally used in Ayurvedic medicine as a brain tonic to enhance brain health and improve memory and cognitive performance. It is noted in traditional texts to increase memory, learning ability and concentration.
Brahmi is traditionally used in Ayurvedic medicine as nervine to support the nervous system. It has been used to aid recovery from exhaustion, stress and debility with aggravation of ‘vata’. Vata is responsible
for movement in the nervous system, muscles, heart and mind. An aggravation or imbalance of vata can manifest as anxiety states.
Antioxidant
Brahmi is an antioxidant and helps reduce free radicals in the body.
It has direct free-radical scavenging activity and increases the activity of endogenous antioxidant systems.
The brain is particularly susceptible to oxidative stress as it is metabolically active, possesses high levels of pro-oxidant iron, and is composed of unsaturated lipids prone to lipid peroxidation. The blood–brain barrier prevents many exogenous antioxidants from quenching reactive oxygen species (ROS) in the brain.
An experimental animal model study assessed the neuroprotective role of bacoside A against oxidative stress in the brains of rats exposed to cigarette smoke. Concentrations of enzymatic and nonenzymatic antioxidants were measured after exposure. Daily administration of bacoside A significantly increased brain levels of glutathione, vitamin C, vitamin E and vitamin A1.
Memory & cognition

Calcium with cofactors
Adequate calcium intake is essential at every stage of life and important for the prevention of osteoporosis later in life. While bone mass accrues in the earlier stages of life, maintaining appropriate calcium levels in the body is important for ongoing bone strength and for reducing the risk of fractures later in life.
After 30 years of age, bone mass begins to decline in both men and women. Osteoporosis affects 1 in 3 women and 1 in 5 men globally, regardless of geographical location1 and over 1 million Australians are affected by osteoporosis2.
Boron is important for the metabolism and utilisation of the bone building nutrients calcium, magnesium and vitamin D. Boron plays an important role in extending the half-life of vitamin D, which is essential for the body’s ability to absorb calcium.
Magnesium, vitamin D and vitamin K are required for calcium to be absorbed in the body. Calcium cannot function without sufficient magnesium, while calcium, vitamin D and vitamin K all work together in a delicate balance to achieve proper bone density.
Equisetum arvense, Horsetail, is a perennial herb and one of the highest natural sources of silica. Silica accelerates the process of calcification and deposition in bone. It also improves bone matrix quality and facilitates bone mineralisation.
Bone health
Super Calcium Plus with Boron is a comprehensive calcium supplement containing two forms of calcium, calcium citrate and hydroxyapatite, with boron for bone health. Calcium citrate is an organic form of calcium that is highly soluble, offering greater bioavailability than other forms of calcium, approximately 25% greater bioavailability than calcium carbonate when given with a meal3.
Super Calcium Plus with Boron also contains vitamin D to support the absorption of dietary calcium as well as other nutritional cofactors.
Calcium is an important mineral to help prevent osteoporosis when dietary intake is inadequate, and a diet deficient in calcium can lead to osteoporosis in later life.
Calcium is essential for building bone and maintaining bone strength; 99% of the body’s calcium is located in the bone matrix. The remaining 1% is found in the blood and other fluids, and is
essential for regulation of heartbeat, muscle contraction, release of neurotransmitters, nerve signalling and blood clotting.
Calcium is well known for its role in bone health, with bone containing more than 90% of the body’s total calcium content. Calcium plays
an important role in bone remodelling, the process where bone is deposited by osteoblasts and resorption is carried out by osteoclasts. In the bone deposition process, bone is created by calcium and phosphate ions binding to create hydroxyapatite crystals.
Calcium homeostasis is tightly regulated by parathyroid hormone, phosphorous, vitamin K and vitamin D. Together they determine the level of calcium absorption and excretion or retention via the kidneys and control the bone remodelling process in the developing skeleton.
Boron is a trace mineral involved in the development and maintenance of healthy bones, while being involved in the efficient absorption of calcium and the activation of vitamin D.
Magnesium is essential for absorption and metabolism of calcium. Magnesium also affects the concentrations of both parathyroid hormone and the active form of vitamin D, which are major regulators of bone homeostasis. Magnesium helps to maintain healthy bones, bone strength and healthy teeth.
Manganese is a cofactor for several enzymes involved in bone formation and the building of osteoblasts.
The major function of vitamin D is to maintain blood calcium concentrations by enhancing the ability of the small intestine to absorb calcium from the diet.
Healthy teeth
Super Calcium Plus with Boron contains calcium, vitamin D and magnesium to support healthy teeth.
Calcium is stored in both the teeth and the bones where it provides structure and strength while magnesium assists by supporting the absorption of calcium.
Vitamin D supports strong teeth as part of its role in regulating calcium and phosphate.

The thyroid is a butterfly-shaped gland located just under the voice box (larynx) and is made up of mainly microscopic sacs called thyroid follicles. The function of the thyroid gland is to take iodine and convert it to the thyroid hormones T4 and T3. T4, also known as thyroxine, contains four molecules of iodine, while T3, triiodothyronine, contains three molecules of iodine.
T4 and T3 are also influenced by thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH). TSH is produced by the pituitary gland in response to signals from the hypothalamus. TSH stimulates the thyroid gland, promoting it to produce more of the thyroid hormones T4 and T3.
T4 is the storage hormone and must be converted into the active hormone T3 by the body. T3 is about 5 times more potent than T4 and only T3 can enter the cell receptors. Receptors throughout the body use T3 to regulate oxygen use, basal metabolic rate (BMR), body temperature, cellular metabolism and growth and development.
Thyroid function
Thyroid Support contains iodine, tyrosine, selenium and zinc, nutrients that are important for thyroid gland health and thyroid hormone production.
Tyrosine, iodine, selenium and zinc are required for the synthesis of thyroid hormones and for the conversion of the inactive T4 to the active T3. Tyrosine is a precursor to the thyroid hormones and is also essential for the proper functioning of the adrenal, thyroid and pituitary glands.
Iodine, especially, is an essential component of both T3 and T4, comprising 65% of the weight of T4 and 59% of the weight of T31.
Ashwagandha assists the production of thyroid hormones by enhancing T4 concentrations2.
Antioxidant
Zinc and vitamin C act as antioxidants, reducing free radical damage to cells and organs in the body and supporting their normal function. Antioxidants protect the thyroid gland from oxidative damage.
Zinc is a powerful antioxidant and free radical scavenger. Zinc's role as an antioxidant is achieved through numerous mechanisms
including protecting vitamin E from depletion, acting as an important structural component of the antioxidant enzyme superoxide dismutase and reducing free radical production.
Vitamin C is antioxidant by scavenging oxygen and nitrogen free radicals, regenerating antioxidant vitamin E and maintaining reduced glutathione.
Figure 1: The link between the adrenal glands and thyroid
Immune health
Thyroid Support contains vitamin C, selenium and zinc to support immune health.
While the thyroid gland is a key part of the human endocrine system, it works closely with both the immune system and nervous system to regulate metabolism. A healthy immune system is required for the optimal functioning of the thyroid gland.
Nervous system & stress response
Thyroid Support contains both Ashwagandha and zinc to support the nervous system and a healthy stress response in the body.

Omega-3 fatty acids
