subsections.heading: TECHNICAL INFORMATION
subsections.text:
Tyrosine is a non-essential amino acid (synthesised endogenously from the essential amino acid phenylalanine) and is an essential precursor for a wide range of diverse and far-reaching biochemical reactions in the body.
The name tyrosine is derived from the Greek word ‘tyros’, meaning cheese, and was first discovered in cheese-derived casein in 1846 by chemist Justus von Liebig. Tyrosine can also be obtained from dietary proteins in dairy products, meats, fish, eggs, nuts, beans, oats and wheat. When dietary intake of tyrosine is inadequate, phenylalanine is converted to tyrosine. Dietary needs of tyrosine are dependent on phenylalanine intake. When phenylalanine intake is adequate (about 9 mg/kg daily), dietary tyrosine intake should be about 7mg/kg daily1.
Tyrosine absorption takes place in the small intestine and is then transported to the liver where it is involved in a number of biochemical reactions including protein synthesis and oxidative catabolic reactions. Any tyrosine not metabolised by the liver enters systemic circulation and is directed to various tissues where it is involved in the synthesis of neurotransmitters and hormones, incorporated into protein structures or deaminated for gluconeogenesis. Peak plasma levels occur 2 hours after administration and remain elevated for around 6-8 hours.
Nervous system health
Tyrosine is an essential precursor for the synthesis of catecholamines adrenaline, noradrenaline and dopamine. Supplementation with tyrosine aids adrenal function helping during periods of prolonged stress, to support the body and improve stress adaptation.
Tyrosine can readily cross from systemic circulation into the brain, functioning in the synthesis of dopamine. Dopamine is the neurotransmitter responsible for motivation and reward.
Tyrosine has been shown to enhance the release of catecholamines when neurons are firing at an increased rate due to stress, but not at their basal rates.
Thyroid hormone production
Tyrosine undergoes iodination to form monoiodotryrosine (T1), a second iodination to produce diiodotyrosine (T2), and these combine to produce the active thyroid hormone known as tri-iodothyronine (T3) and tetraiodothyronine or thyroxine (T4).
As tyrosine is a precursor for the synthesis of thyroid hormones, it is involved in the regulation of basal metabolic rate, oxygen use, cellular metabolism, growth and development.
Tyrosine is an essential precursor in the synthesis of melanin, responsible for skin and hair colour pigment.

subsections.heading: DRUG INTERACTIONS
subsections.text:
Contraindicated with antidepressant drugs (MAOIs, SSRIs and tricyclic antidepressants) - concurrent use may have an additive effect or result in elevated blood pressure.
Contraindicated with levodopa - with tyrosine competes with levodapa for uptake, reducing efficacy.
Caution with levothyroxine – tyrosine may have additive effects. Separate dose by 2 hours and monitor use.
Caution with CNS stimulants – tyrosine may have additive effects. Separate dose by 2 hours and monitor use.

subsections.heading: CAUTIONS
subsections.text:
Contraindicated in hyperthyroidism and Graves’ disease - as tyrosine is a precursor to thyroxine, theoretically it may aggravate these conditions.
Contraindicated in those with melanoma, adrenal tumours or pheochromocytoma.
Not suitable in pregnancy or breastfeeding – safety data regarding high dose tyrosine is unavailable.

Coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10) is comprised of two closely related molecules: ubidecarenone (also known as ubiquinone) and ubiquinol. Ubiquinone is the fully oxidised state of CoQ10, while ubiquinol is the fully reduced or active form.
Ubiquinol is the metabolically active form of CoQ10 that is ready for use in the body. Other forms of CoQ10, such as ubidecarenone, are converted to ubiquinol prior to use. Ageing leads to a decrease in the function of the enzyme that converts ubidecarenone to ubiquinol, resulting in decreasing ubiquinol levels. For anyone over the age of 40, ubiquinol is the preferred CoQ10 supplemental form.
Ubiquinol is more bioavailable than ubidecarenone, demonstrating greater absorption and uptake by the body.
A randomised, double-blind, crossover study examined the bioavailability of both ubiquinol and ubiquinone using an acute intake of 100mg in 10 healthy subjects with 2 weeks between treatments. In the ubiquinol group, plasma concentrations were significantly higher compared to ubiquinone at 6, 8, 12, 24, 48 and 72 hours post-intake (p<0.001). The area under the curve (AUC) for ubiquinol 72 hours
post-intake was 4.3-fold greater than for ubiquinone1.
The ubiquinol in Ubiquinol 100mg is sourced from world-wide ubiquinol specialist, Kaneka, who use innovative patented technology to stabilise ubiquinol (which, under normal circumstances, is readily oxidised by air and converted into ubidecarenone).
Ubiquinol 100mg contains ubiquinol produced in a natural fermentation process by yeast. It is in a rice bran oil base, which provides a stable base. Rice bran oil has a high content of tocotrienols (antioxidants in the vitamin E family), which provide greater stability from oxidation than soy oil.
Antioxidant
Ubiquinol is a potent lipid-soluble antioxidant that helps protect the body from oxidative damage. Specifically, it protects cell membranes from oxidation, supporting cell membrane integrity and cell functioning.
Ubiquinol also supports the antioxidant network by prolonging the activity of vitamins C and E and recycling them back into their antioxidant form.
Energy production & exercise
Ubiquinol 100mg supports energy production. It is an essential component of the mitochondria and is necessary for cellular adenosine triphosphate (ATP) synthesis.
CoQ10 is concentrated in tissues with high energy requirements, such as the heart and skeletal muscle. Physical activity increases
the body’s demand for energy (and therefore CoQ10) and reduces muscle tissue levels of CoQ10. Physical exercise also induces muscle damage associated with a high production of free radicals and pro-inflammatory mediators.
Ubiquinol supports healthy exercise capacity and muscle health after exercise. A randomised trial in 100 healthy individuals showed that short-term supplementation with ubiquinol (200mg/day) before strenuous exercise decreased oxidative stress and improved endothelial function and muscle recovery after strenuous exercise2. Ubiquinol supplementation also increased total antioxidant status.
Cardiovascular health
Ubiquinol 100mg supports cardiovascular system function and helps maintain a healthy cardiovascular system and heart health. Ubiquinol plays a role in all energy-dependent process, including heart
muscle contraction. Cardiac cells are highly metabolically active and, therefore, have higher mitochondrial coenzyme requirements. Ubiquinol supports optimal cellular and mitochondrial function in cardiomyocytes.
The inner lining of blood vessels (arteries, veins and capillaries) consists of a thin, single layer of endothelial cells that form the endothelium. The endothelium has a role in the control of blood fluidity, platelet aggregation and vascular tone. Ubiquinol supports endothelial function by inhibiting inflammatory and oxidative damage in endothelial cells.
Ubiquinol also helps maintain healthy blood vessels by inhibiting the oxidation of LDL cholesterol.
Sperm health
Ubiquinol supports sperm health and sperm motility in males.
CoQ10 is concentrated in the head and midpiece (neck) of sperm and in seminal fluid, where it plays a role in mitochondrial energy release and antioxidant functions. CoQ10 concentrations show a direct correlation with seminal parameters, especially count and motility3.
A double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled study in 228 men showed that 200mg of ubiquinol increased sperm density (p=0.017), sperm motility (p=0.024) and sperm morphology (p=0.027)4.
Statins
Statin medications, used to manage blood cholesterol levels, work by inhibiting 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A (HMG-CoA)
reductase, the enzyme involved in cholesterol biosynthesis (see figure 1). Inhibition of this enzyme also adversely affects the biosynthesis of CoQ10 and reduces both plasma and myocardial levels. A systematic

Coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10) is comprised of two closely related molecules: ubidecarenone (also known as ubiquinone) and ubiquinol. Ubiquinone is the fully oxidised state of CoQ10, while ubiquinol is the fully reduced or active form.
Ubiquinol is the metabolically active form of CoQ10 that is ready for use in the body. Other forms of CoQ10, such as ubidecarenone, are converted to ubiquinol prior to use. Ageing leads to a decrease in the function of the enzyme that converts ubidecarenone to ubiquinol, resulting in decreasing ubiquinol levels. For anyone over the age of 40, ubiquinol is the preferred CoQ10 supplemental form.
Ubiquinol is more bioavailable than ubidecarenone, demonstrating greater absorption and uptake by the body.
A randomised, double-blind, crossover study examined the bioavailability of both ubiquinol and ubiquinone using an acute intake of 100mg in 10 healthy subjects with 2 weeks between treatments. In the ubiquinol group, plasma concentrations were significantly higher compared to ubiquinone at 6, 8, 12, 24, 48 and 72 hours post-intake (p<0.001). The area under the curve (AUC) for ubiquinol 72 hours
post-intake was 4.3-fold greater than for ubiquinone1.
The ubiquinol in Ubiquinol 150mg is sourced from world-wide ubiquinol specialist, Kaneka, who use innovative patented technology to stabilise ubiquinol (which, under normal circumstances, is readily oxidised by air and converted into ubidecarenone).
Ubiquinol 150mg contains ubiquinol produced in a natural fermentation process by yeast. It is in a rice bran oil base, which provides a stable, soy-free base, suitable for individuals with an allergy to soy. Rice bran oil has a high content of tocotrienols (antioxidants in the vitamin E family), which provide greater stability from oxidation than soy oil.
Antioxidant
Ubiquinol is a potent lipid-soluble antioxidant that helps protect the body from oxidative damage. Specifically, it protects cell membranes from oxidation, supporting cell membrane integrity and cell functioning.
Ubiquinol also supports the antioxidant network by prolonging the activity of vitamins C and E and recycling them back into their antioxidant form.
Energy production & exercise
Ubiquinol 150mg supports energy production. It is an essential component of the mitochondria and is necessary for cellular adenosine triphosphate (ATP) synthesis.
CoQ10 is concentrated in tissues with high energy requirements,
such as the heart and skeletal muscle. Physical activity increases the body’s demand for energy (and therefore CoQ10) and reduces muscle tissue levels of CoQ10. Physical exercise also induces muscle
damage associated with a high production of free radicals and pro-inflammatory mediators.
Ubiquinol supports healthy exercise capacity and muscle health after exercise. A randomised trial in 100 healthy individuals showed that short-term supplementation with ubiquinol (200mg/day) before strenuous exercise decreased oxidative stress and improved endothelial function and muscle recovery after strenuous exercise2. Ubiquinol supplementation also increased total antioxidant status.
Cardiovascular health
Ubiquinol 150mg supports cardiovascular system function and helps maintain a healthy cardiovascular system and heart health. Ubiquinol plays a role in all energy-dependent process, including heart
muscle contraction. Cardiac cells are highly metabolically active and, therefore, have higher mitochondrial coenzyme requirements. Ubiquinol supports optimal cellular and mitochondrial function in cardiomyocytes.
The inner lining of blood vessels (arteries, veins and capillaries) consists of a thin, single layer of endothelial cells that form the endothelium. The endothelium has a role in the control of blood fluidity, platelet aggregation and vascular tone. Ubiquinol supports endothelial function by inhibiting inflammatory and oxidative damage in endothelial cells.
Ubiquinol also helps maintain healthy blood vessels by inhibiting the oxidation of LDL cholesterol.
Sperm health
Ubiquinol supports sperm health and sperm motility in males.
CoQ10 is concentrated in the head and midpiece (neck) of sperm and in seminal fluid, where it plays a role in mitochondrial energy release and antioxidant functions. CoQ10 concentrations show a direct correlation with seminal parameters, especially count and motility3.

Zinc is an essential trace element known to play an important role in all human living cells. The human body contains about 2g of total zinc, with more than 85% found in skeletal muscle and bone1.
Zinc plays a crucial role in the pathways involved in inflammation, immunity, carbohydrate and protein metabolism, DNA metabolism and repair, reproduction, vision, taste and bone health.
Zinc is required for the synthesis of new tissue and is an important cellular building block. A complex homeostatic system maintains zinc levels within a narrow range balancing absorption and excretion.
Zinc is widely distributed in foods. Meats, fish and poultry are the major contributors to the diet, but cereals and dairy foods also contribute substantial amounts. The presence of zinc in foods as a complex rather than as free ions affects its bioavailability. The
environment within the gastrointestinal tract, which can be affected by other dietary constituents, markedly influences the solubility and absorptive efficiency of zinc.
Zinc is more difficult to absorb from plant-based foods. Many plant sources of zinc also contain high phytate levels, such as wholegrains and seeds, which inhibit the absorption of the mineral. The requirement for dietary zinc may be as high as 50% greater for vegetarians.
Ultra Zinc + helps maintain zinc levels in the body. To address established zinc deficiency, 25-50mg of zinc per day is recommended2. Signs of zinc deficiency include impaired immune function, reduced sense of taste and smell, poor wound healing, poor cognitive function, irritability and dermatitis.
To date, there is no established reliable marker for measuring an individual’s zinc status. Zinc is stored intracellularly and only a small percentage is found in the plasma, meaning plasma zinc levels are not a precise measure.
Ultra Zinc + contains high-strength vitamin A with 1500IU per capsule. Vitamin A is an essential nutrient required for growth and development, immune function, eye health and the maintenance of epithelial surfaces.
Antioxidant
Zinc is a powerful antioxidant and free radical scavenger. Zinc's role as an antioxidant is achieved through numerous mechanisms
including protecting vitamin E from depletion, acting as an important structural component of the antioxidant enzyme superoxide dismutase and reducing free radical production.
Vitamin A has free radical scavenging properties and, when bound to protein kinase C, is an essential cofactor in redox activation of the mitochondrial signaling pathway.
Immune system health
Zinc is an important mineral for healthy immune system function. It is essential for the normal development and function of immune cells, for mediating non-specific immunity, such as neutrophils, monocytes and natural killer cells and for affecting the development of acquired immunity and T-lymphocyte function.
Poor zinc status has been shown to impair cellular mediators of the body’s innate immune system, reducing the body’s natural resistance to infectious agents.
Vitamin A supports healthy epithelial cells in the body and is therefore a key nutrient for maintaining skin barrier to infection and healthy immune system function. Adequate vitamin A is also important for T cell function and the prevention of prolonged inflammatory reactions3.
Skin health
Ultra Zinc + supports skin health and wound healing. The skin is the third most zinc-rich tissue in the body, with 5% of total body zinc4. Zinc is present in both the epidermis and dermis, though at levels five-fold higher in the epidermis. In skin physiology, zinc stabilises cell
membranes, serves as an essential cofactor for several metalloenzymes and participates in basal cell mitosis and differentiation.
Vitamin A is a key nutrient for normal cellular differentiation and epithelial integrity. Vitamin A deficiency can lead to dry skin.
Both zinc and vitamin A are often recommended for acne. One study found that the serum vitamin A and zinc levels were significantly lower in patients with acne than in age and sex matched healthy individuals in the control group (p<0.001). It also showed a negative correlation between acne severity and zinc levels5.
In another study, plasma vitamin A concentrations were significantly lower in patients with acne than age-matched healthy controls (p=0.007)6.

Zinc is theorised to be beneficial in acne due to its role in the maintenance of cell replication and wound repair, regulation of inflammation, immune function and inhibition of 5α-reductase, which blocks the conversion of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone and supresses sebaceous gland activity7.
A multicentre, randomised, double-blind trial in 332 patients compared 30mg of zinc (n=163) to the antibiotic minocycline (n=169) over 3 months. Zinc supplementation resulted in a decrease in the number of superficial inflammatory lesions by 31.78% on day 30, 42.09% on day 60 and 49.84% on day 90. At the end of the study, 31.2% of people supplemented with zinc had a two-thirds decrease in inflammatory lesions8.
Male reproductive health
Zinc plays an important role in maintaining male reproductive health. It is required for the normal functioning of the prostate gland, while being essential for the healthy formation and maturation of sperm.
Zinc is found in high quantities in prostatic fluid, where it plays an antimicrobial role within the fluid and the prostate gland itself.
Zinc is found in maturing spermatozoa, influencing the motility and head-neck connection of the sperm. Zinc status is strongly correlated with sperm count, sperm morphology and motility.
Taste sensation
The area of the brain responsible for the sensations of taste and smell need adequate levels of zinc to function efficiently.
Adequate zinc helps maintain normal taste sensation.
Vision & eye health
Ultra Zinc + supports eye health and vision.
Zinc is an essential trace metals that is concentrated in the photoreceptors and the retinal pigment epithelium of the eye. Zinc is a cofactor in a number of ocular enzymes, including copper-zinc superoxide dismutase, which functions as an antioxidant by catalysing the conversion of free radicals to hydrogen peroxide.
Vitamin A is critical for vision as an essential component of rhodopsin, a protein that absorbs light in the retinal receptors. It also supports the normal differentiation and function of the conjunctival membranes and cornea.

subsections.text:
Caution with antihypertensive medication – ubiquinol may have additive effects. Monitor blood pressure.
Caution with warfarin and other antiplatelet and anticoagulant medication – conflicting reports have shown ubiquinol may decrease, increase or have no effect on the efficacy of oral anticoagulants. Use only under the care of a health professional.

Contraindicated with retinoid medication (including acitretin, isotretinoin, accutane or roaccutane) – vitamin A supplements should not be taken concurrently due to potential vitamin A toxicity.
Caution with NSAIDs, cephalexin, penicillamine and quinolone antibiotics and tetracycline antibiotics – zinc interferes with their absorption and vitamin A may reduce their effectiveness. Separate dose by 3 hours.
Caution with amiloride (diuretic) – drug can reduce zinc excretion, leading to zinc accumulation.
Caution with eltrombopag – zinc may reduce drug absorption. Separate dose by 4 hours.
Caution with levodopa – vitamin B6 reduces drug effects. However, this effect is prevented by the administration of a dopa-
decarboxylase inhibitor (e.g. benserazide, carbidopa) with levodopa, as is common clinical practice.
Caution with phenobarbital/phenobarbitone and phenytoin (anticonvulsants) – vitamin B6 may reduce serum concentrations. Monitor.
Caution with oral contraceptives – concurrent use may increase vitamin A levels.
Caution with aspirin and paracetamol – zinc and vitamin A may reduce their effectiveness. Separate dose by 2 hours.
Caution with calcium supplements – zinc and calcium compete for common intestinal absorption sites. Separate zinc and calcium supplements by at least 2 hours.

subsections.text: High-strength	✓ Supports nerve health	✓ Supports energy production	✓ Vitamin B1 supplementation

Vitamin B1 (thiamine) is a water-soluble vitamin that is involved in carbohydrate metabolism and nervous system health. As body
reserves of thiamine are small, a steady intake is important to avoid deficiency. Vitamin B1 100mg helps prevent vitamin B1 deficiency.
There is approximately 30mg of thiamine in the average adult, with about half of this stored in muscle tissue. It is also found in high concentrations in the heart, liver, kidneys and brain1.
Vitamin B1 is absorbed in the small intestine. It is generally well absorbed, however, several dietary factors can decrease absorption, including alcohol, thiaminase, sulfite preservatives, high intakes of tea and coffee and folate or protein deficiency. A high alcohol intake is the greatest risk factor for thiamine deficiency, as alcohol both impairs the absorption and enhances the excretion of the vitamin, doubling the risk of deficiency.
Strenuous exercise, fever, excessive alcohol consumption, pregnancy and lactation and adolescent growth periods can increase thiamine requirements. The elderly may also have an increased requirement for thiamine.
Food sources of thiamine include meats, wheatgerm, wholegrain cereals, peas, beans and peanuts, milk, Brewer’s yeast and yeast extracts. Wheatgerm provides an important source of thiamine in the diet, however, thiamine is sensitive to heat and light, so can be lost in processing.
Thiamine hydrochloride is the most common form of supplemental vitamin B1. It consists of 89% thiamine and 11% hydrochloric acid.
Excess thiamine is cleared from the body via the kidneys; as such, there is no evidence of toxic effects from oral administration.
Energy
Vitamin B1 is converted to its active form in the body, thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP). TPP is a vital coenzyme in the production of energy within cells.
Vitamin B1 is required for normal digestion and the conversion of food into energy. It is a cofactor for several enzymes involved in carbohydrate catabolism, including pyruvate dehydrogenase,
transketolase and alpha-ketoglutarate. It is also involved in amino acid catabolism.
Due to its role in energy production, most of the body’s thiamine is stored in muscle.
A study found that supplementation with 10mg thiamine daily in women with a marginal deficiency lead to significantly increased general well-being and decreased fatigue2.
Nervous system
Vitamin B1 is important to maintain a healthy nervous system. It is located in the nerve cell membrane and is important for the transmission of nerve impulses.
Vitamin B1 plays a role in the metabolism of several neurotransmitters, including acetylcholine, GABA and serotonin, and, therefore, plays a role in maintaining healthy mood.
Hormones
A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover study found that 100mg of vitamin B1 daily helped the symptoms of dysmenorrhoea and supplementation had lasting effects up to 3 months after the supplementation3.

Vitamin B2 (riboflavin) is a water-soluble B vitamin that helps maintain the integrity of mucous membranes, skin, eyes and the nervous system.
Riboflavin is mostly present in the body as a component of two coenzymes: Flavin mononucleotide (FMN) and Flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD).
Common clinical symptoms of riboflavin deficiency include inflammation of the throat, mouth (stomatitis), and tongue (glossitis); cracking of the tissue around the corners of the mouth (angular cheilitis) and moist, red, scaly skin.
Vitamin B2 is essential for the activation of other B complex vitamins. FAD is required for the formation of niacin from tryptophan and FMN is required for the formation of the active vitamin B6. Vitamin B2 also participates in folate metabolism. FAD is a cofactor for
methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHRF), which converts folate into its active form.
Vitamin B2 promotes normal growth and tissue repair. It is required for the growth of skin, hair and nails and a deficiency of vitamin B2 can lengthen wound healing time.
Vitamin B2 helps maintain a healthy immune system. It is required for humoral antibody formation and helps maintain tissue barriers to infection.
Antioxidant
Migraines
Several studies have shown vitamin B2 to be an effective prophylactic to reduce the incidence of migraines.
A preliminary open pilot study of 49 patients with migraine (45 without aura, 4 with aura) found 400mg of riboflavin with or without aspirin for 3 months resulted in a 68.2% improvement in migraine severity. Eighty percent of patients treated with riboflavin alone had a 50% or greater reduction in monthly migraine days1.
Following this, a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled study investigated the effects of 400mg riboflavin or placebo daily for 3 months on 55 patients with migraine. Riboflavin was found to be superior to placebo in reducing attack frequency (p=0.005) and headache days (p=0.012). For headache days, the number of patient responders (at least 50% improvement) was 15% for placebo and 59% for riboflavin (p=0.002; NNT 2.3)2.
More recently, a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled study involving 98 patients receiving either 400mg riboflavin daily or placebo for 3 months was performed. The duration and frequency of headache were significantly less in the second and third months of the study in the riboflavin group vs placebo (p=0.012 and p=0.001, respectively)3.
A 2017 systematic review concluded that riboflavin is a well-tolerated and inexpensive treatment, demonstrating efficacy in the reduction of adult patient’s migraine headache frequency as well as duration4.
Vitamin B2 plays an important role in the body’s antioxidant defence
network. FAD is a cofactor for glutathione reductase, which recycles oxidised glutathione.
Vitamin B2, due to its role in antioxidant systems, helps maintain healthy eyes. Glutathione reductase is involved the protection of the lens from free radical damage.
Energy
FMN and FAD are involved in energy metabolism and the release of energy from nutrients in all body cells. FAD is involved in the citric acid cycle, while FMN has a role in the electron transport chain.
Vitamin B2 aids in the metabolism of carbohydrates, fats and proteins, helping to convert food into energy.
Cardiovascular health
Due to its role in folate metabolism, vitamin B2 is important for homocysteine metabolism and, therefore, helps maintain a healthy cardiovascular system.
Vitamin B2 is also important for the formation of haemoglobin which helps transport oxygen in red blood cells and, therefore, helps maintain normal blood.
There is a correlation between plasma levels of vitamin B2 and homocysteine levels, with high homocysteine levels showing low riboflavin status. High homocysteine levels are associated with a higher risk of cardiovascular conditions.

Vitamin B3 can be formed in the body from the amino acid tryptophan, however, it takes approximately 60mg of tryptophan to form 1mg of niacin, with an approximate conversion rate of 60:1. This conversion requires adequate iron, riboflavin and vitamin B6.
As tryptophan is also a precursor to serotonin and dietary tryptophan is preferentially converted to vitamin B3 in deficiency states, low levels of vitamin B3 can result in serotonin depletion and mood alterations.
Energy
Vitamin B3 is used in the body in two coenzyme forms – nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD) and nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADP), which participate in over 200 metabolic reactions.
Vitamin B3, as NAD and NADP, plays a major role in the metabolism of carbohydrate, proteins, fats and alcohol. NAD acts as an electron and hydrogen acceptor in glycolysis and the citric acid cycle. NADP is primarily involved in fatty acid biosynthesis.
Skin health
Vitamin B3, in the form of nicotinamide, supports skin health and DNA repair and has been shown to have a protective effect against damage caused by UV radiation. It prevents the ATP depletion and glycolytic blockade induced by UV radiation, boosting cellular energy and enhancing DNA repair in the skin.
A double-blind, randomised, placebo controlled crossover trial examined the effects of oral nicotinamide on UV exposure in 61 volunteers. Significant immunosuppression occurred in a UV dose-dependent manner in the presence of placebo. Oral nicotinamide, at doses of either 500mg or 1500mg daily, were well tolerated and significantly reduced UV immunosuppression with no immune effects in unirradiated skin1.
A phase 3, double-blind, randomised, controlled trial using 500mg of nicotinamide twice daily substantiated the benefits of vitamin B3 in supporting skin health and protecting skin from the damaging effects of the sun2.

Vitamin B5, also known as pantothenic acid, is a water-soluble B complex vitamin that is widely distributed throughout the food chain.
Pantothenic acid gets its name from the Greek ‘panto’, which means ‘everywhere’ and refers to the ubiquitous nature of this nutrient.
Vitamin B5 is a component of coenzyme A (CoA), the biologically active form of pantothenic acid, which is involved in over 100 metabolic reactions in the body. It is essential for the breakdown of carbohydrates, proteins, lipids and alcohol, the formation of fatty acids, cholesterol, bile acids and steroid hormones, and is involved in energy metabolism.
Major dietary sources of vitamin B5 include chicken, beef, potatoes, oats, tomato products, liver, kidney, egg yolks and whole grains. Vitamin B5 is easily destroyed by food processing, including freezing, canning and refining processes.
Approximately 50% of dietary vitamin B5 is absorbed1. It is absorbed in the jejunum and excreted in the urine. There is currently no upper limit for this vitamin as no toxic effects have been reported.
Pantothenic acid is the most common supplemental form of vitamin B5. It is comprises 91.5% pantothenic acid and 7.5% calcium.
Nervous system
Vitamin B5 supports nervous system health.
CoA is a cofactor in the synthesis of the neurotransmitter acetylcholine, which is involved in learning, memory and mood.
Vitamin B5 is often referred to as the ‘anti-stress’ vitamin, as it is necessary for adrenal function and a healthy stress response. It is involved in the production of glucocorticoids and other adrenal
hormones, including cortisol. Vitamin B5 has been found to enhance adrenal cortical function in animals and may lower secretion of cortisol in periods of stress.
Skin health
Vitamin B5 helps regulate epidermal barrier function and keratinocyte differentiation via CoA metabolism and plays an essential role in normal epithelial function.
Acne is a common skin condition that affects the hair follicles associated with an oil gland. It can present with inflammatory or non-inflammatory lesions.
A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled study looked at the effects of high-strength pantothenic acid in adults previously
diagnosed with mild to moderate acne vulgaris. Forty-eight subjects were randomised to pantothenic acid (2.2g) or placebo for 12 weeks. There was a significant mean reduction in total lesion count in the pantothenic acid group versus placebo at week 12 (p=0.0197)2.
Another open-label, single arm study in 10 healthy adults diagnosed with mild to moderate acne found that pantothenic acid reduced the number of facial skin blemishes by 56% after 8 weeks3.

Vitamin B6, otherwise known as pyridoxine, is a water-soluble vitamin involved in carbohydrate, protein and lipid metabolism. Vitamin B6, unlike other B vitamins that are regularly excreted from the body, is stored extensively in muscle tissue.
Pyridoxine hydrochloride is the most common supplemental form of vitamin B6. After absorption in the small intestine, pyridoxine is
transformed into pyridoxal 5-phosphate (P5P), the active form, either in intestinal cells or the liver and then distributed to tissues.
Vitamin B6 100mg contains high-strength pyridoxine hydrochloride with activated vitamin B6 as P5P.
P5P is a coenzyme involved in more than 150 enzymatic reactions in the body1. It is necessary for transamination reactions that allow the formation of non-essential amino acids, the conversion of tryptophan to niacin (vitamin B3) and serotonin and for the synthesis of glucose from glycogen.
Vitamin B6 is found in wholegrain cereals, organ meats, legumes, eggs and yeast extracts. Like most B vitamins, B6 is sensitive to light, heat, air and mechanical disruption, so its content in food can be reduced by physical processing, cooking, sterilisation and freezing. One study found that cooking loss of vitamin B6 in chicken ranged from 55-89%2.
Aging, excess alcohol and caffeine intake, poor diet, certain medications and chronic stress can increase an individuals’ requirements for vitamin B6.
Nervous system health & emotional wellbeing
Vitamin B6 is important for healthy nervous system function. It is crucial for the synthesis of sphingolipids, essential constituents of the lipid-rich myelin sheath surrounding nerves.
Vitamin B6 supports emotional wellbeing as it is involved in the synthesis of several neurotransmitters, including gamma
aminobutyric acid (GABA), serotonin, norepinephrine and dopamine.
Serotonin and dopamine are neurotransmitters that play a role in an individual’s mood and wellbeing. Dopamine plays a part in
controlling the movements a person makes, as well as their emotional responses. Serotonin is used to transmit messages between nerve cells and contributes to wellbeing and happiness.
A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial found that daily supplementation with high dose vitamin B6 (100mg/day) improved self-reported mood outcomes3.
A deficiency in vitamin B6 has been associated with alterations in mood.
Blood health
Vitamin B6 helps maintain healthy blood. It is necessary for the synthesis of the haem component of haemoglobin, which transports oxygen in red blood cells.
Vitamin B6 also has a role in homocysteine metabolism.
High homocysteine is an independent risk factor for adverse cardiovascular outcomes. The conversion of homocysteine to cysteine requires two P5P-dependent enzymes: cystathionine synthase and cystathionase. Vitamin B6 is best prescribed with folate and vitamin B12 for homocysteine management.
Immune system health
Vitamin B6 supports healthy immune system function. Vitamin B6 participates in the functioning of the entire immune system.
Vitamin B6 plays a key role in humoral and cell-mediated immunity. It supports antibody production and the communicative interactions between cytokines and chemokines, immune chemicals responsible for orchestrating a highly specific immune response4. Thus, a deficiency may suppress immune system function, increasing the body’s susceptibility to infection.
Premenstrual tension (PMT)
Vitamin B6 is a cofactor in the synthesis of neurotransmitters and an immediate precursor to serotonin and dopamine. It is also involved in GABA synthesis and enzymatic steps of tryptophan and tyrosine metabolism. Its deficiency may lead to reduced concentrations of noradrenaline and serotonin. Research suggests vitamin B6 may be
beneficial in managing psychological symptoms of PMS. Low levels of vitamin B6 increases prolactin levels, resulting in more psychological symptoms during the premenstrual period.
The neurotransmitters GABA and serotonin play key roles in mood, anxiety and pain perception. B6 is also important for magnesium transportation into the cell membrane.
A 2016 systematic review of 12 randomised, placebo-controlled trials concluded that using vitamin B6 may reduce the overall symptoms of PMT. There seems to be no dose-related response to treatment, with dosages ranging from 40-300mg daily for the duration of 1-3 menstrual cycles5.

Vitamin C is an essential water-soluble nutrient for humans which cannot be made or stored in the body, so must be taken in the diet on a regular basis.
Vitamin C has several important functions in the body, including supporting the immune system, aiding collagen production for wound healing and skin health, maintaining bone health, supporting the absorption of dietary iron, while also acting as an antioxidant to protect cells from free radical damage.
Zinc is an essential trace element known to play an important role in all human living cells. The human body contains about 2g of total zinc, with more than 85% found in skeletal muscle and bone1. Zinc plays a crucial role in the pathways involved in inflammation, immunity, carbohydrate and protein metabolism, DNA metabolism and repair, reproduction, vision, taste and bone health.
Bioflavonoids are biologically active members of the group of plant-derived compounds known as flavonoids and are present in the rind of citrus fruits. Vitamin C 1000 Plus contains citrus bioflavonoids extract, as well as additional flavonoid support in rutin and hesperidin.
On their own, bioflavonoids are antioxidant, but when added to vitamin C they are known to increase both the efficacy and bioavailability of vitamin C.
Antioxidant
Vitamin C 1000 Plus contains vitamin C, zinc and bioflavonoids, each demonstrating antioxidant activity to reduce free radicals formed in the body.
Vitamin C works in the aqueous environments in the body acting as a potent antioxidant by significantly decreasing the adverse effect of reactive species such as reactive oxygen and nitrogen species that can cause oxidative damage to macromolecules such as lipids, DNA and proteins which are implicated in poor health outcomes.
Zinc is a powerful antioxidant and free radical scavenger. Zinc's role as an antioxidant is achieved through numerous mechanisms including protecting vitamin E from depletion and acting as
an important structural component of the antioxidant enzyme superoxide dismutase.
Citrus bioflavonoids, as well as the bioflavonoids rutin and hesperidin all demonstrate antioxidant activity.
Immune health
Vitamin C 1000 Plus contains high dose vitamin C, along with zinc to support immune system function and immune system health.
Vitamin C concentrations in the body rapidly decline during times of infection and stress. Supplementation of vitamin C has been found to improve components of the human immune system, such as natural killer cell activity and white blood cell function, processes known to fight infection2.
Likewise, inadequate zinc has been shown to impair cellular mediators in the bodies innate immune system.
The research in relation to vitamin C’s role in both the prevention and treatment of colds and flu is extensive. Vitamin C has been shown to not only help prevent the common cold, but also reduce the severity and duration of a cold once one exists3, while the combination of zinc and vitamin C has been shown to reduce the duration and severity of common cold symptoms due to their immune-supporting actions4.
Male reproductive health
Vitamin C 1000 Plus contains vitamin C and zinc to support sperm health and motility and maintain prostate health and reproductive system health in males.
Vitamin C has been shown to improve semen parameters in men. A 2018 study of seminal parameters in 40 men showed the addition of vitamin C demonstrated a statistically significant (p<0.05) improvement in all sperm parameters including count, motility, morphology and viability5.

Zinc is an essential trace element known to play an important role in all human living cells. The human body contains about 2g of total zinc, with more than 85% found in skeletal muscle and bone1. Zinc plays a crucial role in the pathways involved in inflammation, immunity, carbohydrate and protein metabolism, DNA metabolism and repair, reproduction, vision, taste and bone health.

While once only known for its role in bone health, the diverse role of vitamin D in the body is still under discovery. Vitamin D acts like a
hormone in the body, with vitamin D receptors found right throughout the body, including in skeletal and cardiac muscle, all immune cells, many cells involved in cardiovascular homeostasis, brain cells, and reproductive tissues, suggesting its essential role in whole body function.
Vitamin D is essential for the body to absorb calcium effectively, which is important for bone health and muscle function. The main source of vitamin D is exposure to sunlight, although small amounts can be obtained through some foods, such as fatty fish and fortified margarine and milk.
Vitamin D3 1000 is suspended in rice bran oil, providing a stable soy-free base. Rice bran oil provides greater stability from oxidation when compared to soy oil due to its high content of tocotrienols, powerful natural antioxidants that belong to the vitamin E family.
Calcium absorption & bone health
Vitamin D supports bone health by assisting calcium absorption in the intestines and influencing bone remodelling. Vitamin D is necessary for osteocalcin, which binds calcium to bone.
Vitamin D maintains appropriate serum calcium concentrations by enhancing the ability of the small intestine to absorb calcium from the diet. In a low vitamin D state, the small intestine can only absorb approximately 10%–15% of dietary calcium. However, with
adequate vitamin D, intestinal absorption of dietary calcium rises to approximately 30%–40%1.
The National Osteoporosis Foundation (NOF) recommend vitamin D intake of 800-1000 IU daily along with calcium for preventing osteoporosis in adults over 50 years of age2.
Clinical research shows taking vitamin D3 orally with calcium supplements can decrease postmenopausal bone loss, help prevent osteoporosis, and decrease the risk of all fractures by 8% to 17%, nonvertebral fractures by 14% to 49%, and hip fractures by 9% to 30% in older adults3.
Vitamin D helps to strengthen teeth as part of its role in regulating calcium and phosphate.
Immune health
Vitamin D3 1000 supports healthy immune system function.
Vitamin D receptors can be found throughout the body, including on immune cells, such as antigen-presenting-cells, T cells, B cells and monocytes. As these cells are capable of synthesising the active vitamin D metabolite, vitamin D can act in an autocrine manner modulating both the innate and adaptive immune responses.
Vitamin D also affects T-regulatory cells which are responsible for
inflammatory cytokines. Adequate vitamin D inhibits the proliferation of these inflammatory cells, thereby exhibiting an anti-inflammatory action.
Muscle health
Vitamin D supports muscle health and muscle strength.
Adequate vitamin D assists both muscle function and muscle strength, playing an important role in the elderly and post-menopausal women contributing to a reduction in injury and falls4.
Support healthy pregnancy
Vitamin D supports a healthy pregnancy and healthy foetal development.
Low vitamin D status in a breastfeeding mother directly correlates to low vitamin D in breastmilk. Adequate vitamin D is required for both musculoskeletal and neurological growth and for the development of the newborn.

One-a-day
Vitamin K is a group of structurally similar, fat-soluble vitamins that are needed in the body to help the blood clot and for binding calcium in bone.
Vitamin K occurs naturally in two forms: phylloquinone (vitamin K1) and menaquinone (vitamin K2). Menadione (vitamin K3) is a synthetic form that does not occur naturally.
Vitamin K1 is made from plants and found in foods such as broccoli, spinach, cabbage, asparagus, green tea and chlorophyll. Vitamin K in foods is not affected by heating, but can be destroyed by freezing.
Vitamin K2 is mainly of microbial origin and present in animal products and fermented foods such as meat, cheese, eggs, natto and sauerkraut and also made by bacteria in the gut. The concentration of vitamin K2 in foods is very low and digestion and utilisation of vitamin K2 from foods becomes less efficient with ageing1. One exception to this is natto, a traditional Japanese food made from whole fermented soybeans, known to contain very high levels of vitamin K2 - in fact it is the world’s richest food source of vitamin K2. The high consumption of natto in Japan has been postulated as the reason that Japan has a lower fracture risk than other countries2.
Table 1: Vitamin K content in food3
In Australia, there is currently no recommended dietary intake (RDI) of vitamin K, but the adequate intake (AI) is set at 70 micrograms/day for adult men and 60 micrograms per day for adult women4, based on the dose of vitamin K needed to maintain a normal prothrombin time in otherwise healthy individuals. Scientific consensus is that this level is not sufficient to capture the benefits of vitamin K2, with most research being done on 90-180 micrograms.
Vitamin K1 is well-known for its role in blood coagulation, while more and more research is being done on vitamin K2 for bone health and cardiovascular health.
Vitamin K2
Vitamin K2 is a group of compounds composed of a methylated naphthoquinone ring and an isoprenoid side chain of variable length (usually 4-15 units). Menaquinones are further classified according to the length of their side chain, referred to as MK-n, where n denotes the number of isoprenoid units. Currently, MK-4 and MK-7 are the most common forms of vitamin K2, with MK-7 displaying higher bioavailability and functionality.
Vitamin K2 MK-4
Vitamin K2 MK-7
MK-7 is absorbed within 4 hours of ingestion, has a long half-life of 72 hours, and has been shown to be more bioavailable and have greater bioactivity than both vitamin K15 and MK-46.
K2VITAL™
Vitamin K2 180 MAX contains vitamin K2 as K2VITAL™, a proprietary form of vitamin K2 for enhanced stability and efficacy.
K2VITAL™ is produced in Norway using state of the art technology to ensure ingredient purity and stability. K2VITAL™ is produced by organic synthesis, derived from essential flower oils to create a pure and stable vitamin K2 that is identical to the vitamin K2 molecule found in nature.
The stability of vitamin K2 is negatively affected by high temperatures, light and pH. Vitamin K2 180 MAX is manufactured under carefully controlled conditions to ensure that light, temperature and pH have as little influence as possible to ensure stability throughout the product shelf-life.
MK-7 can exist in two forms – cis or trans isomers, or a combination of both. The chemical structure of MK-7 determines its biological activity, with only the all-trans form sustaining biological activity7.

Vitex agnus-castus (Chaste tree) has a long history of traditional use in Western herbal medicine (WHM) for the relief of menstrual irregularities and symptoms of premenstrual tension (PMT).
The dried fruit from the Vitex plant contains several active constituents including flavonoids, iridoids, alkaloids and volatile oils.
The mode of action of Vitex is multifaceted. Vitex acts on dopamine (D2) receptors in the anterior pituitary gland, decreasing high prolactin levels. Prolactin is a hormone that primarily functions to help women produce milk after childbirth. However, in non-breastfeeding mothers, elevated prolactin can block the production of other hormones in the body, including oestrogen and progesterone. Elevated prolactin levels are associated with menstrual irregularities and symptoms of PMT1.
Low doses of Vitex have been shown to increase luteinising hormone (LH) while decreasing follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), working indirectly on achieving oestrogen and progesterone balance within the body. Oestrogen dominance in females is linked to mood disorders, including PMS, and menstrual irregularities.
It is recommended Vitex be taken in the morning, before breakfast, as this is the time the pituitary gland is the most receptive.
Premenstrual syndrome
Premenstrual syndrome (PMS) is a combination of emotional, physical, psychological and mood disturbances that generally occur after a female ovulates and before the onset of a menstrual period.
Emotional symptoms can include irritability, crying, oversensitivity and mood swings, while physical symptoms may present as fatigue, bloating, breast tenderness, skin issues such as acne or appetite changes and food cravings.
It is estimated that as many as 90% of women experience at least one PMS symptom most months and about 50% of women experience several PMS symptoms each month2.
For some women who suffer from PMS, the symptoms are severe enough to interfere with regular day-to-day activities.
Vitex 1000 for PMS
Several clinical studies have been conducted on Vitex for premenstrual syndrome. A phytopharmaceutical formulation of an extract of Vitex fruit was used in 1634 females suffering from PMS symptoms. Self-assessment questionnaires were used to assess symptoms such as headache, anger, irritability, mood, breast fullness and bloating. After taking Vitex for three menstrual cycles, 93% of females reported either a decrease in the number of symptoms or complete cessation of complaints3.
A further study of 178 women with symptoms of PMS tested against placebo demonstrated a statistically significant improvement against symptoms of irritability, mood alteration, anger, headache, breast fullness and bloating4.
Trickey, R. (2011). Women, Hormones & the Menstrual Cycle (2nd ed). Allen & Unwin.
Vitex 1000 for menstrual regulation
Irregular periods can be caused by many factors, including but not limited to, sporadic ovulation, decreased progesterone or increased prolactin.
Vitex works by increasing the release of luteinizing hormone from the pituitary gland, which raises progesterone and normalises the second half of the menstrual cycle.
Vitex & the oral contraceptive pill (OCP)
Vitex is generally not considered suitable to be used alongside the OCP.
Vitex may reduce the effectiveness of contraceptives as it can act as a precursor to the hormones involved in ovulation. This may negate the ovulation-inhibiting effects of the OCP. As a result, women using Vitex alongside birth control could experience an increased risk of unplanned pregnancy5.

subsections.heading: DRUG INTERACTIONS
subsections.text:
Contraindicated with fertility drugs or IVF – the addition of Vitex could potentially cause hyperstimulation of the ovaries.
Caution with hormone replacement therapy, oral contraceptive pills and progesterone drugs – given Vitex’s hormone modulating effect, it may theoretically interfere with the action of these drugs.

subsections.heading: CAUTIONS
subsections.text:
Avoid use in individuals with tumours sensitive to oestrogen or progesterone.
Vitex is not generally recommended in females under 20 years of age as the natural hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis can be easily disrupted.
Vitex is most effective during the first three to six months of use. After that, its effect on the pituitary starts to diminish. It is recommended to take a break from Vitex for two months before resuming use.
Not recommended during pregnancy without medical advice and breastfeeding due to insufficient studies relating to safety.

subsections.text: In some cases, Vitex may initially worsen PMS symptoms.

One-a-day
Women’s Multi + contains a blend of vitamins, minerals, nutrients and herbs in a one-a-day supplement to support women’s health.
Women’s Multi + contains Grape seed extract equivalent to dry herb 12g. Grape seed contains oligomeric proanthocyanidins which are potent antioxidants to reduce free radicals formed in the body. Grape seed also supports healthy veins, blood vessels and microcirculation.
Women’s Multi + contains antioxidant nutrients vitamin C, citrus bioflavonoids, vitamin E, zinc and selenium to help reduce free radical damage. Vitamin C is the most important water-soluble antioxidant in the body, while vitamin E is a fat-soluble antioxidant whose major role is to protect polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFA) from oxidation. It acts as an antioxidant in the lipid phase of cell membranes.
Women’s Multi + contains nutrients that support immune system function, including vitamin C, vitamin E, vitamin D, zinc and selenium.
Women’s Multi + contains nutrients that support blood health and assist healthy red blood cell production. Iron, folate, vitamin B12 and copper help the formation of red blood cells in the body and support normal blood function.
Women’s Multi + contains chromium to assist sugar and carbohydrate metabolism. Chromium assists in the uptake of glucose into the cells by stimulating insulin uptake and enhancing its activity. Requirements for chromium are increased when consuming a diet high in sugar.
B vitamins
Women’s Multi + contains therapeutic doses of all the B group vitamins, plus the active form of folate and vitamin B12.
As B vitamins are water soluble, regular daily intake is required to support general health. B vitamins work synergistically in the body and are, therefore, best taken together.
B vitamins support energy production, assist sugar and carbohydrate metabolism and help convert carbohydrates and protein into energy.
Women’s Multi + contains methylfolate (5-MTHF), the active form of folate. Folate is the generic term for a large family of chemically
similar compounds known as vitamin B9. Folic acid is a synthetic form of the vitamin and must be reduced to methylfolate for use in the body.
Many people have mutations on the MTHFR gene, which affects their ability to convert folic acid into the active form (40-70% reduction in activity of the MTHFR enzyme). Methylfolate is a good alternative in individuals with MTHFR mutations as it is ready for use in the body and does not require conversion.
Women’s Multi + contains methylcobalamin (mecobalamin), the metabolically-active coenzyme form of vitamin B12 that is readily bioavailable for use in the body. Commonly-used cyanocobalamin is a form of vitamin B12 that does not occur naturally in foods and needs to be converted to methylcobalamin for use in the body. Methylcobalamin differs from cyanocobalamin in that the non-toxic cyanide molecule is replaced by a methyl group.
Nervous system
Women’s Multi + supports nervous system health and a healthy stress response.
B vitamins are involved in nerve impulse transmission and the synthesis of neurotransmitters, including acetylcholine, gamma aminobutyric acid (GABA), dopamine and serotonin, so they have a role in emotional balance and mood. Vitamin B12 is important for the manufacture of the myelin sheath, the protective sheath surrounding many nerves. Vitamins B5 and B6 help support a healthy stress response in the body as they are required for the synthesis of the adrenal hormones adrenaline and noradrenaline. Vitamin B5, as coenzyme A, is needed for healthy adrenal cortex function and the

Methylfolate and vitamin B12 support brain health, cognitive function and memory.
Skin health
Women’s Multi + contains nutrients, vitamin C, vitamin E, zinc and copper, that support healthy skin, connective tissue formation and wound healing.
Vitamin C is found in the epidermis and the dermis of the skin, where it acts as an antioxidant, protecting against free radical damage, including UV-induced photodamage. Vitamin C also
enhances collagen synthesis and stabilisation, enhances keratinocyte differentiation and improves wound healing. Vitamin E is the major naturally-occurring lipid-soluble antioxidant protecting the skin from oxidative stress.
Thyroid health
Women’s Multi + contains iodine and selenium, which help maintain healthy thyroid function and assist thyroid hormone production. Iodine is a precursor for thyroid hormones, required for normal growth and metabolism. Selenium is required for normal thyroid hormone synthesis, activation and metabolism.
Vitamin D
Women’s Multi + contains 1000IU of vegan-friendly vitamin D3, the maximum daily dose in a listed medicine. Vitamin D supports bone health in women and helps maintain bone density and strength in post-menopausal women.
Vitamin D assists the intestinal absorption of calcium and phosphorus, helping to maintain serum calcium concentrations. Research shows that in low vitamin D states, the small intestine absorbs approximately 10-15% of dietary calcium. When vitamin D levels are adequate,
the small intestine can absorb 30-40%1. A diet deficient in calcium can lead to osteoporosis in later life. The National Osteoporosis Foundations guidelines (2014) recommend a daily intake of 800-1000IU vitamin D daily with calcium for preventing osteoporosis in adults over 50 years of age2.
Vitamin D supports bone health independent of calcium. It is actively involved in bone formation and bone remodelling by osteoblasts and osteoclasts, resorption and mineralisation. Research shows that vitamin D with or without calcium can reduce the risk of all fractures by 8% to 17%, nonvertebral fractures by 14% to 49% and hip fractures by 9% to 30% in older adults3.
Vitamin D supports muscle function and helps maintain muscle strength. It has a role in the regulation and uptake of calcium in muscle cells, which is important for muscle strength, muscle contraction, mitochondrial function and insulin sensitivity.

subsections.heading: DRUG INTERACTIONS
subsections.text:
Separate dose from medication by 2 hours to minimise any interactions.
Caution with phenobarbital and phenytoin (anticonvulsants) - high doses of vitamin B6 or folate can decrease their efficacy. Use only under the supervision of a health professional.
Caution with L-Dopa - vitamin B6 increases the peripheral metabolism of levodopa and may lower levodopa levels for CNS penetration, resulting in reduced levodopa effects. The effect of pyridoxine is prevented by administration of a dopa-decarboxylase inhibitor (e.g. benserazide, carbidopa) with levodopa, as is common clinical practice.
Caution with methotrexate (folic acid antagonist) - co-administration with folate may reduce the effects. Patients should take folate only under the supervision of a health professional.
Caution with aluminium-containing phosphate binders - vitamins C and D can increase aluminium absorption. Separate dose.
Caution with thiazide diuretics - thiazides may reduce urinary calcium excretion and increase serum calcium levels when
administered with high doses of vitamin D. Monitor serum calcium levels.
Caution with cardiac glycosides (e.g. digoxin) - vitamin D can elevate serum calcium levels, which may lead to increased inflow of calcium into myocardial cells, increasing toxicity of cardiac glycosides. Monitor calcium levels.
Caution with orlistat – may impair the absorption of fat-soluble vitamins. Take Women’s Multi + at least 2 hours after orlistat.
Caution with phosphate and drugs containing phosphate -
vitamin D increases the absorption of phosphates which may lead to hyperphosphataemia. Monitor.
Separate the dose from colestyramine and colestipol – may reduce absorption of fat-soluble vitamins, vitamin B3 and folate. Space administration as far apart as possible.
Caution with calcium channel blockers - vitamin D may reduce the effectiveness of these drugs. Use under medical supervision.
Caution with blood thinning medications, including warfarin - vitamins E and C, selenium and Grape seed may interfere with the activity of vitamin K in producing blood clotting factors and lead to increased clinical effects of oral anticoagulants. Monitor.
Caution with NSAIDs, cefalexin, penicillamine and quinolone and tetracycline antibiotics – form insoluble complexes with magnesium and zinc, decreasing absorption. Seperate dose by 3 hours.

Zinc and vitamin C are two of the most important nutrients known to man. They are both required for hundreds of processes in the body, including antioxidant protection and healthy immune system function.
Zinc is an essential trace element known to play an important role in all human living cells. The human body contains about 2g of total zinc, with more than 85% found in skeletal muscle and bone1.
Zinc plays a crucial role in the pathways involved in inflammation, immunity, carbohydrate and protein metabolism, DNA metabolism and repair, reproduction, vision, taste and bone health.
Zinc is required for the synthesis of new tissue and is an important cellular building block. A complex homeostatic system maintains zinc levels within a narrow range balancing absorption and excretion.
Zinc is widely distributed in foods. Meats, fish and poultry are the major contributors to the diet, but cereals and dairy foods also contribute substantial amounts. The presence of zinc in foods as a complex rather than as free ions affects its bioavailability. The
environment within the gastrointestinal tract, which can be affected by other dietary constituents, markedly influences the solubility and absorptive efficiency of zinc.
Zinc is more difficult to absorb from plant-based foods. Many plant sources of zinc also contain high phytate levels, such as wholegrains and seeds, which inhibit the absorption of the mineral. The requirement for dietary zinc may be as high as 50% greater for vegetarians.
Zinc Forte + C helps maintain zinc levels in the body. To address established zinc deficiency, 25-50mg of zinc per day is
recommended2. Signs of zinc deficiency include impaired immune function, reduced sense of taste and smell, poor wound healing, poor cognitive function, irritability and dermatitis.
To date, there is no established reliable marker for measuring an individual’s zinc status. Zinc is stored intracellularly and only a small percentage is found in the plasma, meaning plasma zinc levels are not a precise measure.
Vitamin C is an essential water-soluble nutrient for humans which cannot be made or stored in the body, so must be taken in the diet on a regular basis.
Vitamin C has several important functions in the body, including supporting the immune system, aiding collagen production for wound healing and skin health, maintaining bone health and supporting the absorption of dietary iron.
Zinc Forte + C combines high-strength zinc and vitamin C in a delicious raspberry flavoured powder that is naturally sweetened with Stevia and free from artificial colours and flavours.
Antioxidant
Zinc Forte + C contains antioxidant nutrients to reduce free radicals formed in the body.
Vitamin C is antioxidant by scavenging oxygen and nitrogen free radicals, regenerating antioxidant vitamin E and maintaining reduced glutathione.
Zinc is a powerful antioxidant and free radical scavenger. Zinc's role as an antioxidant is achieved through numerous mechanisms
including protecting vitamin E from depletion, acting as an important structural component of the antioxidant enzyme superoxide dismutase and reducing free radical production.
Immune health
Both vitamin C and zinc are important for a healthy immune system.
Vitamin C concentrations in the body rapidly decline during times of infection and stress. Supplementation of vitamin C has been found to improve components of the human immune system such as
antimicrobial and natural killer cell activities, processes known to fight infection.
Likewise, zinc undernutrition or deficiency has been shown to impair cellular mediators of the body's innate immune system. Therefore, both vitamin C and zinc play important roles in immune function and the bodies natural resistance to infectious agents.
Vitamin C levels are quickly depleted when an individual is put under stress; lack of vitamin C dramatically increases the chance of catching an infection.
Vitamin C has been shown to not only help prevent the common cold, but also reduce the severity and duration of a cold once one exists3.

Skin health
Zinc Forte + C supports healthy skin.
Normal skin contains high concentrations of vitamin C as vitamin C is actively accumulated into the epidermal and dermal cells of the
skin. Vitamin C supports epithelial barrier function against pathogens and promotes the oxidant scavenging activity of the skin, thereby potentially protecting against environmental oxidative stress and providing antioxidant protection against UV-induced photodamage.
Six percent of total body zinc is in the skin. Zinc is present in both the epidermis and dermis, though at levels five-fold higher in the epidermis. In skin physiology, zinc stabilises cell membranes, serves
as an essential cofactor for several metalloenzymes, and participates in basal cell mitosis and differentiation.
Both vitamin C and zinc have a positive effect on the inflammatory processes in the skin and assists wound healing. Vitamin C is a
co-factor in enzymes directly involved in the synthesis of collagen, while also providing antioxidant protection against UV-induced photodamage.
Vitamin C, through its role in collagen synthesis, helps maintain healthy blood vessels in the body and is a component of haemoglobin, assisting in the production of red blood cells.
Zinc is often recommended for acne. One study found that the serum zinc levels were significantly lower in patients with acne than in age and sex matched healthy individuals in the control group (p<0.001). It also showed a negative correlation between acne severity and zinc levels5.
Zinc is theorised to be beneficial in acne due to its role in the maintenance of cell replication and wound repair, regulation of inflammation, immune function and inhibition of 5α-reductase, which blocks the conversion of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone and supresses sebaceous gland activity6.
A multicentre, randomised, double-blind trial in 332 patients compared 30mg of zinc (n=163) to the antibiotic minocycline (n=169) over 3 months. Zinc supplementation resulted in a decrease in the number of superficial inflammatory lesions by 31.78% on day 30, 42.09% on day 60 and 49.84% on day 90. At the end of the study, 31.2% of people supplemented with zinc had a two-thirds decrease in inflammatory lesions7.
Male reproductive health
Zinc plays an important role in maintaining male reproductive health. It is important for the normal functioning of the prostate gland and essential for the healthy formation and maturation of sperm.
There is a strong correlation between zinc status and sperm count, morphology and motility.
Vitamin C has also been shown to improve semen parameters in men. A 2018 study of seminal parameters in 40 men showed the addition of vitamin C demonstrated a statistically significant (p<0.05) improvement in all sperm parameters including count, motility, morphology and viability8.
Taste
The area of the brain responsible for the sensations of taste and smell needs adequate levels of zinc to function efficiently.
Adequate zinc helps maintain normal taste sensation.
Absorption of dietary iron
In the presence of vitamin C, the body absorbs iron far more efficiently. This is significant for vegetarians and vegans where absorption of iron from non-heme (plant-based) sources is generally lower than heme-based (animal) sources.

subsections.heading: DRUG INTERACTIONS
subsections.text:
Caution with NSAIDs, cephalexin, penicillamine and quinolone and tetracycline antibiotics – zinc forms complexes with these drugs, reducing absorption of both. Separate dose by 3 hours.
Caution with amiloride (diuretic) – drug can reduce zinc excretion, leading to zinc accumulation.
Caution with eltrombopag – zinc may reduce drug absorption. Separate dose by 4 hours.
Caution with calcium supplements – zinc and calcium compete for common intestinal absorption sites. Separate zinc and calcium supplements by at least 2 hours.

subsections.heading: CAUTIONS
subsections.text:
Use in caution if there is a history of renal calculi (kidney stones) as vitamin C (ascorbic acid) may increase the risk of recurrence of calcium oxalate calculi.
Caution in iron overload conditions, such as haemochromatosis, as vitamin C can increase iron absorption.

subsections.text: High dose of zinc (50-150mg/day) may a cause mild gastrointestinal upset. Taking zinc with foods reduces the incidence of side-effects.
